Lily stopped and looked at Alma. She remembered how she felt when her cousin wouldn't share the little bell. She paused for a moment and held the hoop tightly.
—I don’t know, Alma… You didn’t share your little bell with me…
Alma looked down at the ground. She realized how selfish she had been.
—I’m sorry, Lily. I know I made you feel sad. I promise if you let me play with you, I’ll never be like that again.
Lily looked into Alma’s honest little eyes and smiled.
—Okay, I guess we can play together.

Both little lambs started to pass the hoop back and forth, making up fun games. They laughed so much that other little lambs from the flock joined in, and soon the hoop and the little bell were part of all sorts of games. 🎉
At the end of the day, Alma looked at her cousin warmly.
—Thank you, Lily, for sharing with me. I realized that playing together is so much more fun.
From then on, Alma learned to share not just her little bell, but also her time and her laughter with everyone. And in the meadow, their play days became happier than ever before. 🌞

Hansel and Gretel lived in a tiny, drafty cabin deep in the woods with their father, a humble woodcutter, and their mother. The family had fallen on hard times; the pantry was empty, and their stomachs rumbled louder than the wind outside. One evening, the children overheard a hushed, desperate conversation in the kitchen.
"We have nothing left to feed them," their mother whispered, her voice trembling. "If we leave them in the forest, perhaps a kind stranger will find them and give them a better life."

Hansel and Gretel looked at each other, eyes wide with fear. But Hansel took a deep breath. He wasn't going to give up. That night, he slipped out the back door and filled his pockets with smooth, white pebbles that glowed under the moonlight. 🌕

The next morning, the parents led the children deep into the thicket of trees. As they walked, Hansel lagged behind, dropping a pebble every few steps. Plink, plink. When the parents left them in a clearing to "gather firewood," the children waited. As soon as the sun set and the full moon rose, the pebbles shone like silver coins on the dark path. Hand in hand, they followed the trail all the way back to their front door. 🌲🌟

Their parents hugged them tight, tears in their eyes, but the cupboard was still bare. A few days later, despair took over again, and they decided to take the children even deeper into the woods. This time, Hansel couldn't sneak out to get pebbles. Instead, he crumbled his last piece of bread in his pocket. As they walked, he dropped little crumbs to mark the way. 🥖
But when night fell and they tried to find their way back, the trail was gone! Hungry birds had swooped down and eaten every single crumb. 🐦

Lost and shivering, they wandered through the forest all night. Just as the sun began to peek over the horizon, they saw something incredible: a cottage made entirely of treats! 🎂 The roof was tiled with colorful hard candies, the windows were framed in thick white frosting, and the walls were baked gingerbread. The air smelled of vanilla and warm sugar.
"It looks like a dream!" Gretel cried out.

Unable to resist, they ran forward. Crunch, munch! They broke off pieces of the porch and ate happily. Suddenly, the front door creaked open. An old woman with thick glasses and a crooked nose peered out. 👵
"Nibbling on my house, are we?" she rasped, though she offered a toothless smile. "Don't worry, little ones. Come inside. I have plenty more."

The children were hesitant, but their hunger won out. They stepped inside, but the cozy feeling vanished instantly. The inside was dim and dusty, filled with strange jars and cages. Slam! The old woman—who was actually a wicked witch—shoved Hansel into a heavy iron cage and turned to Gretel with a menacing grin.
"Do as I say, girl, or your brother is in big trouble!"

Gretel quickly realized the witch planned to fatten Hansel up to turn him into a stew! Every day, the witch served Hansel piles of pancakes and roast beef, but gave Gretel only scraps. However, Hansel was clever. When the near-blind witch asked him to stick out his finger to check if he was gaining weight, Hansel stuck out a leftover chicken bone instead. 🍗
"Still too thin!" the witch would grumble, pinching the bone. "I need to wait longer."
Weeks passed, and Gretel racked her brain for a plan. Finally, the witch lost her patience.
"Thin or fat, I'm cooking him today!" she shrieked. She ordered Gretel to check if the big oven was hot enough for baking bread.
Gretel saw her chance. "I don't know how," she lied, putting on a confused face. "The opening is too small. How do I look inside?"
"Silly child!" the witch snapped. "Move over, I'll show you."

The witch leaned deep into the oven. Whoosh! Gretel summoned all her bravery and gave the witch a mighty shove, slamming the heavy iron door shut and bolting it tight. The witch disappeared into the roaring flames, gone for good. 🔥

Shaking but relieved, Gretel found the key and unlocked Hansel's cage. Click, clack. He jumped out and hugged his sister. While searching for food for their journey home, they found a dusty chest under the bed. It was filled with gold coins and sparkling jewels! 💎

With their pockets full of treasure and their bellies full of food, they set off. After days of hiking, the woods began to look familiar. 🏠 They burst through the door of their cabin, where their parents sat weeping, filled with regret over what they had done. When they saw the children, they rushed to embrace them, promising never to let them go again.
The family shared the treasure, repaired their home, and lived happily—and safely—ever after. 🌟

In the heart of a noisy, bustling city, there was a forgotten park. It was a place filled with ancient trees that whispered stories to the wind. But over the years, it had become dark, sad, and neglected. Few visited it, and those who did often left trash behind, contributing to the park's decline.

A group of teenagers had found refuge there. Despite its rundown appearance, the park offered them something that no other place in the city could: tranquility and freedom. There, they could chat, listen to music, and laugh without anyone interrupting them.

One day, as they wandered among the trees, they realized that something was wrong. The leaves were withered, even though it was far from autumn, some branches were falling, and the ground was covered in trash and debris. Could it be that the trees were dying? This worried them deeply.
The birthdays of two members of the group, Ashley and Alex, were approaching. Their initial plan was to go to a famous burger chain and then to the movies, but then, Ashley had a different idea.
—What if we do something special? We could organize a picnic here, in the park. We'll decorate it, clean it up a bit, and celebrate like never before!—she proposed excitedly.
—Here?—asked Jamie, somewhat skeptical.—But it's full of trash…
—That's exactly why. This place needs a little life, like us. Besides, we could ask our families for help. I'm sure they'd like it too—added Alex, convincing the others.

When they shared the idea with their families, they not only agreed but were also enthusiastic. Each family took charge of preparing healthy dishes: fruit salads, whole-wheat sandwiches, vegetable skewers, and homemade lemonade. They also brought trash bags and gloves so everyone could help.

On the day of the picnic, the group met in the center of the park, where the oldest trees formed a natural circle. They began to pick up the trash, but not as a boring chore: they turned it into a game. Ashley invented a contest to see who could find the most plastic in 15 minutes, while Jamie organized a contest for whoever found the most improbable piece of trash. Even the little ones joined in, laughing and running among the trees, with a little one winning who found an old pocket watch, with its lid rusted.

When they finished, the park looked different. Although much remained to be done, the ground was clean, and the trees seemed to breathe better. Sitting on colorful blankets, they enjoyed the food and shared laughter under the shade of the ancient trees.
However, they knew that one day was not enough.
—We have to keep it like this—said Alex, looking around.—What if we organize something regular? Like events where people from the neighborhood come, bring food, play games, and take care of the park.
—We can do workshops! My aunt knows a lot about plants and could teach how to care for them—proposed Ashley.
—And we could also do yoga, races, or just picnic days like today—added Jamie.

Thus, The Centennial Park Gang was born. From that day on, they not only recovered a natural space but also created a community. Each event attracted more neighbors, who shared their knowledge, took care of the trees, and enjoyed healthy and sustainable leisure. 🌟

The park was filled with life again, not only by the singing of birds and the whispering of the wind but by the laughter and effort of the people who decided that saving it also meant taking care of themselves. 🌳✨

🛁 One afternoon, Tommy was in the bathtub, playing with mountains of bubbles he had created with his mom's shower gel. That gel, with its vanilla scent, was his favorite. It reminded him of freshly baked cookies, and he had fun shaping the foam into funny shapes. While he was playing, he noticed something strange: a giant, shiny bubble filled with tiny rainbows.
✨ Suddenly, poof! The bubble burst, and a little being made of foam appeared. He had a pointy hat, a bubbly beard that moved with the air, and a cheerful voice like the sound of many bubbles popping.
—Hello, Tommy! I am the Bubble Genie, the master of baths, the sage of showers. Do you want to learn how to shower all by yourself?
Tommy, surprised but excited, nodded enthusiastically.
—Perfect. But there's one condition: you'll have to answer my riddles. If you guess right, I'll teach you a trick to be a bath master. But, if you fail... a prank awaits you!
—Okay! —said Tommy, enthusiastically.
—First riddle —said the Genie while inflating another giant bubble—: "I'm in a bottle and I smell great. If you rub me with your hands, I'll make foam that's first-rate. What am I?"
Tommy knew it immediately. —The shower gel! Like my mom's!

👏 The Genie clapped, throwing bubbles into the air. —Correct! But listen: it's better to apply it with your hands. Rub a drop between your palms and then spread it all over your body. That way you make a more pleasant foam. Try it!
Tommy did as the Genie instructed and discovered that the foam was even softer and more fun to use.
—Second riddle —continued the Genie—: "I'm liquid and slippery, and if you use me, your hair will be pretty. What am I?"
Tommy replied without hesitation. —Shampoo!
🌟 —Very good! —said the Genie, smiling—. Remember: rub your scalp well and rinse until there's no foam left.
Tommy did it and felt like an expert. But the Genie had one last riddle:
—Last riddle: "I'm a powder or fine grain, I dissolve instantly. I make the water colorful and a relaxing scent. What am I?"
Tommy thought and replied: —Toothpaste?
😂 The Genie burst into bubbly laughter. —Incorrect! The answer was bath salts. And now... bubbly punishment!
Before Tommy could protest, the Genie blew a cloud of foam that tickled his nose. Tommy couldn't stop laughing while trying to dodge it.
—Tommy, baths are okay once in a while, but using so much water isn't good for the planet. Showers are quick, fun, and you can also make lots of foam, like you like! How about trying them more often?
Tommy nodded with a big smile. —I want to try it next time!

👏 The Genie clapped and, after a moment, said: —Now, the last step. The towel! It's very important to dry yourself well, especially between your toes, behind your ears, and in the folds of your skin. Here, look.
🧼 The Genie floated to an imaginary towel and showed Tommy how to wrap it around his body and dry himself without leaving any wet spots. Tommy picked up his real towel and practiced.
🎉 —Perfect! You're quite the bath expert —said the Genie, satisfied—. Remember: whenever you make foam, I'll be near. See you soon, little shower-taker!
With a pop, the Genie disappeared among the bubbles, leaving Tommy excited to tell everyone how well he knew how to shower now, thanks to the Bubble Genie! 🛁✨

In a quiet corner of the forest, lived a little spider named Lila 🕷️. She was young and full of dreams. Although she had practiced weaving small webs, she had never made a real one to live in. Now, she had the chance to build her very own home on a high, sunny branch.

It will be the most beautiful web in the forest! she thought, even though deep down, she knew she wasn't quite ready. But she didn't want to admit it. If the others think I don't know how, they'll laugh at me, she whispered to herself.

With great excitement, Lila began to spin. At first, everything went well, but as she continued, the threads became loose, the connections weren't strong, and some of the knots started to come undone. When Gus, the friendly worm 🐛 who lived nearby, came to visit, he wanted to cheer her on.
—Your web is looking so pretty, Lila! Gus said with a smile. But when he looked closer, he added gently, —Although, I think that thread over there is a little loose…
—It's not loose! Lila answered quickly, trying to hide the mistake with one of her legs. —It's… it's part of the design.
Later, Ruby, the ladybug 🐞, stopped when she saw Lila working.
—Lila, have you tried pulling those center threads tighter? They seem a little floppy, she commented.
—Everything is under control, Ruby! I know exactly what I'm doing.
Lila frowned, feeling a little stressed.

As the days went by, things got worse. The loose threads made the web's structure wobble in the wind, and Lila started getting tangled in her own work. She tried to fix it by herself, but the mess only grew. Exhausted and frustrated, she sat on a leaf 🍃, unable to hide her problems any longer.
That's when her friends came over again. This time, not to point out mistakes, but to offer support.
—Lila, we all learned how to do things from someone else, Ruby said softly. —Maybe you could ask Tessa, the elder spider, for advice. She's always happy to help.
At first, Lila hesitated. What if she laughs at me? she mumbled.
—Tessa? Never! She's a great teacher, Gus assured her enthusiastically.
Finally, Lila gathered her courage and went to see Tessa, who was spinning a perfect web in a corner of the forest.
—Hello, Tessa, Lila said shyly. —Could you help me with my web? I tried to do it alone, but… I don't know how to fix it.
Tessa smiled warmly. —Of course, Lila. We've all been there. Come, I'll show you a few tricks.

With patience, Tessa showed her how to choose the best branches for support, how to pull the threads tight so they would be strong, and how to make the knots secure. Little by little, Lila began to understand what she had been doing wrong.

Back on her branch, Lila, following Tessa's instructions, rebuilt her web from the beginning. This time, even though it wasn't perfect, it was much stronger and worked much better. When she finished, her friends came to visit again.
—It's beautiful, Lila! exclaimed Ruby.
—And this time, it won't blow away in the wind, Gus joked.
Lila smiled, proud but also thankful. —Thank you for not giving up on me. Now I know that asking for help isn't a bad thing, and that we all need to learn from others.
From that day on, Lila was never afraid to ask for advice when she needed it. Her web sparkled in the sun 🌞, and she lived happily, surrounded by friends who were always there to support her.

83.t: The Wolf and the Seven Young Kids
p: Mama Goat lived with her seven little kids in a cozy cottage right at the edge of the Whispering Woods. One sunny morning, Mama Goat gathered her children in the living room.

“My darlings,” she said, adjusting her apron. “I’m heading out to the meadow to gather some fresh clover for lunch. Lock the door and do not open it for anyone. You must be very careful of the Big Bad Wolf!”
The seven little goats promised to stay inside 🏡 and keep the door locked tight. Mama Goat gave them each a kiss on the forehead and trotted down the path toward the woods.

The Big Bad Wolf, who had been lurking behind a large oak tree 🌳, watched Mama Goat leave and grinned a toothy grin. “Now is my chance,” he whispered. He crept up to the cottage and knocked loudly on the front door.
Knock, knock, knock!
“Open up, kiddos! It’s Mommy. I’m home!” he boomed.
The little goats, whose ears were perked up 🐐, knew something was wrong immediately. Barnaby, the eldest goat, shouted through the door:
“You’re not our Mommy! Her voice is soft and sweet. Your voice is rough and scratchy! Go away, you Big Bad Wolf!”

The Wolf growled in frustration and stomped away. But he had a plan. He ran to the local grocery store and stole a big jar of honey. He gulped the sticky honey down in one go. Now, with his throat coated and smooth 🍯, his voice sounded as sweet as sugar. He ran back to the cottage.
Knock, knock, knock!
“It’s me, my darlings,” the Wolf sang out softly. “Open up for Mommy.”
The goats listened. The voice did sound sweet, just like Mama Goat's. But Barnaby was smart. He called out:
“If you’re really our Mommy, put your paw on the windowsill so we can see it!”
The Wolf, feeling confident 🐾, slapped his big, hairy black paw onto the sill. The little goats gasped and jumped back.
“You’re not our Mommy!” they cried. “Mommy has white paws! Yours are black and scary! Go away, you impostor!”
The Wolf roared with anger, but he wasn't ready to give up. He sprinted to the village bakery.
“I need some flour for... a cookie recipe,” he lied to the baker.
As soon as he had the sack of flour, he dusted his paws until they were snowy white. Chuckling to himself, he ran back to the cottage for the third time.
Knock, knock, knock!
“Little ones, it’s Mommy,” he crooned. “Look at my white paw and listen to my sweet voice. Please let me in!”
The goats peeked at the windowsill and saw the white paw. They heard the sweet voice. Convinced it was safe, they unlocked the bolt and swung the door open.
But it wasn't Mommy—it was the Big Bad Wolf!

With a howl, he leaped into the living room. The terrified goats scrambled to hide! One dove under the bed 🛏️, one squeezed into the laundry hamper, one hid in the oven 🍳, one behind the curtains... and Pip, the youngest and smallest, hopped inside the old grandfather clock ⏰.
The Wolf was fast. He found them one by one and gobbled them up. But he didn't check the clock. With a full belly, the Wolf stumbled outside and fell asleep under a shady tree.
When Mama Goat returned, she saw the door wide open. Her heart sank. She searched the house, calling their names, but it was silent. Finally, a tiny voice whispered from the clock.
“Mommy... I’m in here.”
Mama Goat opened the clock door and hugged little Pip, who was shaking.
“The Wolf took everyone!” Pip sobbed.
Mama Goat wiped her tears and grabbed her sewing kit—scissors, needle, and thread ✂️. She marched into the woods and found the Wolf snoring loudly.
Snip, snip, snip. Very carefully, she opened the Wolf’s belly. Out popped Barnaby! Then the others! One by one, all six goats hopped out, unhurt and safe. They hugged their mother tight.
“Quickly,” whispered Mama Goat. “Gather some heavy river stones.”
The seven goats worked together to fill the Wolf’s belly with stones, and Mama Goat sewed him back up tight.

When the Wolf finally woke up, he felt incredibly thirsty. He stumbled toward the river to get a drink, but the stones were so heavy that—SPLASH!—he tipped right over into the water. The current swept him far, far away, never to be seen again 🌊.
Mama Goat and her seven little kids danced all the way back to the cottage. From that day on, they were always careful, and they never, ever opened the door to strangers again 🏠❤️.

Gus was four years old and had an inseparable friend: Mikey 🐭. Mikey was a special toy, a square of fabric with a small mouse head in one corner. Even though he was old and patched up, Gus couldn't sleep without him. It was as if, when he hugged him, everything around him became safe and calm.
Gus's moms had tried to get him attached to other toys, but Gus always went back to Mikey. He was his faithful companion, and without him, the nights were impossible.

One afternoon, while they were tidying up the house, Mikey disappeared. Gus and his moms looked for him everywhere: under the bed, in the drawers, even in the washing machine. But Mikey didn't appear. That night, Gus cried inconsolably. His moms gave him cuddles and words of comfort, but the emptiness of not having Mikey by his side seemed enormous. Finally, exhausted, he fell asleep.
In his dream, a teddy bear with a golden ribbon around her neck appeared. The bear, with a soft and reassuring voice, introduced herself:
—Hello, Gus. I'm Luna 🐻, the guardian of lost objects. I'm afraid Mikey has arrived in our world, but you're not alone. Come, I want to show you something.

Luna took Gus's hand, and together they flew through the night sky until they reached a magical place, a forest enveloped in a luminous mist. There were little houses made of leaves and trunks. As they approached, Gus saw that inside slept little magical beings: elves, fairies, and little raccoons 🧚‍♂️🦝.

—When a comfort object arrives here —explained Luna—, it finds a very special new purpose. It helps our little inhabitants sleep well. And if they rest, they can use their powers to help the great wizards, like Santa Claus, the Tooth Fairy, or even the Easter Bunny.

Gus looked curiously at the little houses. In one of them, a tiny elf was hugging Mikey, fast asleep. Although he felt sadness seeing him there, he also felt some relief thinking that Mikey was helping someone else.
—Is Mikey happy? —asked Gus with a lump in his throat.
—Very happy —assured Luna with a warm smile—. Now he has a great mission, but he also wants you to move on. That's why I'm bringing you a very special gift.
Luna gave him a small cushion with soft edges, decorated with a golden star ⭐ embroidered on it.

—This is your new magical helper. It doesn't replace Mikey, but it has a little bit of his magic. When you hug it, remember that Mikey is fulfilling an important task, and that you can also be brave at night.
Gus hugged the cushion and felt a comforting warmth. Then, Luna gave him a kiss on the forehead.
—This magical kiss will help you always remember how special you are, Gus, and how much Mikey loves you, wherever he is.

When he woke up, Gus found the little cushion next to him. Although he still missed Mikey, he hugged the cushion and thought about the little elf who was now sleeping thanks to his friend. That night, for the first time, he fell asleep without crying.

Over time, Gus continued to remember Mikey, but he no longer felt sadness, but joy for everything he had given him. And so, little by little, he grew up with a new companion by his side and a memory full of affection in his heart.

Once upon a time, there was a little drop of water trapped in the eternal embrace of a glacier. There, in the heart of a mountain, everything was stillness and silence, broken only by the crunching of the ice as it slowly moved. The drop slept, nestled among thousands of its companions, under a sky so clear it seemed like a window to infinity. Until one day, the sun caressed the summit with warm fingers, and the drop awoke from its long wait. ❄️

At first, it only felt a tickle, a slight vibration. Then, like a distant whisper, the water began to slide. The drop, now liquid and alive, let itself go, slipping down the icy surface. Its journey began in a timid trickle, which gradually transformed into a singing stream. Each curve of the road was full of dancing lights, reflected in the rock walls and in the leaves of the pine trees that guarded the river. 🌲💧

The stream grew, joining others, forming a wide and majestic river. The drop felt the force of the water surrounding it, but there was no rush, only a constant and serene movement. Around it, silvery fish swam in zigzags, and the roots of the trees plunged into the banks as if they wanted to touch it. The air smelled of damp earth and life. 🐟🌿

Further on, the river carried it to a waterfall. The drop felt the vertigo as it plunged into the void, but also the freedom of floating in the air, suspended for an instant that seemed eternal. The water roared as it crashed against the rocks, but as it fell into the pool, everything calmed down again. The drop sank for a moment, embraced by the coolness of the bottom, before emerging and continuing its way to the sea. 🌊✨

When it reached the ocean, the horizon opened immense, infinite. The drop was rocked by the waves, which carried it like a cradle. Sometimes, the water was so transparent that it could see the gentle swaying of the algae and the flashes of the most curious fish. Other times, the deep blue enveloped it completely, as if the whole world were a whisper. 🐠🌅

With the heat of a sunny day, the drop felt something inside it change. Little by little, it began to rise, light as a feather. It was the wind who now carried it, merging it with the sky. There, among the clouds, everything was a gentle game. It joined other drops, forming swirls and caresses among fluffy cottons. The air was fresh, with a sweet touch that only the sky could offer. ☁️☀️

The clouds traveled together, crossing landscapes of green valleys and golden plains. Until, one night, the air turned cold again. The drop felt how it transformed, crystallizing into a snowflake. Now it was light and delicate, and its fall from the heights was so slow that it seemed like a dance. Around it, millions of flakes fell silently, filling the world with a white calm. ❄️🌨️

Finally, the drop, turned into a bright flake, landed gently on a snow-covered mountain. There, in the stillness of winter, it rejoined its companions, patiently waiting for the sun to wake it up again. Because it knew that its journey would never end, and each stage was a whisper of calm, a perfect moment in the eternal cycle of life. ⛅❄️

86.t: Distant Horizons 6: Veridita, the Connection to the New World
p: The orange sun of Veridia-7 rose over the hills, painting the forests with a soft gold. Aura, Zoe, and Alexia stood by the fence where the galebres rested. These creatures, which combined the majesty of an Earth horse with the agility of an antelope, had become a vital resource for exploring the planet's difficult terrain. However, taming them had been quite a challenge.
—I think he hates me —said Zoe, stepping back as a mottled-skinned galebre snorted in front of her.
—He doesn't hate you, he's just sizing you up —replied Aura, gently stroking the neck of her own galebre, a young one named Lira.

The galebre turned its head towards her and emitted a low gurgle that seemed to vibrate in the air. Since that day in the cave, Aura had noticed something different in her relationship with these animals. It was as if they perceived something in her, something that even she didn't fully understand.
—Why is he so docile with you? It's like...
—Like he understands something we don't —completed Alexia, who was already mounted securely on another long-legged galebre, her posture relaxed and confident.
—How do you do it? —asked Zoe, admiringly.
—It's not magic —replied Alexia with a satisfied smile—. It's patience. And trust.

Aura smiled distractedly. Her mind was elsewhere. Since inhaling that gray dust in the cave, something inside her had changed. Under certain lights, her skin emitted a subtle glow that seemed to pulse with the planet, not to mention the intricate design that had emerged from her injured ankle, extending up her leg, like an organic tattoo.

The scientific team had called it Veridita, an unknown mineral until their arrival on Veridia-7. Initially, they had mistaken it for Tantalum, one of the essential materials for the biomechanical prosthetics that ensured their survival on the planet. But they soon realized it was something completely different. The measurement scanners they used, precise and advanced, failed to detect it under certain conditions, which had led to the initial confusion. On the other hand, while Tantalum was inert, Veridita seemed alive, interacting with organisms, adapting them in still unpredictable ways.

Aura had felt it in her own body: a connection to the planet, to its rhythms. The galebres seemed to perceive it too. They had alerted the colony to the earthquake before the systems even detected the slightest anomaly. Mara had mentioned that the way the mineral entered the body could make some kind of difference. Isaac, who had only absorbed it through open wounds, had shown a clear increase in his physical abilities. In Aura, who had also inhaled it, the changes were more subtle, more emotional.
—Aura? —called Zoe, interrupting her thoughts—. Are you coming or would you rather stay here dreaming about Isaac?
Aura felt the heat rise to her face. —I'm not dreaming about Isaac —she protested, though she knew her friends wouldn't believe her.
—Come on, don't play hard to get. He's gorgeous, and he looks at you like you're the center of his universe —joked Alexia as she held out her hand to help her mount.

Aura sighed, deciding not to deny the obvious. —It's complicated —she admitted as she climbed onto Lira—. Sometimes it seems like everything fits between us, but there's something… I don't know, something that doesn't let me be sure.
—It's because you care about things. And you care about him too —said Zoe with a reassuring smile—. Give it time.

The group set off towards a nearby meadow, where the galebres could run freely. As they rode, Aura felt how Lira reacted to her thoughts even before she gave the orders. It was as if they were connected.
—Don't you feel it? —asked Aura, stopping her galebre at the top of a hill.
—Feel what? —asked Alexia, looking around.
—It's like something is watching us. But not in a threatening way… It's like the planet knows we're here —replied Aura, stroking Lira's neck.

Zoe and Alexia exchanged glances. Since the earthquake, their friend had become more introspective, almost mystical. Sometimes they weren't able to follow the line of her thoughts, but they respected her.
Suddenly, a flash caught their attention. At the foot of the hill, a small crack in the ground shone with the silvery glow of Veridita.
—Shall we go explore? —asked Zoe, her eyes shining with excitement.
Aura nodded. They carefully descended and dismounted, watching as the galebres stayed close, restless but not fleeing.

As they approached, they saw that the crack contained a pure crystal of Veridita, iridescent and complex. Alexia took out a tool to try to extract a sample, but as soon as she touched it, the galebres began to snort nervously.
—Wait! —exclaimed Aura, stopping her.

Aura closed her eyes and placed her hand on the crystal. A current of gentle energy ran through her arm, and for a moment, she could feel the environment like never before: the roots of the trees, the flow of the wind, even the heartbeats of her friends.
—Aura, are you okay? —asked Zoe, worried.
—It's… It's like the planet is alive, and this —she said, pointing to the crystal— is part of its essence.
They decided not to extract the Veridita, but to mark the place for the experts to investigate later.

Back in the colony, they noticed a different atmosphere. The colonists were gathered in small circles, speaking in low voices, and the tension was palpable. In the center of the meeting hall, Mara was arguing with other officials while a holographic star map floated over the table.

—We have a problem —said Mara, her voice grave but contained—. The analyses indicate that the main moon of Veridia-7 is rich in Tantalum. Without it, we won't be able to continue developing the prosthetics or the advanced technologies we need to survive here.
An older man, in a technician's uniform, crossed his arms with a worried expression. —We know how essential it is, but sending an expedition now... we're not ready to face additional risks yet.
—We'll never be completely ready —replied Mara firmly—. But this mission can't wait. We don't have enough Tantalum to keep the systems running in the coming months. It's a matter of survival.

Aura watched the discussion from a corner, noticing how the colonists around her shared uneasy glances. Although Mara's words were rational, the emotional cost of separating from their loved ones, even for temporary shifts, along with the dangers involved in such a mission, seemed to weigh on everyone.
Later, as she crossed a corridor of the colony, she ran into Zoe. She avoided looking at her, hurrying past her.
—Zoe! What's wrong? —Aura caught up with her, grabbing her arm.

Zoe turned with a tense expression. —Your mother is going to send my parents on the expedition —she said, her voice full of reproach—. In addition to the mine, she wants to set up a telecommunications base up there—
Aura opened her mouth to reply, but didn't know what to say. The contained rage in Zoe's eyes turned into sadness. She lowered her gaze.
—Sorry, Aura —she murmured, her eyes red—. I know it's not your fault, or your mother's. But I can't help it. I'm scared.
Aura felt a pang of compassion and, without thinking, put a hand on her shoulder. —I understand. I would be scared too. But your parents are strong. They're going to come back.
Zoe nodded weakly before leaving, leaving her alone in the hallway.

On the day of departure, the entire colony gathered in front of the ship. The colonists formed a solemn corridor through which the members of the expedition passed. One by one, the team members crossed the hatch, disappearing into the luminosity of the interior.

The silence was total, broken only by the slight sound of footsteps. When it was the turn of the last member, a young technician, he stopped at the threshold and turned his head towards the crowd. His eyes slowly scanned the faces with a mixture of melancholy and determination, until they met Aura's.

Time seemed to stop, the world disappeared momentarily around her. As their eyes met, Aura felt an inexplicable warmth in her chest, a current of emotion that she couldn't fully understand. It was just an instant, but it was etched in her mind when the technician finally turned around and disappeared inside the ship.
When the hatch closed and the ship took off, the weight of the farewell fell on the colony like a dense cloud. Some hugged in silence, others returned to their tasks, their eyes fixed on the ground.

Hours later, Aura was called to the medical facilities along with Isaac. Apparently, they wanted to study the effects of Veridita on their bodies further because they were considering starting to use it on other colonists. While they waited, they sat in silence, but Aura was aware of Isaac's presence in a way that went beyond the physical. It was as if she could feel him, like a constant and warm energy next to her.

Isaac, guessing the line of her thoughts, raised his hand and placed it gently on Aura's. The warmth of his touch sent a shiver down her spine. For a moment, neither of them spoke, but the connection between them was palpable, a silent current that didn't need words.
—Aura —he said finally, his voice barely a whisper—. Why do you keep avoiding me?
Aura looked into his eyes, and in them she saw something deep: tenderness, devotion, but also the strength of someone who had learned to fight against their own demons.
—I'm not avoiding you —she replied, though she knew it wasn't entirely true.
Isaac didn't insist. He withdrew his hand delicately, but the intensity of his gaze remained etched in Aura's mind as the door of the room opened and they were called in.

As the doctors began to analyze them, Aura let herself be carried away by her thoughts. She felt that something inside her was changing, not only physically, but also in how she saw the world and the people around her.

For the first time since they arrived on Veridia-7, she didn't feel like a stranger. Now she saw opportunities, connections, and a prosperous future on a planet that, although mysterious, was teaching them how to live in harmony with it.
When the examination was over, Isaac waited for her outside. Aura looked at him, and although she didn't say anything, a small smile appeared on her face.
—Would you like to take a walk? —he asked.
Aura accepted, feeling that a part of her, the one that had been fighting against her own fears, had finally decided to take the step.

87.t: Miss Millie and the Perfect Red Ribbon
p: One sunny morning, Miss Millie the mouse was sweeping the wooden porch of her cozy cottage. Swish, swish, swish went her broom, pushing away the autumn leaves. Suddenly, something sparkled near the steps.
It was a shiny gold coin! It sat there, gleaming and perfect, as if waiting just for her.
"Oh my! What luck!" Miss Millie squeaked with delight. "With this treasure, I can finally treat myself to something special."

She scurried off to the village market, her nose twitching with excitement. She passed stalls selling cheddar cheese, colorful fabrics, and shiny mirrors. But then, she saw it: a bright, silk red ribbon 🎀. It was the most beautiful thing she had ever seen.
"If I wear that ribbon, I’ll be the fanciest mouse in the whole neighborhood," she thought. She bought it immediately and tied it in a perfect bow around her tail.
On her way home, Miss Millie couldn't believe the stir she caused. She looked so fancy that all the animals in the neighborhood stopped to stare. One by one, they stepped up, hoping to win her heart.
First came Mr. Rooster 🐔, puffing out his colorful chest feathers. "Miss Millie, Miss Millie, you look so divine! Won't you please be mine?"
Millie twirled her tail and asked, "Perhaps. But how will you wake me up in the morning?"
The Rooster cleared his throat and blasted, "COCK-A-DOODLE-DOO!"
Miss Millie covered her ears. "Oh, goodness no! That is far too loud. It would give me a headache before breakfast!" she said politely but firmly.
Next came Percy the Pig 🐷, trotting over with a confident grin. "Miss Millie, Miss Millie, you look so divine! Won't you please be mine?"
Millie asked again, "And what sound will I hear around the house?"
Percy grunted deeply, "OINK! OINK!"
"Oh, dear no! That sound is much too grumpy for me," Millie replied, and Percy trotted away, huffing.
The parade continued. A donkey who brayed too loudly, a duck who quacked too much, and a dog who barked non-stop. Miss Millie shook her head at all of them. None of them seemed right.
Finally, Jasper the Cat 🐱 arrived. He was sleek, elegant, and had the most polite manners. He bowed low. "Miss Millie, Miss Millie, you look so divine! Won't you please be mine?"
Millie looked at him. "And what does your voice sound like?"
Jasper purred, soft as velvet, "Meeeoooow... Puuuuurrrrr..."
Miss Millie was charmed. "Oh, how soothing! You sound like the perfect gentleman." Dazzled by his elegance, she agreed to go with him.

Jasper, looking very pleased with himself, invited her to his house to celebrate. It was a grand house, and Jasper seemed so kind. But the moment they stepped inside, he slammed the door shut with a loud THUD.
He leaned in close, his smile turning wicked. "Miss Millie, Miss Millie, you look so divine... and you'll make a delicious dinner tonight!"
Millie’s paws began to tremble, but she remembered what her grandma always told her: When you're in a jam, use your wits, not your feet.

"Oh, wait! Dear Jasper!" she said, keeping her voice sweet and steady. "You can't eat me just like that! Look at my beautiful red ribbon. Don't you think it makes me special? Surely, a fancy cat like you wants to show off his prize to the neighbors before dinner?"
Jasper, who was very vain, paused to think. "You have a point. No one has caught a mouse as fancy as you."

The moment Jasper turned his head to look in the mirror, Miss Millie saw her chance. She leaped onto the windowsill and scrambled out the open window, running home as fast as her little legs could carry her.

Back in her safe, cozy cottage, Miss Millie let out a huge sigh of relief. She took off the red ribbon and looked in the mirror. She had learned a big lesson: just because someone looks perfect on the outside, doesn't mean they are nice on the inside.
A few days later, Millie was watering her garden when a quiet voice spoke up. It was Timothy 🐭, a simple field mouse carrying a small basket of sunflower seeds.
"Hello, Millie," he said shyly. "I heard you like flowers, so I brought you some seeds for your garden."
Millie smiled, truly touched. "That is very thoughtful of you, Timothy. Thank you."

They started talking, and soon realized they loved the same things: watching the sunset, baking cheese pies 🧀, and keeping a tidy home. Timothy didn't have a fancy coat or a smooth purr, but he had a kind heart.

They became the best of friends. And when they finally decided to be together forever, Miss Millie knew she had chosen the right partner—someone who loved her for who she was, not just for her pretty red ribbon.
And so, Miss Millie lived happily ever after, safe and sound, knowing that true beauty is found in the heart. 🐭❤️

In the alien city of Kalta, a place in a galaxy still unknown to Earthlings, lived Trix, a little green alien with big, bright eyes who always dreamed of being a hero. But nobody took him seriously because he was super clumsy. If he tried to help carry boxes, they'd end up flying everywhere. If he offered to clean something, he'd break the mop. So, Trix spent his days dreaming of big adventures… that never came. 🌟
One morning, while walking with his head down, he heard a shout:
—"The Sun Egg is gone! Without it, Kalta will freeze tonight!"

The Sun Egg was a glowing sphere the size of a melon that floated above the central tower, keeping everything warm and bright. Without it, Kalta would be left in icy darkness. Trix felt a fire light up in his chest.
—"I can find it!" he exclaimed. But the neighbor standing next to him chuckled.
—"You? You can't even carry a backpack without falling over." 😅

Embarrassed but determined, Trix walked to the marketplace, where everything from singing fruits to color-changing clothes was sold. It occurred to him that whoever stole the Sun Egg might try to sell it at the junk stall. There, a small, rusty robot named Rusty watched him from a pile of parts. 🤖
—"Are you going to laugh at me, too?" Trix asked.

—"No, I'm offering to help," Rusty replied in a metallic, slightly scratchy voice. "Although… you'll need something better than clumsiness to save the Sun Egg. Luckily, I have a radar… that mostly works."
Trix, excited, accepted Rusty's help. The robot, who could detach his legs and turn them into wheels, began to scan the square. Bleep... bleep...
—"I'm picking up a trail that leads… yikes! Into the maze of pipes. Are you brave enough?" 🚀

Trix gulped, but he nodded. Together, they entered the dark tunnels under the city. The walls were covered in glowing moss, puddles bubbled, and strange echoes bounced in the distance. At one point, Rusty got stuck in an old doorway.
—"Go on without me," he said. "I'll guide you with the radar from here."

Trix continued, trying not to trip too much. Suddenly, a group of small, speedy shadows zipped past him. "It's the zorbits!" he whispered. They were mischievous little creatures, like ferrets with glowing eyes, that stole shiny things to decorate their dens. ✨

Following their tracks, he arrived at a room lit up by the Sun Egg. The zorbits were having some kind of party, jumping around the egg as if it were a trophy. Trix hid behind a pipe, trying to think. "I can't just grab it… they'll chase me, and I might accidentally squish one," he thought.

Suddenly, he remembered Rusty. With some junk he found nearby, he built a small, shiny lure that reflected the egg's light. He tossed it to the other side of the room, and the zorbits, curious and excited, scurried after it, leaving the egg unguarded.
—"This is my chance!" Trix dashed toward the egg, grabbed it carefully (though he almost dropped it), and ran out before the zorbits noticed. 🏃‍♂️
When he arrived back in the square with the Sun Egg, the crowd gasped in amazement. Trix had saved Kalta! Even Rusty, who was waiting for him outside the maze, seemed thrilled. 🥳
—"Well, what now?" the robot asked.
Trix smiled.
—"Now, I just hope I don't fall while putting this back in its place."

89.t: The Star Who Forgot How to Shine
p: Once upon a time, there was a star that shone less brightly each night. She was small and delicate, but she had always had a warm, constant glow that illuminated the dark sky. However, one day, the star stopped finding meaning in her light. She looked around and felt that no matter what she did, her place in the universe seemed empty, and her heart filled with anguish. 🌌
The Moon, 🌙 who was her closest neighbor, noticed her sadness. In her serene tone, she said—"Little star, perhaps you need to shine brighter. Make everyone see you, and I'm sure you'll feel better."
The star tried to shine with all her might, but the effort only exhausted her more. 😔
Then, the Wind 💨 passed by, whispering softly—"Don't worry. Stop shining for a while and rest. I'll make sure no one notices."
The star hid behind a veil of darkness, but that only increased her loneliness. 🌑
A nearby planet 🪐 also wanted to help. From a distance, it offered practical advice—"Perhaps what you need is to rotate in a different orbit. Change your routine, and I'm sure you'll feel better."
The star tried to move, but she couldn't find another position in the sky where she felt comfortable. 🌠
Finally, a passing cloud ☁️ spoke to her as she floated nearby—"Cry, star. Sometimes, letting your tears fall relieves the soul."
And the star cried. She cried until her tears mingled with the raindrops from the cloud. But although her pain eased a little, the anguish didn't disappear. 🌧️

One night, as the star watched silently from her corner of the sky, she heard a very soft voice coming from Earth. It was a little girl named Lily 👧 who was looking up, sitting on her windowsill. She said—"I wish the star up there felt better. I've always looked at her when I don't know what to do, because her light keeps me company."

The star felt something different inside her. It wasn't advice or a solution; it was a pure wish, a genuine connection. Lily kept talking, but her words were simple, full of innocent love—"It doesn't matter if you don't shine much. I like that you're there."

For the first time in a long time, the star felt warmth inside. Her light, though faint, became warm again. Not because she had been given a solution, but because someone had simply accepted her as she was. ✨

From then on, the star understood that she didn't have to be the brightest or the strongest. It was enough to be herself, because somewhere, someone was looking at her and finding comfort in her presence.
And her light returned to illuminate the sky in her own unique and special way. 🌟

Once upon a time, there was an orange elephant named Gus 🐘. He had a big trunk, enormous ears, and on his head, he proudly wore a blue bow that sparkled in the sun. All the animals in the forest stared when he passed by, because they had never seen such an original elephant before. Even the wind seemed to respect him, gently swaying his bow each morning.

One day, Gus decided to explore beyond his familiar pond. He walked and walked until he reached a place where the trees were as tall as giants, and the flowers had petals so big they looked like colorful umbrellas. There, he met a very jokey frog named Freddy 🐸, who burst out laughing when he saw him: “Ha, ha, ha! What a weird elephant you are!”
In his deep voice, Gus replied: “Weird? Well, this is how I was born. I like my orange color, and the blue bow is the best accessory I have.”
Freddy shrugged, not quite knowing what to say. But inside, the poor elephant felt a little pang of sadness when he was judged for his appearance.

Continuing his way, Gus met a playful giraffe named Ginny 🦒, who was stretching her neck to taste some very high leaves. Seeing her, the elephant greeted her enthusiastically: “Hello! Could you tell me what's beyond the trees?”
And she replied: “Beyond, you'll find a big meadow full of magical flowers… but I don't know if you could fit in there with your color so… bright.”
This time, Gus decided not to be sad. Instead, he remembered something his mom, a wise gray elephant, had taught him: “Differences are special, there's no need to be ashamed of them.”

With a firm step and his head held high, he entered the meadow. The flowers were a deep violet, so soft and fragrant that they made him sneeze: “Achoo!” 🌸 And right in the middle of the meadow, Gus discovered a little white rabbit named Ricky 🐇, who was sobbing.
“What's wrong, little friend?” asked the elephant.
The rabbit explained between sobs: “My ears are too long, and nobody wants to play with me. They say I look like a mop.”
Gus looked at him tenderly and said: “I'm told I'm weird because of my color and my bow. But you know, I like being different.”

Gus decided to teach Ricky a game he invented himself when he felt a little lonely: the “silly poses” game. It was about each of them creating the funniest pose they could think of. The rabbit waved his ears like flags, and Gus started spinning his trunk at full speed. Both burst out laughing, and without realizing it, other animals began to arrive, curious to see so much joy. Soon, Freddy 🐸 and Ginny 🦒 also wanted to join the party.
When everyone joined the game, they understood that what they called “weird” about others was actually something that made them unique and fun.
Gus, proud of his orange color and his blue bow, told them: “It doesn't matter what we look like on the outside, what matters is how cheerful and kind we are on the inside.”

That's how the animals learned that differences should not separate us, but enrich us with new experiences. And each one, with their own style and color, lived happily accepting themselves and celebrating the diversity of others. 🌈

In the Miller family 🏡, the days were a whirlwind of chaos. Every morning, the house was filled with rushing, backpacks on the floor, unfolded clothes, and exhausted parents running around to get everything ready. The four siblings, Clara, who was 13 years old, the twins Dylan and Sophia, who were 10, and little Marty, who was 6, always found something more interesting to do than help with the household chores.

One day, the parents, tired of no one helping, announced a strike. “We are exhausted, so we have decided not to do anything until everyone participates in the house chores,” said their mother. “Nothing at all?” asked Clara, raising an eyebrow.
“Nothing,” confirmed her father with a smile.

At first, the children took it as a joke. “No problem, this will be a piece of cake,” said Dylan. That night they had frozen pizza that Clara heated in the oven. Everyone laughed and enjoyed their “new freedom.” But on the second day, things started to get complicated. Sophia couldn't find her clean basketball uniform. “Mom, I don't have my uniform!” she shouted from her room.
“Not my problem,” replied the mother while reading a book on the sofa.
On the other hand, Dylan couldn't find his tennis racket. This mess is a disaster, he muttered while rummaging through the piles of coats and backpacks piled up in the entrance.

At dinner time, they realized that the frozen pizzas were gone. They tried to improvise something with what was in the pantry, but the dirty dishes kept piling up in the sink, and no one was willing to wash them.

On the night of the third day, little Marty started to cry. “I don't want to sleep in my bed! It's all messed up and there are piles of things on the floor. It looks like there are monsters hiding!” The older siblings tried to calm him down, but they realized that the mess had gotten out of control. “We can't continue like this,” said Clara while hugging her little brother. “This is chaos. If we don't do something, we won't last much longer.”

The next day, Clara, Dylan, and Sophia decided to divide the chores. Clara took care of tidying up the living room, Sophia started washing the clothes, and Dylan tried to organize the entrance. Although at first everything was a disaster, little by little they began to make progress. The parents, seeing their effort, began to help subtly. “If you place the glasses like this, more fit in the dishwasher,” suggested the mother.
“Can I help you fold those shirts?” asked the father to Sophia.

The mother put music 🎶 on the speaker, and soon everyone was singing and dancing while they worked. Clara took care of sweeping, Dylan washed the dishes, and even Marty helped put away the toys. What seemed like an impossible mission became a fun family activity.

When they finished, the parents surprised them with a special plan. “We've earned it! We're going out to eat and to the movies this afternoon,” announced the mother. The children, excited, got dressed quickly and enjoyed an unforgettable day.

That night, upon returning home, Clara offered to prepare some sandwiches 🥪 for everyone while the mother bathed Marty and the father helped the twins with their homework. The atmosphere at home was much calmer and more organized.

From then on, the children understood that helping with chores not only made the house more comfortable, but also helped the parents to be less tired and have more time to have fun together. In addition, they discovered that, with music and a little good humor, chores could even be fun.

The Miller family never returned to the chaos of before. And although sometimes they had to remind the children of their responsibilities, they knew that by working as a team, everything was much better. 💪✨

92.t: The Scrubby-Dubbies vs. The Grime Gang
p: In a tiny corner of our world, so small no one can see it, lived tiny beings who had always lived peacefully with people. But as cities grew and humans changed the world around them, many of these beings lost their homes. Some found ways to adapt, others moved far away, but one group became very grumpy and mean: The Grime Gang.

The Grime Gang had found a way to fight back: they grew yucky germs and trained tiny soldiers that would stick to kids' hands at the park, on the swings, and even in the sandbox. Those soldiers would wait for kids to touch their mouths or noses to release the germs into their bodies and then sneak back to their hideouts.

But The Scrubby-Dubbies, led by the wise Dr. Sparkle, didn’t want people to get sick. They knew that humans didn’t realize the harm they were causing, so they worked in secret to protect them. One day, Dr. Sparkle discovered something terrible: The Grime Gang had created a germ so strong that people couldn't get better easily.
Meanwhile, a 5-year-old boy named Leo was having fun at the park, climbing on the monkey bars and building castles in the sand. When it was time for a snack, he didn't want to wash his hands.
—It’s just a little dirt, Mom! —he said as he took a big bite of his sandwich.

That night, Leo started to feel very yucky. His tummy hurt and he felt hot with a fever. While he was sleeping, something amazing happened. The Scrubby-Dubbies entered his body with their magic cure, but they needed Leo's help to beat the super-germ.
In his dreams, Dr. Sparkle and his team reached out to Leo.
—Leo, The Grime Gang sent their soldiers onto your hands, and from there, into your body. That’s why you’re sick —Dr. Sparkle explained—. We can help you, but you have to promise us something.
—Anything! —said Leo, with tears in his eyes.
—You must always wash your hands before you eat. It’s the only way to defeat The Grime Gang and protect yourself from their attacks.

Leo nodded. The Scrubby-Dubbies worked all night, bravely fighting the germs. The next morning, Leo woke up feeling much better. He ran to the bathroom, grabbed the soap, and started washing his hands while singing a little song:
"Goodbye to yucky germs, scrub and rinse away, with soap and water, I'll win the day!"

From that day on, Leo never forgot to wash his hands. And when he saw his friends at the park, he would tell them the story of The Scrubby-Dubbies and The Grime Gang, so they could learn how to stay healthy too.
And that’s the story of how Leo became a hand-washing hero. 😊

93.t: Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves
p: Once upon a time, in a faraway city, there lived a humble carpenter named Ali Baba, who lived modestly with his wife. Every day he went out into the forest 🌲 to gather wood to sell, all the while dreaming of a more peaceful life.

One day, while collecting firewood, he heard the sound of horse hooves 🐎. He quickly hid behind a tree and watched as a group of forty men arrived at an enormous rock 🪨. The leader of the group, with a firm voice, said:
“Open, sesame! 🌟”

Right before Ali Baba's eyes, the rock opened up as if it were alive, revealing a dark cave. The men went inside with their heavy sacks and, after a while, came out empty-handed. When the leader shouted:
“Close, sesame!”
The rock closed once again.
Ali Baba, intrigued, waited for the men to leave. With his heart racing ❤️, he approached the rock and said:
“Open, sesame!”

The rock opened, and he stepped into the cave. There he discovered a treasure 💰 like he had never imagined: piles of gold coins, jewels, and precious objects. He took only a few coins and returned home, determined to use this wealth wisely.

When Ali Baba arrived home, his wife asked to borrow a scale from the wife of his brother, Cassim, to weigh the gold coins. His sister-in-law, curious about what they could possibly be measuring, stuck a little bit of melted wax 🕯️ to the bottom of the scale before lending it out. When it was returned, she found a gold coin stuck to the bottom and rushed to tell Cassim.
Filled with greed 😈, Cassim went to see his brother and demanded to know where he had gotten the gold. Trusting him, Ali Baba revealed the secret of the cave and the magic words.
The next day, Cassim headed to the cave with large sacks to fill with treasure. He entered, saying:
“Open, sesame!”

Inside, amazed, he filled the sacks. But when he tried to leave, he forgot the magic words. When the thieves returned, they found him trapped. Before killing him, they managed to force a confession out of him: his brother Ali Baba had discovered the cave.

The thieves, furious 😠, devised a plan to capture Ali Baba. The leader disguised himself as an oil merchant 🛢️ and arrived at Ali Baba's house with forty jars, claiming he was looking for a place to stay. In reality, each jar hid one of the thieves, except for one that contained actual oil.

Morgiana, the family's housekeeper, noticed something strange. While working in the kitchen 🍳, she heard whispers coming from the jars. Realizing the danger, she came up with a plan to save her master.

She heated the oil until it was boiling 🔥 and poured it into the jars, putting an end to the thieves one by one. Then, she faced the leader of the thieves, who tried to attack her, but Morgiana took him down with a hidden dagger and protected the family.

Grateful for her bravery, Ali Baba offered Morgiana a permanent place in his home 🏡 as an equal. Together, he, his wife, and Morgiana decided to use the treasures from the cave wisely, sharing the wealth among the most in need in the city.

Ali Baba learned that true wealth is not found in gold, but in kindness and in surrounding oneself with loyal people 🤝. And so they lived, helping their community and sharing the fortune that, by chance, had come into their lives.

It was a cool afternoon in the last days of winter, and Lily was walking hand-in-hand with her parents through the neighborhood streets. The air carried the scent of plants beginning to sprout, and the sun, now warm, illuminated everything around them with its golden glow. Turning a corner, they came to a shop with a sign that read: "Bulk, Flavors and Aromas of the World." Lily felt a spark of curiosity and was happy to feel her mother's hand guiding her toward that place 🌱.

Upon entering, the air changed. A warm blend of spices, soaps, and grains filled the room, as if the whole world had been kept in that place. The light was soft, filtered by linen curtains, and Lily felt as if she had entered a secret corner, full of things to discover ✨.

While her parents spoke with the shopkeeper, Lily slipped over to the large fabric sacks that lined the wall. There was everything: chickpeas round as marbles, small and smooth lentils, white rice that looked like a handful of tiny moons, and many more legumes and seeds that she didn't know. Lily looked around, making sure no one was watching her, and put her hands into a sack of lentils. They were cool and light, slipping through her fingers like a river of cold pebbles. She closed her eyes and listened to the whisper they made as they fell from her hand. Then she moved to the sack of rice; the grains were hard and heavier, but just as pleasant. The beans surprised her with their smoothness and tinkle as they bumped against each other.

In the spice section, an explosion of colors and aromas enveloped her. There were jars filled with oregano as green as a meadow in spring, with a scent that reminded her of the pizzas she loved to eat 🍕. Lily took a deep breath and felt her stomach rumble with hunger. The peppercorns were small and round, with shades ranging from deep black to reddish brown and even white. But what caught her attention the most was a star anise; she held it in her hand and observed its sharp points and dark center, like a small work of natural art.

Nearby, large glass jars contained liquid soaps in pearly colors. Lily approached one of them just as a woman was opening the tap to fill a glass bottle. She watched fascinated as the gel flowed slowly, with a texture that looked like shiny honey 🍯. Her eyes followed the hypnotic movement of the substance until the bottle was full. The tap closed with a soft click, but a drop remained hanging thick, delicate, shiny.

Mother: “Do you want to help me?” 💞 — Her mother's voice snapped her out of her reverie. Lily nodded with a smile. Her mother gave her a metal scoop and showed her how to use it to fill a bag with chickpeas. The scoop had a dull shine and was cold to the touch. Lily enjoyed the dry sound of the chickpeas falling into the cloth bag, as if they were playing a tiny drum. When she finished, she carefully carried the bag to the scale, where the shopkeeper weighed the containers with calm movements.
As she left the store, with her hands still smelling of spices and the sensation of the grains on her skin, Lily looked at her parents.
Lily: “Can we come back here another day?” 🌱
Father: “Of course, we can! Did you like it?” 😁

Lily nodded enthusiastically. As they walked back home, the feeling of tranquility and discovery accompanied her, as if she carried a piece of that store in her heart. And that night, as she closed her eyes, she felt the whisper of the lentils, the smell of oregano, and the shine of the pearly soap in her memory again 🌟.

95.t: Raven and the Gift of Fire
p: Long, long ago, in the days when the world was wrapped in a blanket of eternal ice and snow, humans lived in darkness and bitter cold. They knew nothing of the warmth of fire and relied only on thick furs and huddled shelters to stay alive. Yet, high atop the jagged mountains, the ancient gods guarded the fire, hiding it jealously within a massive cavern that glowed with its golden light.

Raven, who in those days possessed plumage as white as the frost itself and was renowned for his sharp wit, watched the humans suffer below. His strong wings could carry him above the ice, but his heart ached for the mortals who had no escape from the freezing winds. He decided he must help them, even though he knew that challenging the gods was a perilous task.

One day, Raven flew to the very peak of the mountain where the gods were holding a grand feast beside their roaring fire. Pretending to be nothing more than a harmless bird, he perched near the cavern’s entrance, watching closely as they fed the sacred flames. It was then that he hatched a plan.

He waited patiently until the gods were distracted by their banquet and laughter. With movements as swift and silent as a shadow, Raven swooped down toward the flames. Snap! He snatched a burning branch in his beak and shot out of the cavern before the gods could even realize what had happened.

The fire blazed against his beak, and flying sparks rained down upon his beautiful white feathers, scorching them. The smoke swirled around him, dyeing his plumage a deep, sooty black. Despite the searing pain, Raven kept flying, protecting the flame with all his might while the furious gods chased him across the sky.

Finally, exhausted but triumphant, Raven reached the human settlements below. He dropped the burning branch onto a pile of dry wood. Whoosh! The fire spread instantly, lighting up the dark sky and filling the freezing air with a warmth the humans had never felt before.

Although the gods could not steal back the flame, they punished Raven for his daring theft. From that day on, his feathers remained black as coal, and his singing voice was taken away, replaced by a harsh, raspy sound—a permanent reminder of the sacrifice he made to bring humanity the gift of fire.

The humans celebrated Raven as their hero. And so, thanks to his bravery and sacrifice, fire became the heart of their homes, helping them cook, keep warm, and survive in the cold world that surrounded them.

96.t: Red, the Fox Who Found His Home
p: Hunger and cold had weakened him so much that he could barely move his paws. His small wire cage was the forest itself: a fence that had trapped his tail and left him prisoner, and in trying to free himself desperately, he got even more caught, hurting himself. When he heard footsteps in the snow, he tried to move; his instinct was to flee, but he only managed a weak whimper.
—Dad, come quickly! —exclaimed a child's voice.

—Don't touch him, son; he looks like a fox cub. If we don't do something for him, I don't think he'll last much longer —said a male voice— I'll get my tools from the shed; can you bring a blanket, sweetheart? —he added.

The human freed him carefully, ignoring his exhausted growls and speaking to him in a soft, calm voice. Suddenly, he felt something warm and soft enveloping him. A hand stroked his little head carefully. He smelled of humans, but not like the hunters; it was different, warmer, less threatening. He closed his eyes as they carried him to a place full of unknown smells and soft noises.
—He's gorgeous, even though he's worn out. Do you think he'll survive? —asked a woman's voice.
—We'll do what we can. He's very young; he can still recover —replied the man.

The warmth of the place enveloped him, and when they offered him food, hunger was stronger than fear. That warm liquid that smelled like meat was the best thing he had ever tasted in his life. Little by little, he regained strength, and with it came the desire to explore. The boy, who was always nearby, began to call him.
—Look how soft and fluffy his fur is getting!
—Indeed, he's a very handsome redhead, we should call him Red 🦊.
Red didn't know what all those words meant, but he felt safe and protected, receiving constant attention and care.

The days in that house were wonderful. There were other animals, bigger ones, who always wanted to play with him. They were the dogs, fun companions who sometimes managed to catch his attention, but other times Red preferred to go his own way. He liked to sniff around, bite things, and run like the wind through the garden. However, not everything worked perfectly; he got many scoldings for his behavior, especially the day he escaped to sneak into the neighbor's chicken coop. He had a great time, but apparently, he scared them so much that they stopped laying eggs for several days.

What happened was that they caught his attention so much that he couldn't resist. One day Red sneaked into the coop again, attracted by the clucking of the hens and the smell of their feathers. He ran after them, excited, but the chaos he caused was enormous. The birds flew and screamed, and the neighbor appeared with a weapon. Red ran home, but the neighbor followed him and confronted his human family.
—This can't go on like this! —shouted a man at the door of the humans' house— If it happens again, I'll call Animal Control. This fox can't stay here; he's a danger to my animals!
Red watched from inside the house. He didn't understand the exact words, but he knew the tone was angry. Something was wrong.
That night, the humans talked for hours.

—He told us clearly. If he enters the coop again, he could do something irreversible to the hens. Besides, if Animal Control comes, they'll catch him and… —The woman paused and looked at Red, who was curled up next to the boy on the sofa.
—We can't allow them to take him anywhere. But he can't stay here either. We need to find a place where he can live like a fox.

Thus began the calls. Red saw them talking with tension in their voices, one after another. Many said they didn't accept foxes; others seemed like cold places, without space, where Red wouldn't be happy. Until, finally, someone told them about a place called Granja el Aprisco, a sanctuary for domestic and wild animals.
—It's just what we need. He'll be safe there.
Red felt that something big was happening when they put him in the car. The boy cried as he stroked him for the last time.
—You'll be okay, I promise.

When they arrived at the sanctuary, the smells were different. Earth, grass, animals. Kind humans welcomed him and guided him to a space with other foxes. There was an old fox with gray fur who moved carefully, as if she couldn't see, and another fox who watched him with disinterest before walking away.

Red felt strange. It was a big place, which scared him as much as it caught his attention. At first, he didn't dare to move much and stayed away from the other foxes, but one rainy afternoon, the old fox, Luna 🌙, allowed him to approach. She sniffed his face carefully and let him curl up next to her. Little by little, they began to spend more time together.

The other fox, Trueno ⚡, almost always ignored him, but one day, while playing at hunting small prey hidden by the caretakers, Red saw him smile. It was a different smile, more like his own, and for the first time, he felt that maybe this place was his home.

Trueno allowed Red to follow him and showed him how to act in that life of semi-freedom. They became playmates and hunting partners, and for the first time in a long time, Red felt that he truly fit in.
When the humans who had cared for him came to visit, Red looked at them from afar, with a mixture of curiosity and nostalgia. The humans hugged while watching him scamper around the enclosure.
—He's where he needs to be. Look at him; he seems happy.
And it was true. For the first time, Red felt his emptiness filling. He had found his place.
Geppetto lived all alone in a cozy, humble cottage. One afternoon, feeling a bit lonely, he decided to carve a puppet out of wood to keep him company.
"I shall call him Pinocchio," Geppetto said, carving the wood with great care and affection.
That very night, a shimmering light filled his workshop. It was The Blue Fairy.
"Good Geppetto," she whispered, "you have brought so much joy to others that you deserve to have your wish come true. You shall have a son."
With a gentle wave of her magic wand, she tapped Pinocchio, and the wooden doll sprang to life.
"Papa!" exclaimed Pinocchio, hopping right off the workbench.
The Fairy warned him gently:
"Pinocchio, if you prove yourself to be brave, truthful, and unselfish, someday you will become a real boy. And you, Jiminy Cricket, shall be his conscience. Help him tell right from wrong."
The Fairy tapped her wand on a cricket who lived in Geppetto’s pantry, giving him a tiny suit and a big job to do.
The next morning, Geppetto, bursting with pride, sent Pinocchio off to school. Even though he had very little money, he had sold his only warm coat to buy Pinocchio a spelling book.
"Pinocchio, please don't get distracted, and always listen to Jiminy Cricket," Geppetto said, shivering slightly in the cold air.
"I promise, Papa!" Pinocchio chirped.

Pinocchio left the house with his spelling book tucked under his arm, but he hadn't gone far when he heard music and laughter drifting from the town square. It was a puppet theater! Curiosity bubbled up inside him, stronger than his promise.
I just have to see what's happening inside! he thought.
"Don't do it!" warned Jiminy Cricket, hopping onto his shoulder. "Remember, you need to go to school!"
"It will only take a minute," said Pinocchio, brushing the cricket aside.
When he arrived at the booth, Pinocchio realized he needed money for a ticket. Without thinking twice, he sold his brand-new spelling book to a stranger and bought a ticket.
Inside the tent, he was amazed to see puppets dancing and singing. But suddenly, the puppets on stage stopped. They recognized him!
"It's Pinocchio! It's our brother!" they cheered, rushing to hug him.
The audience grumbled at the interruption, and the puppet master, a giant man named Mangiafuoco, stomped onto the stage.
"What is the meaning of this ruckus?" he roared with a voice like thunder.
When he realized what had happened, Mangiafuoco looked at Pinocchio with a scowl.
"You ruined my show. Tonight, I shall use you as firewood to cook my dinner!"
Pinocchio burst into tears.
"Please, sir! Don't burn me! I just want to go home to my Papa!"
Mangiafuoco looked scary, but deep down he had a soft heart. Seeing the little puppet cry made him sniffle.
"Alright, alright. I forgive you. And so you can get home safely, take these five gold coins."
Pinocchio promised to use them to help Geppetto and ran out of the theater, shouting his thanks.
On the way home, Pinocchio met a limping Fox and a blind Cat.
"Where are you going with all that gold?" asked the Fox with a sly grin.
"I'm taking it home to help my Papa."
"Why not make it grow into a mountain of gold?" suggested the Fox. "If you plant the coins in the Field of Miracles, a money tree will grow overnight!"
Before he could agree, Pinocchio heard a tiny voice. It was Jiminy Cricket, who had been following him.
"Don't trust them, Pinocchio! They are tricking you!"
"Don't be a wet blanket, Jiminy. They just want to help me," Pinocchio replied, dazzled by the Fox's words.
They arrived at the dusty Field of Miracles and dug a small hole.
"Now, bury the coins and wait for the tree to sprout," said the Cat.
Pinocchio did as he was told. But when he came back later, the hole was empty. The coins were gone!
"I've been robbed!" he cried, tears rolling down his wooden cheeks.
Jiminy Cricket hopped onto a leaf nearby.
"I warned you, Pinocchio. Now you have nothing."
Penniless and hungry, Pinocchio wandered until he fainted on the road from exhaustion.
When The Blue Fairy found Pinocchio lying on the path, she carried him to her cottage and cared for him until he woke up.
"Pinocchio, how did you end up in this trouble?" the Fairy asked sweetly.
Pinocchio, feeling ashamed, started to make up a story.
"Well, actually, I was walking to school just like Papa said, but a gang of giants attacked me and..."
Before he could finish, something strange happened. Creak! His nose began to grow. First an inch, then two, until it was so long he couldn't turn his head without bumping into the walls.
"Every time you tell a lie, your nose will grow," explained the Fairy patiently. "It is a sign that you are not being honest."
Pinocchio began to weep.
"Please, help me! I promise never to lie again!"
The Fairy tapped his nose with her wand, and zing!—it shrank back to its normal button size.
"Remember, Pinocchio: honesty is one of the most important virtues."
Pinocchio promised to be good, but it wasn't long before he was tempted again. His old 'friends,' the Fox and the Cat, found him.
"Pinocchio, come with us to Toyland! There is no school and no work. It's just candy and games all day long!"
Pinocchio hesitated, but the idea was too sweet to resist.
Toyland was loud and colorful, filled with roller coasters and popcorn. Pinocchio spent days having fun without a care in the world, until one morning he felt something fuzzy on his head.
"My ears!" he screamed, grabbing them.
He had started turning into a donkey! Soon after, he was sold to a circus, where he was forced to perform tricks and work very hard.
Jiminy Cricket finally found him in the circus stables. He brought terrible news: Geppetto had gone to sea to look for Pinocchio and had been swallowed by a giant Whale!
One day, while performing a trick, Pinocchio tripped and hurt his leg. The circus owner, angry that the donkey was lame, threw him into the ocean, with Jiminy Cricket clinging to his tail.
As soon as he hit the water, the donkey spell broke, and Pinocchio became a wooden puppet once again.
"I have to save my father!" cried Pinocchio, paddling bravely into the deep waves.
Luck was on his side. After swimming for a while, the massive Whale rose from the depths and—GULP!—swallowed Pinocchio whole.
Inside the dark, damp belly of the beast, he saw a flickering light. It was Geppetto!
"Papa! I'm here to rescue you!"
"My son! I knew you would come back."

Together, they came up with a plan. They gathered driftwood from old shipwrecks inside the whale and built a roaring fire. The smoke made the Whale sneeze—AH-CHOO!—and the force blasted them right out into the open sea.
Back home, Geppetto was weak and sick from his journey. Pinocchio worked tirelessly to nurse him back to health, chopping wood and bringing food every single day.
"Papa, I promise to study and be a good son from now on."
One night, while they slept, The Blue Fairy appeared in the room.
"Pinocchio, you have proven yourself brave, truthful, and unselfish. You deserve to be a real boy."
When the morning sun rose, Pinocchio looked at his hands. They weren't wood anymore!
"I'm a real boy!" he shouted with joy.
Geppetto hugged him tight, tears of happiness in his eyes. He finally had a son of flesh and bone.
"Now we are a real family."
From that day on, Pinocchio lived happily, working hard and being a good son, always remembering the lessons from his magical adventures.

In Ryan's room, everything was spotless. On the shelves, perfectly arranged boxes and baskets gleamed, and every toy had its assigned place. In charge of this kingdom of perfection was the White King ♟️, a proud and strict chess piece who ruled from his board, placed high on the desk. From there, he saw everything, making sure order reigned in his domain.

However, there was a problem. Although everything was organized, Ryan hardly played with his toys anymore. Ever since he got a phone for his last birthday, he spent more time with the screen than with his old adventure companions. Many toys had been locked in boxes for months, forgotten at the back of the shelves. The White King knew this, but he preferred a silent, orderly kingdom to a chaotic and messy one.

One day, Alex 🚴, Ryan's little brother, burst into the room on his tricycle. Despite the sign on the door that declared it "off-limits" with a picture of him as a baby crossed out in red, Alex couldn't resist the temptation.
