When he braked, he crashed into a shelf, knocking over several figures. The White King watched the disaster with horror, for he could not stand Alex.

—Alex, get out of my room! —yelled Ryan, as he reluctantly picked up the scattered figures. But as he placed an action figure back, he couldn't help but move it as if it were in a battle. For a few seconds, Ryan was playing again. Then, he remembered his phone and put everything back in its place.

Early that morning, while people and toys were asleep, Spider-Man 🕷️, a flexible rubber figure, came up with a plan. Carefully, he rappelled down from the shelf and opened the box of building blocks. He scattered several pieces around the room and returned to his spot with a mischievous smile.

The next morning, Ryan woke up and stepped on a block. —Ouch! Alex, stop touching my stuff! —he yelled. However, as he picked up the pieces, something sparked within him. He started building a small tower, then a house. Without realizing it, he was playing again. The White King watched from his board, astonished and annoyed by the chaos.
When Ryan went down for breakfast, the toys gathered to discuss what had happened. The White King demanded answers.
—This is unacceptable! Who disobeyed my rules?
Spider-Man stepped forward.
—I did, your majesty. But it was for a good reason. Ryan played with us because of the mess.

The argument heated up among the toys. Some defended order; others supported Spider-Man, arguing that being forgotten in boxes was pointless. Finally, Spider-Man decided to seek advice in Alex's room.
There, he found Glowbug 🌟, an old stuffed toy that had once belonged to Ryan.

—It’s normal for kids to stop playing as they get older —explained Glowbug in a calm voice— But it's also true that if we're too hidden away, they can't find us. Order is good, but hoarding toys that are no longer interesting doesn't help. You have to find a balance and appreciate what you have.
Spider-Man returned to the kingdom of toys with this lesson. They organized a meeting between the White King's advisors and the toys from Alex's room. Glowbug proposed a revolutionary idea:
—Ryan could donate some toys he doesn’t use anymore to kids who need them. That way, there would be more space for the ones he does want.
The White King, though reluctant, agreed.
—Very well. Let’s do it. But everything must be done with the utmost order.

That night, Spider-Man and Glowbug prepared a flyer with the slogan: “Are your toys bored to bits? Give away the ones you don't use and bring back the fun!” The next day, Ryan woke up with new energy, and after seeing the flyer on his nightstand, he decided to reorganize his room. He set aside toys to donate and left others more accessible.

That afternoon, he played with Alex and discovered that, although his brother was small and sometimes annoying, he was a great playmate. The White King watched from his board, satisfied that his kingdom was not only in order but also full of life and laughter.

From then on, Ryan's room was not just an orderly place, but also a space where toys and the stories they told were cherished. And, most importantly, where Ryan slowly discovered that playing would always be more fun than a screen.

Once upon a time, there was a young parrot named Pete, who lived with his mom in a cozy tree by the harbor. Pete had a dream: to become a real pirate parrot. He had heard exciting stories about adventures on the high seas, hidden treasures, and secret maps, and he wanted to be part of that world.
One morning, full of enthusiasm, Pete headed to the pirate ship called The Wandering Treasure. On the dock, Captain Silver Hook, a big man with an eye patch and a thick beard, watched him curiously.
—Why do you want to be a pirate parrot, little one?—asked the captain in a gruff voice.
Pete puffed out his chest and replied:
—I want to live adventures, find treasures, and repeat fearsome phrases like, “Surrender, sea dogs!”
The captain smiled amused.
—Very well, young Pete. You shall be our pirate parrot apprentice. But listen carefully: you will have to repeat my orders so that the crew hears them. And remember to be quick and clear!
Pete nodded enthusiastically and climbed onto the ship, ready to start his training.
The first day, Pete was nervous but determined. The captain shouted:
Pete wanted to be quick, but his nerves betrayed him and he repeated:
Suddenly, the pirates began looking for pots and pans, ready to fill them with food. The captain raised an eyebrow and then burst out laughing.
—No, lads! Leave the pots! It's port side, not pot side!
The crew laughed along with the captain, and Pete scratched his head with his wing, embarrassed. 🪶

The second day, Pete appeared with a small eye patch that his mom had made for him that morning. Proudly, he stood on Captain Silver Hook's shoulder, who showed him off amusingly, awakening the tenderness of the crew. ❤️
—Very well, little one, today we are going to bury our loot. Give the order to hoist the sails!
Pete, excited, squawked with all his might as he flew around the deck:
—Bury the sails! Hoist the loot!

The pirates looked at him confused, not understanding exactly what the order was. Silence fell on the ship until everyone burst into laughter. Pete, embarrassed, stopped squawking and went to perch on the helm, but Silver Hook encouraged him amidst the laughter.
—Don't give up, Pete! Try again! AAAAAArrrrrrrrr, hoist the sails, you lazy bums!
And Pete took flight again:
—Hoist the sails! Hoist the sails!
The crew, with their hearts ignited by laughter and good humor, got to work, beginning another day of hard work. ⚓

On the third day, Pete wanted to practice his pirate laugh to impress everyone. He had heard the other parrots on the ship laugh with a fearsome “Argh, argh, argh!” However, when he tried, what came out was:
—Hee-hee-ha-ha-ho-ho!
The pirates couldn't contain themselves and doubled over with laughter. 😂
—That parrot has a unique laugh! He's our happy parrot!—shouted one of the sailors.

Pete perched triumphantly on his captain's shoulder. That our from the sailor had touched his heart; he had earned his place. He knew he had much to learn, but he was determined to succeed and strive to the fullest in the company of the crew, who supported and encouraged him. 🏴‍☠️
—You have potential, lad. Follow this path and you will be the best pirate parrot of the seven seas.
Pete decided that his pirate parrot name would be "Happy Parrot" and continued to work hard to fulfill his dream, with his little patch knitted by his mom always accompanying him. 🦜

100.t: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
p: Once upon a time, in the heart of a deep winter, a Good Queen sat sewing by a window framed in black ebony. As she watched the snowflakes drift down like white feathers ❄️, she pricked her finger with her needle, and three drops of ruby-red blood fell onto the snow. Admiring the beautiful contrast of red, white, and black, she made a wish:
Good Queen: "Oh, how I wish I had a daughter as white as snow, as red as blood, and as black as ebony!" 😊
Soon after, her wish came true. She gave birth to a baby girl whom she named Snow White. But sadly, the Good Queen passed away shortly after, leaving the King and the little girl in deep mourning. 😢

Years went by, and the King married again. His new wife was a woman of striking beauty, but she was also arrogant and cruel. She possessed a magic mirror, and every single day she would stand before it and ask:
Evil Queen: "Mirror, mirror, on the wall, who is the fairest of them all?" 🪞
And the mirror would always reply:
"You, my Queen, are the fairest of them all." ✨

The Evil Queen was satisfied, for she knew the mirror could not lie. But as Snow White grew older, her kindness made her more beautiful with each passing day. One morning, when the Queen asked her usual question, the mirror replied:
"You, my Queen, are fair, it’s true. But Snow White is a thousand times fairer than you." 🌹

Green with envy, the Evil Queen summoned a Huntsman. She ordered him to take Snow White deep into the forest and bring back her heart as proof that she was gone forever. The Huntsman led the girl into the woods, but when he looked at her innocent face, he couldn't bring himself to harm her.
Huntsman: "Run, child! Run far into the forest and never come back!" 🏃‍♀️
To trick the Queen, he hunted a wild boar and presented its heart to her. The Evil Queen accepted it with a wicked grin, believing her rival was gone for good. 🐗❤️

Meanwhile, Snow White ran until her legs felt heavy. Just as the sun began to set, she stumbled upon a tiny cottage nestled among the trees. Inside, everything was small: a table set with seven little plates and seven little cups, and seven tiny beds lined up in a row. Tired and hungry, she nibbled a little bit of vegetables from each plate 🍽️ and took a sip of water from each cup 🥤. Then, she curled up on one of the beds and fell fast asleep. 🛌

When night fell, the owners of the cottage returned. They were seven Dwarfs who worked hard all day digging for diamonds in the mines. They lit their seven lanterns and gasped when they saw someone had been in their home!
Barnaby: "Who has been eating from my plate?" 🍽️ Silas: "Who has been drinking from my cup?" 🥤 Pip: "And look! Who is that sleeping in my bed?" 🛌

When they held their lanterns up to Snow White, they were amazed by how peaceful she looked. They decided to let her sleep. When morning came, Snow White woke up with a start, but the Dwarfs smiled kindly. She told them her sad story, and the eldest dwarf, Barnaby, nodded solemnly.
Barnaby: "If you look after our cottage and be careful not to let strangers in, you can stay with us. We will keep you safe." 🏡
Snow White happily agreed. She and her new friends—Barnaby, Silas, Pip, Jasper, Fritz, Otto, and Gus—lived together in joy. 😊
However, back at the castle, the Evil Queen discovered the truth. She stood before her mirror and asked:
Evil Queen: "Mirror, mirror, on the wall, who is the fairest of them all?" 🪞
"You, my Queen, are fair, it’s true. But Snow White, in the cottage beyond the mountains, is still a thousand times fairer than you." 🌹
Furious, the Evil Queen concocted a plan. She used a spell to disguise herself as an old peddler woman. She traveled to the cottage, knocked on the door, and called out:
Evil Queen: "Fine wares for sale! Pretty laces and ribbons!" 🧶
Snow White peeked out the window. "Good morning, ma'am. What do you have there?" 👀
Evil Queen: "Beautiful silky laces, my dear. Perfect for a girl like you." ✨
Thinking there was no harm in buying a ribbon, Snow White opened the door. The old woman smiled sweetly.
Evil Queen: "Let me help you tie it properly. It will look lovely." 😊
Snow White turned around. The woman began to lace the bodice, but suddenly she pulled the strings tighter and tighter. "Isn't that too tight?" Snow White gasped, feeling dizzy. 😟
Evil Queen: "Just a little more!" the woman hissed. She pulled with all her might until Snow White couldn't breathe and collapsed to the floor. 😈
Evil Queen: "Now I am the fairest once again!" she cackled, fleeing into the woods. 🏃‍♀️💨
That evening, the Dwarfs returned and found Snow White lying still.
Jasper: "What happened to her?" 😟
Seeing the tight laces, Silas quickly cut them with his knife. Snow White took a deep breath and opened her eyes. When she told them what happened, the Dwarfs looked worried.
Barnaby: "That was no peddler. That was the Queen! You must never open the door to anyone." 🚪🚫
Back at the castle, the Evil Queen asked her mirror again, only to hear the same infuriating answer: Snow White was still alive and fairer than her. 🌹

Shaking with rage, the Evil Queen went to her secret dungeon. She took a beautiful apple and dipped half of it into a sleeping potion. One side was green, and the other was a tempting, shiny red 🍎🍏. Disguised as a sweet farmer's wife, she returned to the forest.
Evil Queen: "Fresh, sweet apples for sale!" 🍎🍏
Snow White looked through the window but kept the door locked. "I cannot let anyone in," she said firmly. 🚫🍎

Evil Queen: "Are you afraid of poison?" the woman laughed softly. "Look, I have too many apples and hate to see them go to waste. Here, I'll share one with you. I will eat the green half, and you can have the sweet red half." 🍎🔪

Seeing the woman eat the fruit, Snow White thought it must be safe. The red apple looked so delicious that she couldn't resist. She opened the door and took a bite. Instantly, the room spun around her. She fell softly to the floor like an autumn leaf 🍂.
Evil Queen: "White as snow, red as blood, black as ebony! This time, the dwarfs cannot wake you!" 😈
She returned to her castle, asked the mirror, and finally heard:
"You, my Queen, are the fairest of them all." ✨
When the Dwarfs came home, they found Snow White on the floor. They tried everything, but she would not wake up. Pip wiped a tear from his eye.
Pip: "We cannot help her this time..." 😔

She looked as if she were only sleeping, her cheeks still rosy. They could not bear to bury her in the dark earth. Instead, they built a beautiful coffin made of clear glass so they could always see her. They placed it on a mountaintop surrounded by wildflowers 🌸🌼🌺. The sunbeams danced on the glass, lighting up her face. ☀️
Barnaby: "We will watch over her forever," he promised. 🕊️

Time passed, until one day, Prince Julian from a neighboring kingdom was riding through the forest 🏇. He saw the glass coffin shimmering on the hill. When he saw Snow White, he was captivated by her peaceful beauty.
Prince Julian: "It is a tragedy for such kindness to be lost to the world. Please, let me take her to my castle. I will honor her memory as if she were my own family." 💔

The Dwarfs saw the Prince's sincerity and agreed. He ordered his servants to carry the coffin gently. But as they walked down the rocky path, one of the servants stumbled! The coffin jolted, and the piece of poisoned apple dislodged from Snow White's throat. Her eyes fluttered open! 🍎✨
She sat up, looking around in wonder. Prince Julian was overjoyed to see her alive. He helped her out of the glass case and asked her to come with him to his kingdom. Snow White smiled and agreed. 💍
They invited everyone to their wedding celebration. When the Evil Queen arrived, thinking she was the fairest, she saw Snow White on the throne and turned pale with shock. 😱
Snow White, now strong and safe, banished the cruel woman from the kingdom forever, never to harm anyone again. 🏰🚫
Snow White and Prince Julian lived happily ever after, surrounded by their friends, the Dwarfs. And the magic mirror sat silent and dusty on the wall, for true beauty had finally won. 🌟❤️

🌌 Life on Veridia-7 went on. After several months of study and experimentation, the medical team concluded that the best way to inoculate the Veridita was through the drinking water system. Initial tests had shown that this method allowed for a uniform and controlled distribution, promoting the colonists' adaptation without disrupting their daily routines.

They were already fully aware that the veridita enhanced the colonists' adaptive abilities. The exact long-term effects remained a mystery, and the changes were subtle in most, barely an increase in sensory acuity or a more intuitive connection with the planet's rhythms. However, in Aura and Isaac, they had seen that the effects were much more pronounced. Their skin had acquired a faint glow under certain conditions, the patterns on their skin in areas where contact had been through wounds grew more intricate each day, and their cells seemed more resistant to the conditions they were subjected to in the lab. They were convinced that their survival on the planet depended entirely on their communion with the veridita. 🌱

Meanwhile, research continued. They had established a science base remote from the main one where they studied the local fauna with an approach of minimal possible interference in the ecosystem. Zoe had been temporarily assigned to do a formal internship at that base. It was a unique opportunity for her, as she had shown a natural talent for biology and was thrilled. Every afternoon, she would video call Aura to tell her what she had seen or learned that day.

That morning, the first rays of Veridia-7's orange sun illuminated the main base. The fresh air, entering through the various windows, mingled with a palpable tension, as if the planet itself were trying to issue a warning. Aura woke up with a knot in her stomach. It wasn't just a bad dream; something was off. An unsettling vibration in the air, barely perceptible, caused the small windowpanes to emit a faint hum. The light that normally flooded the room with warmth today had a colder, almost threatening hue. Even the slight murmur of the ventilation system seemed irregular, as if the planet were breathing erratically.
She was just finishing getting dressed when a rhythmic sound came from the door. It was Isaac's signature knock. 🛎️
—Did you sleep well? —Isaac asked, leaning against the doorframe when Aura opened it, as he buttoned up his uniform. His tone was gentle, but his eyes reflected a shared unease.
Aura shook her head. —No, something… something isn't right. You feel it too?
Isaac nodded. —Everyone feels it. I haven't heard anyone laugh this morning. Even the galebres are restless.

They melted into a comforting hug, sharing a moment of calm amidst the tension. —We'll be okay —Isaac murmured, resting his forehead against hers. Aura looked into his eyes, feeling a swirl of emotions, and lifted her face to his, seeking his lips. Isaac responded to the gesture, pressing his mouth against hers.

🌟 Aura was the one who kissed him first. He had invited her for a walk and, using the excuse of helping her over a small, uneven patch of ground, he took her hand. She didn't let go, so he, emboldened, invited her to sit on a fallen log, facing him, and whispered softly, asking if he could kiss her. She moved closer, perceiving Isaac as she never had with anyone before—the rapid beat of his heart, the iridescent sheen of his skin, the whisper of his hair in the breeze, the intensity of his gaze, his scent, his breath. She pressed her lips against his, letting all her senses take over and marking the beginning of their romantic relationship.

The base's alarm cut through their embrace, confirming their suspicions. A soft, indistinct, somewhat metallic voice announced that the probes had detected a sandstorm approaching from the east. The colonists had eight hours to prepare. ⚠️

The facilities were a hive of activity as scientists and technicians secured the various departments and equipment. Mara directed the operations with authoritative calm, assigning tasks and verifying safety measures.
—Aura, stay in the safe zones. We don't need any more risks —said Isaac, seeing her gathering tools.
Aura spun around abruptly. —I'm not a child, Isaac. I can help just as much as you can.
—That's not what this is about… —he began to say, but Aura cut him off with a harsh look before walking away. Isaac sighed in frustration and returned to his work.
Mara, who had observed the exchange, decided to approach her daughter later. She found her chance during lunch and went over to Aura, who was already sitting at a table, alone, picking at her food.
—Honey, can we talk?
Aura nodded reluctantly, setting her spoon down on the table and crossing her arms.
—Isaac… it's complicated. He's changed, I know, but I can't forget how he used to treat you. There's something about him that worries me, though I can't quite put my finger on it —said Mara.
Aura frowned. —Why can't you stop judging him? He's here, working hard like everyone else. It's not fair.
—I don't want you to get hurt, Aura. Sometimes there are things a mother can't help but see… —Mara sighed, but her daughter had already made it clear she wasn't willing to listen.

When the storm arrived, it was unlike anything they had ever experienced. The sand particles moved at an alarming speed, battering the base's structures with force. What initially seemed like just an intense storm soon revealed its true nature: the sand was corrosive. Within minutes, the fasteners on one of the sections began to deteriorate. 🌪️
—The crop section! —yelled one of the technicians.

Protected by their gear, several colonists, including Aura and Isaac, rushed out to try to protect the area. The scene was chaotic. Melted equipment, weakened structures, and crops exposed to the abrasive wind. The scientists' protective suits were beginning to fail against the corrosion.
—Aura, watch out! —Isaac shouted as a metal bar crashed down beside her. —You have to get out of here!
—Not without protecting the crops! —she retorted.

The scientists began to scream, backing away as the sand, having breached their protective gear, came into contact with their skin. However, it barely affected Aura and Isaac, especially Isaac's hands, which were completely untouched.

They sealed the section with the Earth plants, but the research area with the hybrids was completely exposed with no way to protect it. To their relief, however, they saw that those crops were holding up quite well against the onslaught of sand. When the storm finally passed, the unease in the main base grew. Communications with the remote science base, where Zoe was stationed, had been cut off. The probes couldn't fly, and the ships were temporarily unusable due to the damage.
Mara organized a rescue party, and Isaac was among the volunteers. —I want to go. I know Zoe, and I can help if something went wrong.

Mara hesitated but finally nodded. —Be careful. Everything will depend on you until we can send help. —Although she valued the boy's courage, she couldn't help but worry about the look of devotion Aura gave him.

The journey to the base was long and dangerous. Luckily, they had the galebres 🐎, which hadn't been affected by the storm at all. Though they were agile, the journey would take at least a day and a half, factoring in the time they'd need to rest. Isaac took charge of the animals' well-being during the brief overnight stop to regain their strength. Thanks to his connection, he understood the galebres' needs better than anyone, and they seemed confident and calm by his side. This earned Isaac a deep respect from the other volunteers, who began to follow and obey him, even though he was visibly younger than the rest.

When they reached the base, the scene was devastating. The collapsed structures formed a chaotic labyrinth of twisted metal and materials eroded by the storm. The remains of roofs and walls were scattered about, exposing parts of what were once research labs and rest areas. The scientists who had managed to survive had improvised shelters in the few intact corners. Their faces showed fatigue and dehydration. Some had superficial burns on their skin from the corrosive sand, while others wore expressions of fear and relief upon seeing the rescue party. However, Zoe was not among them.
—Keep searching —Isaac ordered, guided by an inexplicable feeling. Finally, he found her under the enormous leaves of a local plant, seriously injured but alive.
—The plant… it protected me —Zoe murmured before losing consciousness. Isaac carried her in his arms, leading the way back while taking care of her and the other injured.

When the probes were operational again, they were sent to find the rescue party. Once contact was made and their situation and needs were assessed, they sent hovercrafts, which would take much less time to make the trip, to transport the injured. Aura got on one of them to lend a hand, trying to calm the anxiety that had been eating at her since she heard what happened. Upon arrival, she saw Isaac leaning over Zoe, helping to make her comfortable and checking her vitals with an almost professional focus. Zoe, pale and exhausted, gave him a weak, grateful smile. It was a scene that might have seemed routine at another time, but something about Isaac's posture or the way Zoe looked at him filled Aura with an inexplicable unease. She shook her head, trying to rationalize her thoughts, telling herself that the important thing was that everyone was safe.

Isaac's hands moved carefully over Zoe's wounds, cleaning them and making sure she was comfortable. Zoe, despite her weakness, gave him looks full of gratitude, and that silent connection between them hit Aura like a splash of icy water. Her heart pounded as she tried to ignore the pang in her chest that made her question everything. The way he protected her, Zoe's grateful glances… it was all too much.

Isaac smiled when he saw Aura, but she couldn't return it. There was something different in his expression, something that filled her with an inexplicable dread. As the hovercrafts carried them back, Aura fixed her gaze on the landscape, trying to ignore the feeling that something had changed between them. She felt a deep sense of betrayal, when she should have felt relieved and happy for her friend. She couldn't stop thinking about the arguments where Isaac would reproach her for her kindness to other colonists, arguing that they might mistake it for a different kind of interest.
Zoe had rested her head on Aura's lap, who felt the doubts tightening in her chest. Deep in her mind, she knew that the storm clouds weren't just in the skies of Veridia-7. ⛈️

🐾 Buddy was a tiny, scruffy dog with one of his fangs sticking out. When he was a puppy, a woman adopted him and loved him immensely. Maybe that's why, in his dreams, Buddy was a huuuuuuge dog who lived huuuuuuge adventures.

The woman had no children, and at one point, she became very ill, so much so that she had to be admitted to the hospital. Her neighbor, a always smiling lady who had two other dogs, took care of Buddy with all the love in the world. 😊

The problem was that while he dreamed, his exploits were so, so big that Buddy made gigantic growls, gave mighty swipes and kicks, and ended up throwing his companions out of their beds. The other two doggies, tired of flying out of their beds every night, were so angry that they didn't even want to play with him anymore. The neighbor tried to have Buddy sleep with her in her bed, but nothing, the little guy wouldn't let her get a wink of sleep! 😵
—Buddy, you have to relax —she said while stroking him—, we can't go on like this!
She tried to wake him up when he started dreaming, but they both ended up exhausted after spending so many interrupted nights. 🥱
Desperate, the neighbor went to a friend at the dog park who had a huge dog, a Neapolitan mastiff named Goliath. 🐕 Goliath was so big that, probably, not even in his dreams could Buddy match him.
Goliath's owner listened amused to Buddy's story and his big dreams.
—Bring him to me for a few days, don't worry, Goliath gets along with everyone —he said laughing—. Surely with him he will find his place.

That same afternoon, Buddy arrived at Goliath's house. Upon entering, the little one couldn't help but gape: Goliath's bed looked like a giant sofa, and his feeder, a washtub! During dinner, Goliath ate from his huge plate, while Buddy had a small bowl with his fair share. Then, Goliath's owner sat on the sofa and began to pamper the two dogs while watching a show. Buddy was delighted. 🛋️🍖

When it was time to sleep, Buddy didn't dare to lie down near Goliath. But the great mastiff made a little space for him, moved his huge paw to accommodate him, and gave him a tender look. Buddy, warmed by the body of his new friend and lulled by his rhythmic breathing, fell asleep immediately. 😴
And then the dreams began.

In the first growl and swipe that Buddy let out, Goliath, without barely opening his eyes, put one of his enormous paws on top of the little one and kept him in place. Surprisingly, that was enough for Buddy, without realizing it, to continue sleeping peacefully. 🐾
The next morning, everyone had rested like never before.

When Buddy's owner recovered, the little one returned home. Although he had been treated like a king by Goliath and his owner, nothing compared to the happiness of reuniting with his owner. Since then, his dreams continued to be just as fantastic and full of adventures, but something had changed: Buddy now knew how to dream big without bothering others.
Perhaps because, deep down, he had discovered that the most beautiful dreams are those that are shared with those you love most. 💕
And the end. 🎉

The morning sun illuminated Aprisco Farm 🌞, a sanctuary for domestic and wild animals, when a group of children arrived with their backpacks full of curiosity. The caretaker guided them through the different enclosures, explaining the story of each rescued animal. When they arrived at the meadow where Felipe, the deer 🦌, lived, the woman stopped and pointed to his slender figure under the shade of a tree.
—Look! This is Felipe, a deer who is about to return to his home in the forest —she said with a smile.
The children approached the fence, observing the majestic animal with amazement. A girl raised her hand and asked:
—Can we touch him?
The caretaker shook her head gently.

—No, little one. Felipe is a wild deer. Even though he's here temporarily, our goal is for him to return to his natural home and keep his wild instinct. Deer belong in the forest, where they run free and enjoy nature.
She leaned in slightly towards the children, as if about to tell an important secret.
—But Felipe's life changed one night when he was crossing the road with his herd. A car that was going too fast couldn't brake in time, and Felipe was hit.
The children's eyes widened in surprise.
—Was he badly hurt? —asked a curly-haired boy.

—Yes —replied the caretaker in a serious tone—. He had a fracture in one of his legs and some wounds on his side. But luckily, the occupants of the car were okay and quickly called the Civil Guard, who came to rescue him. They brought him here, where we have a small hospital for wild animals.
The children nodded in admiration.

—At the hospital, they operated on him and took care of his wounds —continued the caretaker—. For a while, he had to stay in a small pen because we needed to give him medication and make sure he healed well. He didn't like being locked up or near humans, but it was necessary. As soon as he got a little better, we released him into this larger space so he could regain his strength and feel freer.
A girl with glasses raised her hand.
—Is he going to stay here forever?
The caretaker smiled tenderly.

—No, on Saturday we're going to release him back into the forest. Felipe is fully recovered now, and we've done everything we can to prevent him from getting used to humans. We want him to go back to his herd and live free, as he should be.
The children looked at each other, excited. Then, a smaller girl asked:
—Are you going to miss him?
The caretaker was silent for a moment before answering.

—Of course, I will. It's always hard to say goodbye to an animal that we've cared for so lovingly. But my heart fills with joy knowing that we're doing what's best for him. Felipe belongs in the forest, and our mission is to return his freedom.
The children nodded, some with smiles and others with thoughtful expressions. Before continuing with the tour, the caretaker took the opportunity to give them an important message.
—That's why it's so important to protect natural spaces —she said—. Wild animals need forests, rivers, and mountains to live. Taking care of the environment also means taking care of them.

As the children walked away, Felipe raised his head and looked towards the horizon. His instinct told him that he would soon return home. And in the heart of the forest, he would regain the freedom he longed for so much. 🌳🦌

104.t: The Science of a Gentle Touch
p: Once upon a time, there was a scientist named Emma who had a very special mission: she wanted to discover what made a gentle touch so magical. For her, these touches weren't just signs of love; they were something deeper, something that healed the spirit and, with it, the body too. ✨
Emma always said that a gentle touch had a hidden science, a secret she wanted to discover and share with the world. 🧪
One afternoon, while sipping a warm cup of tea in her lab, she remembered all the gentle touches that had comforted her throughout her life. ☕

First, she thought of the nurse who gave her a shot when she was little. Her arm was trembling with fear, but before the needle even touched her skin, the nurse gently stroked her hand. It was as if her fear dissolved into the air, just like the sugar had dissolved in her tea, replaced by a warm calm, like a whisper saying: "Everything is okay, I'm here with you."

Then she remembered her teacher, the afternoon she scraped her knee on the school playground. Her tears were falling like a little stream, but when her teacher stroked her hair and carefully cleaned the scrape, Emma felt the pain shrink, as if it were hiding in a corner. In its place was a warm feeling, like an invisible hug. 🤗
Next, she thought of her older sister, who always knew what to do when Emma got a bump on her head.
—"Come, let me see," she would say, while gently dabbing her forehead with a cool cloth. Her sister's touches were like water on a hot day: fresh and soothing, able to wash away any worry. 💧

Grandpa also appeared in her memory. Emma remembered the day she got upset because they didn't buy her a piece of candy. She was furious, with her arms crossed, when Grandpa stroked her cheek with his warm, wrinkled hand. That gentle touch not only took away her anger but filled her chest with a tenderness so big that she had to smile, even if she didn't want to. 🍬

And then, of course, there were Dad's touches. That time she argued with her best friend, she felt her heart was as heavy as a stone. But Dad sat her down beside him, and as he ran his hand over her shoulders, her heart began to feel lighter, as if it were floating on a soft cloud that rocked everything to sleep. ☁️
However, no gentle touch was like Mom's. 💖
Mom's touches were different, special. They were made of a much more powerful ingredient than anyone else's.

Emma closed her eyes and could feel them again. When Mom stroked her arm, her whole body filled with calm. The weight of her day would disappear, and she felt like she could fly. When she touched her feet or her legs, it was as if all the tension slid off her skin and was lost far away beneath her. 🌬️
When Mom stroked her head, her thoughts stopped racing in circles and turned into soft little lights, dancing like fireflies on a quiet night. 🌟

But the best was when Mom touched her chest. Her hands were so soft and cool that Emma felt as if her whole being were filling with an immense peace, as if a serene lake, full of well-being, was being born inside her body. 🕊️
Emma knew that Mom's gentle touches could heal anything.

So in her lab, surrounded by books and experiments, Emma decided to dedicate her life to understanding the science of a gentle touch. And the more she studied, the more she understood that there was no exact formula, no single answer under a microscope. Gentle touches were magical because they were made of love, of that unique love that important people give us. ❤️

In a cozy little village nestled between high, green mountains, lived a young shepherd named Leo. His job was to watch over the villagers' fluffy flock of sheep. Every morning, he would lead them up a grassy hill where he could see the rooftops of the entire town below. However, Leo often got bored. Watching sheep eat grass all day was very lonely work. 🐑

One sunny afternoon, while the sheep were munching peacefully on clover, a mischievous idea popped into Leo’s head. He stood on his tiptoes, looked down toward the village, and screamed at the top of his lungs:
“Wolf! The Wolf! He’s chasing the sheep! Help!” 🐺

Down in the valley, the villagers froze. Mrs. Miller, the baker, left her bread in the oven. Mr. Steele, the blacksmith, dropped his heavy hammer with a clang, and even Mayor Higgins jumped up from his desk. They all grabbed sticks, brooms, and shovels, racing up the hill as fast as their legs could carry them to save the flock.
But when they arrived, huffing and puffing, there was no wolf. There was only Leo, rolling on the grass and laughing.
“You actually believed there was a wolf!” he giggled, wiping tears of mirth from his eyes. “You should have seen your faces!” 😂
The villagers were not amused. They frowned and dusted off their clothes. “Don't play tricks like that, Leo,” warned Mayor Higgins, wagging a finger. “One day, you’ll be sorry.”
But Leo thought his prank was too funny to stop. A few days later, boredom struck again. He cupped his hands around his mouth and shouted even louder than before:
“Wolf! The Wolf is here! Hurry! Help me!” 🐺
Once again, the kind villagers dropped their work and scrambled up the steep path to help. But when they reached the top, they found Leo clutching his sides, laughing hysterically.
“Tricked you again! It’s so easy to fool you all!” 🤭
This time, the villagers were furious. “That is enough!” scolded Mrs. Miller, her face red from running. “If you keep lying, nobody will believe you when you actually need help.”
Leo just shrugged. He didn't listen. He thought his jokes were harmless fun.

A few days later, the sky turned a gloomy gray, and the forest at the edge of the hill went strangely silent. Suddenly, a massive wolf stepped out from the shadows of the trees. Its eyes glowed yellow, and its sharp teeth glistened. 😨 Leo froze in terror. He scrambled up onto a high rock and screamed with every ounce of breath he had:
“The Wolf! Please, it’s real! The Wolf is attacking! Help me!” 🐺
Down in the village, the people heard the screams. But this time, nobody moved.
“It’s just another one of his tall tales,” grumbled Mrs. Miller, kneading her dough. “Let him shout,” added Mr. Steele. “He needs to learn a lesson.”

Leo yelled and waved his arms, but no one came. The wolf, seeing no one was coming to stop him, chased the flock. By the time the wolf disappeared back into the woods, the sheep were scattered, and many had been snatched away. 🐑🐾
With tears streaming down his face, Leo walked slowly back down to the village to tell everyone what had happened. The villagers listened quietly, their faces serious.
“This is what happens when you lie, Leo,” said Mayor Higgins gently. “Nobody believes a liar, even when he is telling the truth.”
From that day on, Leo never told a lie again. He learned that trust is like a mirror—once it’s broken, it’s very hard to fix. ✨

106.t: Patty the Flea from the Circus
p: 🎪 Once upon a time, there was a tiny flea named Patty, who lived in a very special traveling circus. It wasn't just any circus, but a flea circus that traveled through gardens and meadows on a tiny carriage made from a cookie box. Despite its small size, every night it offered a spectacle full of wonder and magic for the other insects in the area.

The circus traveled inside its wheeled box, which was carefully pulled by Tommy the beetle so as not to hurt his flea artists. That box had small colored lights that lit up in the dark, and tiny flags hung on its roof. It was truly wonderful to see the parade of flea tightrope walkers, flea jugglers, and flea acrobats who made incredibly high jumps, almost touching the stars ✨.

Patty had always dreamed of getting on a trapeze and flying from one end to the other, like the most adventurous fleas. However, there was one detail that made her self-conscious: she considered herself too small, even for a flea. She thought that, with that size, no one would see her when she did her act. She feared that, when she appeared before the audience of ants 🐜, ladybugs 🐞, and cockroaches, she would go so unnoticed that their applause would be for anyone but her.
—I'm not big enough. My jumps won't be noticed in the show,— Patty complained every night while watching her colleagues rehearse.
Her circus friends, the flea tamer of pillbugs and the flea-magician who drew sparks from a dandelion seed, tried to encourage her:
—It's not the size that matters, Patty,— they told her, —but the passion with which you jump.

But Patty remained insecure. Even so, she enjoyed seeing the circus travel every day: in spring they settled under a flowering rose bush; in summer, under a large sunflower; and in autumn, among the fallen leaves of a huge tree. They always found a different and welcoming place to turn into their stage 🌻.

One afternoon, when the sun was beginning to set behind a field of daisies, worrying news arrived: Tommy, the beetle in charge of towing the circus-box, was injured. He wouldn't be able to guide the caravan to the next garden. All the artists gathered worriedly to think about what to do. If they couldn't move, the circus wouldn't arrive in time for its next performance, and the audience of ants and bumblebees wouldn't have a show.

The flea-magician, who always wore a tiny hat full of mysteries 🪄, tried a magical solution: he waved a wand made of a splinter of twig, said some strange words, but nothing happened. The tightrope walkers tried to push the box, but it was too heavy for their thin legs. Even the flea tamer of pillbugs organized her docile pets to drag the carriage, but they barely managed to move it a few inches.

Meanwhile, Patty watched the scene with a heavy heart. How could she help, if she was the smallest of all the fleas? Then, she saw that, very close to the box, a group of ants was transporting breadcrumbs; they marched in single file with great coordination. Patty had an idea: form a team.

She jumped decisively to stand in front of the column of ants 🐜 and told them her story: she told them about the circus, about Tommy the sick beetle, and about the excitement of bringing the show to other insects. The ants consulted each other with their little antennae and decided to help. With their discipline and collective strength, they lined up around the carriage. —One, two! One, two!— they repeated. In a matter of minutes, the wheeled box advanced without problems. The circus was on the move again! 🎉

Everyone celebrated enthusiastically. Under the sunset, the ants continued to push the carriage to the edge of a clearing, where the flea-magician placed his tiny tent. That night, the circus put on its show in honor of the ants who had saved the performance. Patty prepared to go out on the trapeze for the first time. She trembled with nerves, but this time she felt something new: courage. She had discovered her inner strength and understood that no heart is too small to do great things when you have the help of others.

In the middle of the show, the curtain, made of rose petals, opened to reveal Patty standing on the trapeze. The audience was silent. With an energetic impulse, Patty swung and... jumped! She went so high that she seemed to touch the moon. The audience burst into tiny but very sincere applause. The ants raised their antennae to cheer, the ladybugs applauded with their little legs, and the cockroaches played a jar as a drum. No one could believe how that little flea had come so far.

At the end of the show, Patty approached to greet the audience, radiant with joy. She understood that the greatest magic was not in her jump, nor in the colorful lights, but in the power of friendship and collaboration. Thanks to the ants, the circus was able to travel. Thanks to the circus, many little bugs had an unforgettable evening. And thanks to Patty's brave heart, everyone learned that, with self-confidence and with the help of others, you can achieve dreams that seemed impossible.

From then on, every time the flea circus arrived in a new garden, the ants gladly joined in pushing the little carriage. And Patty, with her example, inspired insects big and small to try, to dare, and to share their talents with the world. And happily ever after, the flea circus never stopped traveling. And it always carried with it the greatest magic of all: unity! 🤝✨

Summer was the most anticipated time of the year for the four cousins. Like every year, they returned to their grandfather's house in the countryside, where the days were filled with swims in the lake, walks in the forest, and endless adventures. Twins Carlos and Luis, twelve years old, their cousin Silvia, thirteen, and little Carolina, eleven, were inseparable during those months of freedom. ☀️

Grandfather had clear rules: they had to help in the orchard, take care of the chicken coop, and keep the house in order. But most importantly, what they should never do, was enter the shed. That old wooden structure, covered in cobwebs and with a rickety door, had always given the cousins the creeps. And although they had never felt too curious, something changed that summer.
Every night, they saw Grandfather enter the shed with tools and a flashlight. He stayed there until late at night, and when he came out, he locked it. This sparked the cousins' intrigue.

One morning, Grandfather announced that he had to go to town and would not return until the next day. He left them prepared food and reminded them that, in case of any emergency, they could call him. However, he forbade them from using their cell phones for anything else.
As soon as he left, Carlos noticed something unusual. The shed key was hanging in plain sight on a hook in the kitchen. The cousins looked at each other. It was an invitation impossible to ignore.

With racing hearts, they entered the shed. The air was dense and dusty. Old tools, rusty wheels, and junk covered in cobwebs filled the place. But in the middle of everything, something gleamed: old bicycles, carefully restored. Grandfather had been fixing them up.
—They're for us!—exclaimed Luis with excitement.
—Maybe we should wait for him to give them to us,—suggested Carolina hesitantly.
—But if he's repaired them, it's because he wants us to use them,—replied Silvia.

Determined, they prepared a picnic and set off on the bicycles along the forest path. The fresh air hit their faces as they descended a steep hill. Suddenly, the wind began to swirl strongly around them. Leaves, branches, and papers swirled in a whirlwind that enveloped them. Everything became blurred, and in the blink of an eye, they were no longer in the forest. 🚲💨

Before them stood imposing pyramids under construction. The sound of copper hammers hitting stone echoed in the air. Dozens of men dragged huge blocks under a scorching sun that tinted the sand golden. The air smelled of hot dust and sweat. 🏜️
—Where are we?—whispered Silvia, her eyes wide. 🤔

Carolina shrugged, pursing her lips. It wasn't the best time to be speechless. They crouched behind some rocks to observe better. Then, they noticed someone was watching them. A few feet away, a girl their age scrutinized them with wide eyes and a tense body, ready to run. 🕵️
In the background, a measured voice recited something in a melodic and rhythmic tone. It wasn't exactly a song, but not a conversation either. 🎶
—Who are you?—asked the girl in a faint voice. 👧
She spoke in a different language, but for some reason, the cousins understood her perfectly.
—We are... travelers,—said Carlos, hesitantly.

The girl took a step back distrustfully. A few feet away, she watched them cautiously, trying to decide if they were a threat. —Travelers? From where? I've never seen clothes like yours...—she whispered, without taking her eyes off them. 🌍
—It's complicated to explain,—intervened Silvia, with a reassuring smile.—Don't worry, we don't want to hurt you. 🤝

The girl looked at them suspiciously. For a few seconds, the only sound was that hypnotic chant that continued to envelop the air. Finally, she seemed to relax and, with a shy smile, introduced herself:
—My name is Nefret.

The cousins looked at each other, relieved. Then, Luis, remembering the picnic they had brought, decided to share his food with her. Nefret observed the fruits, sweets, and pastries with fascination before gratefully accepting. 🍏
While they shared lunch, Carlos asked the question that burned on the tip of his tongue:
—Hey, Nefret... what year is it?
She frowned, confused.
—I don't understand your question. We are in the reign of the great Pharaoh Khufu.
Silvia thought for a moment. —"Khufu"?...—Something about that name seemed familiar. And suddenly, she snapped her fingers.
—Of course! We know him as Cheops! We are in the year 2550 B.C.!
Nefret tilted her head, intrigued.
—I've never heard that name before,—she said.—Here everyone calls him Khufu. He is the pharaoh who is building his eternal dwelling.
She pointed to the enormous pyramid under construction, and her eyes shone with excitement. 🏗️

—The pyramids are the pharaoh's house when he leaves this world,—she explained.—His spirit, when it leaves his mortal body, needs a special place for its journey to the afterlife. That's why we leave everything inside that he might need: food, clothes, jewels... even statues, representations of servants to help him in the other life.
Silvia nodded, fascinated.
—And the gods?—asked Carolina suddenly, remembering a book of Egyptian mythology she had at home.—Do they also live in those pyramids?
Nefret giggled. 😄
—Not exactly. The gods are everywhere. In the sky, in the river, in the mountains... but Khufu is special. He is not just a man, he is the living image of Horus, the great falcon god.
Carlos frowned, intrigued.
—Do you mean that Khufu is a god?

—Yes and no,—replied Nefret, tilting her head.—He is not a god like Ra, who shines in the sky, nor like Osiris, who rules the world of the dead. But while he lives, he is the link between the gods and us. He is their voice on Earth.
Silvia frowned.
—And when he dies?
—Then he will join them,—whispered Nefret, solemnly.—He will become Osiris and reign over the afterlife.
The cousins looked at each other, marveling. ✨

From their hiding place, Nefret showed them the impressive activity of the construction. Men with skin bronzed by the sun dragged stones with thick ropes, while the foremen gave orders in a firm voice. Scribes sitting on mats recorded every detail on papyrus: the materials, the number of workers, the progress of the work. Beyond, the artisans carved inscriptions on stone blocks, ensuring that the pharaoh's story was engraved for eternity.
—It's impressive the number of slaves...—whispered Carlos.

—Slaves?—Nefret looked at him strangely.—No! All these men you see here are workers of the pharaoh. We live in nearby villages and work in shifts. Thanks to this work we receive food, clothing, and medical care. It is an honor to help the great Khufu.
Suddenly, a high-pitched sound rose in the air. It was a kind of long and monotonous cry, like the call of a giant bird. The cousins startled. 🦅
—It's just a scribe!—said Nefret, laughing.—He is reciting the accounts of the construction.
—Oh, of course! That explains everything!—said Carlos, rolling his eyes, but still paying attention.
—Without the scribes, no one would know how many stones have been used or how much progress has been made,—added the little girl, understanding the irony in the boy's voice.
Nefret looked at the sky and stood up in a jump.
—I must go. My mother is waiting for me...—she said, but before leaving, she smiled enigmatically.—Sometimes, the stories that our mothers tell us turn out to be true.
Without giving further explanations, she left a small lapis lazuli scarab in Silvia's hands. —So you remember your trip,—she whispered before disappearing running towards the crowd. 🏺

When night fell, the cousins took refuge among some rocks, hugging each other for warmth. The darkness of the desert enveloped them, and the sound of the wind whistling through the dunes made their skin crawl. Tiredness weighed on their bodies, but fear did not let them sleep. What if they were trapped in another time forever? What if no one found them? They heard in the distance the echo of tools hitting stone and the voices of the workers, working even at night. Every shadow that moved around them made them hold their breath.
Carolina snuggled between her siblings and whispered:
—What if we never go home?

No one answered. The silence was more terrifying than any word. Fear and uncertainty invaded them. The sand crunched under their bodies, and the distant sound of the night work on the pyramid kept them alert. They barely managed to sleep. 🌙
The next morning, Carolina woke up with a sudden idea.
—We have to find a hill and go down with the bikes at full speed.

The cousins had no better option. They mounted their bicycles, found a slope, and descended with force. The same whirlwind enveloped them and, suddenly, they were back in the forest, right where they had started.
Without wasting time, they ran back to the house. They left the bicycles in the shed, still covered in dust and mud, and locked themselves in the house just in time.

Shortly before noon, Grandfather returned and the afternoon passed with as much normality as possible, considering that the four cousins were exhausted and still digesting the adventure they had just experienced.

After dinner, Grandfather went to the shed as usual. Seeing the dirty bicycles, he smiled knowingly. He checked the basket of the largest one and took out the small lapis lazuli scarab. Carefully, he opened a hidden box in a corner. Inside, there were other small treasures from different eras: ancient coins, carved stones, badges of forgotten kingdoms, and even other small scarabs.

With a mischievous smile, he put the small amulet with the rest, closed the box, and returned to the house to hang the key back in its place. Who knows, maybe his grandchildren would live many more adventures that summer. 🔑✨

108.t: The Selkie’s Song: A Legend of the Sea
p: On a rugged, windswept island in Scotland, where the cliffs seemed to kiss the sea and the wind danced among the whitecaps, lived a young fisherman named Ewan. Every day, he took his small boat out to navigate the chilly waters in search of fish. Yet, despite the beauty around him, Ewan carried a heaviness in his heart that he couldn't quite explain—a deep, aching nostalgia every time he gazed at the endless blue horizon. 🌊

The village elders often whispered stories by the fire about the Selkies—magical creatures who lived as seals in the ocean. But legend had it that on nights when the moon was full, they would emerge from the waves, shed their seal skins, and dance on the sand in human form. 🌕✨

One night, driven by a curiosity he couldn't control, Ewan hid quietly among the jagged rocks of a secluded cove. The moon hung like a giant pearl in the sky as he watched a group of seals swim to the shore. To his amazement, they began to slip out of their skins, revealing women of otherworldly beauty, with long, flowing hair and eyes as deep and dark as the ocean itself. They danced with grace, laughing with the sea breeze, wild and free under the starlight. 🌊💃

Ewan was captivated by one Selkie in particular. Her hair shimmered with silver highlights, like sea foam catching the light. While she was lost in the rhythm of the dance, Ewan felt a sudden, desperate impulse. He slid silently across the sand and took her seal skin, hiding it quickly beneath a pile of heavy stones.

When the moon began to dip toward the horizon, the Selkies scrambled to find their skins, slipping back into the water one by one. But the young woman with the silver hair could not find hers. Panic filled her eyes. She looked around frantically until she spotted Ewan, who stood watching her, his heart pounding in his chest.
"Where is my skin?" she asked, her voice trembling like a ripple in a pond.
"I cannot give it to you," Ewan whispered, stepping closer. "But I promise, I will take care of you. I will love you with all my soul."

Without her skin, the Selkie could not return to the sea. With no other choice, she followed Ewan back to the village. Over time, she learned the ways of humans. They married, and she grew to care for him. Eventually, they had a son named Finn, a boy with dark hair and eyes that sparkled like the ocean depths. But despite the passing years and the love she held for her family, the Selkie never stopped looking at the sea with a quiet, heartbreaking sadness. 🌊💔

One afternoon, while Finn was playing on the beach, he found something strange tucked deep inside a crevice in the rocks. It was a bundle of fur—soft, pearly, and smelling of salt and memories. He ran home, carrying the bundle to his mother, unaware that he held the key to her freedom in his small hands. 🔑🌊

The Selkie trembled as she touched it. A rush of memories flooded back: the cold embrace of the currents, the rolling waves, and the secret songs of the ocean creatures. With tears streaming down her face, she knelt and pulled Finn into a tight hug.
"Never forget, my sweet boy," she whispered, "that the sea is a home that always calls its own."

That night, when the moon rose high, the seal woman walked down to the water’s edge. She cast one last, loving look toward the village where her son slept, then wrapped herself in her skin and slipped into the waves. 🌕🌊

Since that day, the local fishermen say that on nights of the full moon, a magnificent seal swims close to the shore. She sings sweet, haunting melodies to the boy who remained on land, so he will never forget that his mother loves him, always and forever, from the deep blue sea. 🎶💙

Among the branches of a slender birch tree, in a sun-drenched forest, lived a tiny Seed growing in a cluster with its siblings. They all dreamed of taking root, growing strong, and becoming majestic trees. But not this one. Our little Seed didn't feel ready to stay in one place. Its tiny plant heart beat with longing to see the world, to travel and discover everything around it. But, at the same time, it was filled with anxiety at the thought of being trapped by its roots. 🌱

So one day, a mischievous breeze blew strongly, and without thinking twice, the Seed let go and drifted away. It floated in the air until it landed on the back of a fluffy Bunny. Snuggled in its soft fur, it traveled across meadows and forests, hopping from one place to another. "This is wonderful!" it thought as the Bunny bounced through the bushes. It felt like a rider in a great race, dodging branches and leaves, seeing everything from above. But when the animal decided to give itself a good shake, the Seed shot off like a shooting star, spinning in the air before landing and rolling uncontrollably through the grass. It bounced between pebbles, jumped over a root, and, after one last leap, fell with a light splash into a stream. 🌬️

The water embraced it with softness and coolness, and the Seed floated, letting itself be carried by the current. It saw silvery fish swim beside it, hid among seaweed that danced with the movement of the water, and traveled under the shade of willow trees. At one point, a curious fish tried to gulp it down, but the Seed, with an agile jump propelled by a bubble of water, managed to escape. Filled with adrenaline, it felt like an intrepid explorer in search of new worlds, invincible, ready to continue living adventures. However, the stream carried it to the shore, slowing its progress, and the little Seed was saddened to sense that its journey was ending. 💧

Luckily, a Girl was playing in the mud with her bare feet nearby. Without the little one noticing, the Seed slid and stuck to her little foot. When the Girl went to put on her shoe, it detached in time inside the shoe, managing to go unnoticed and enjoy an interesting car ride. 🚗
When they arrived at the house, it activated again when it felt the Girl taking off her shoes.
—Wow! A little plant got stuck to me —exclaimed the Girl, shaking her sneaker and causing the Seed to fall on the floor of the entrance. 😮

The family’s Cat, who was watching everything attentively, pounced to play with the tiny Seed. First, it pushed it with one of its paws, making it slide gently across the floor. Then, with a more energetic tap, it launched it into the air and caught it in impossible spins. Overcome with emotion, the Seed felt like it was on a roller coaster of movements until, in a final display of energy and flexibility, the Cat tried an impossible jump, causing the Seed to slip off the balcony. 🐱

The Seed, after several turns in the air, landed on the windowsill of an open window of another nearby building. A Pigeon perched there looked at it with interest, tilting its head curiously, as if deciding whether to peck it or not. The Seed held its breath for a moment. But, just as the tension grew, a new unexpected breeze pushed it strongly and, with a jump, it once again soared through the skies, spinning uncontrollably in the air before regaining its balance and taking advantage of the air currents to float. From above, it saw the town pass by, hills, rivers, more houses and forests, and for the first time it felt too small for such a big world. 🌍

The Seed felt something different inside. It liked its adventurous life, but now it also wanted to find a place to call home. It looked around and saw a clearing in the forest, with spongy soil bathed in sunlight. "Here I could take root," it thought. 🏡

It descended gently and, for the first time, felt the warmth of the earth embracing it. It settled down calmly, letting the moisture envelop it. Now it understood that it wasn't giving up its adventures, but rather starting a new one. Sinking its roots, the Seed knew that, from there, it could see the world in a different way: growing towards the sky, observing the sway of the wind, and waiting for the day when its own seeds would begin new journeys. 🌳
And so, the adventurous Seed became a strong and majestic tree, with many stories to tell. 🌟

For several weeks now, a nickname echoed through the school hallways, unquestioned by anyone: the flea-bitten girl. No one remembered exactly who started the rumor, but everyone repeated it. It was said that she didn't bathe, that she smelled bad, that if you got too close, you might catch something. The truth was, everyone knew it was a lie, but the game had become a shared truth. And the worst part was that the girl herself had stopped defending herself.

Emily had always been one of those who watched from the sidelines. She didn't make fun, but she didn't say anything either. Sometimes, she would laugh out of obligation when her friends commented on something, and when the flea-bitten girl passed through the hallway, she avoided making eye contact so as not to attract attention. Even so, she began to feel something in her stomach every time she saw her hunched over in her desk. It wasn't fear or shame. It was discomfort. Something wasn't right.

One morning, Emily entered the classroom right behind her. She saw her lower her head and clutch her books against her chest. Something in her posture made her feel a pang of guilt. Without thinking, Emily blurted out a simple: “Hello.”
The girl looked up, surprised. Her eyes showed bewilderment, as if she expected it to be a joke. Finally, she mumbled a soft “Hello” before sitting down at her desk.
Emily felt eyes on her. Her friends whispered behind her back.
—But how can you talk to her? She doesn't shower—one of them said, in a tone half-joking, half-serious.
For the first time, Emily didn't respond with a timid laugh or a shrug. Seriously, but in a low voice so that not too many people heard her, she replied:
—That's not true, and you know it.
Her friend blinked, surprised by her response. She didn't insist, but the comment was already floating in the air.
That night, at dinner, Emily couldn't help but tell the story.
—There's a girl in my class they call the flea-bitten girl. No one goes near her, and they say mean things about her all the time.
Her mother frowned. Her father put his silverware down on his plate.
—And you?—he asked.
Emily shifted in her seat.
—I... nothing. I don't mess with her.
—And do you do anything to defend her?—he insisted.
Emily knew that her father was right to ask her that question, but it still seemed somewhat unfair.
—No, Dad. I'd like to help, but I'm afraid they'll mess with me too...
Her mother sighed and gave her some advice:

—If you really want to help, you can do two things. First, don't laugh at other people's "jokes." Second, invite her to your house. If you're worried about being picked on for hanging out with her, you can always give her your support that way. Sometimes, the most effective way to change things is to act without speeches.

Emily thought about it all night. If she talked to her, would they laugh at her too? Would they call her flea-bitten too? Was it really worth risking it for someone she had never treated? Despite all the doubts, the next morning, when she entered the classroom and saw her alone at her desk, she made up her mind.
—Do you want to come to my house this afternoon? We can do homework together and then play for a while.
The girl looked at her skeptically.
—Of course—Emily smiled.
When her friends saw her with the flea-bitten girl, there were looks and whispers. Emily got nervous, but she didn't let that stop her.

The afternoon was surprisingly normal. She discovered that the girl had a contagious laugh, that she liked the same music as her, and that she was good at math. She was, in short, exactly like any of them. Then, Emily understood something: the bullying could have been against anyone. If it had happened to her today, it could have happened to Emily or any of her friends tomorrow.

The next day, Emily greeted the girl again as she entered the classroom. And then, during recess, she dedicated herself to chatting and walking around the patio with her. And the next day, she acted the same. And the next. Emily had decided that she preferred that they stop talking to her too than to participate for one more minute in that unjustified harassment.

Little by little, something began to change. Some of Emily's closest friends also began, naturally, to get together and chat animatedly with them. The invisible barrier that had turned the girl into an outcast began to crumble, and for the first time in a long time, she felt seen. Her smile, at first timid, became more luminous, daring to intervene more and feeling integrated again as the days passed.
Until one day, someone in the class mentioned the nickname again: flea-bitten girl. But this time, another voice answered without hesitation:
—Come on, nobody believes that. Just drop it.
The silence was immediate. The rumor had lost its strength.
The laughter with that joke had died down. No one wanted to be the only person left on the side of those who did harm for no reason.

And, without the need for confrontations or heroic speeches, the flea-bitten girl ceased to be so. She went back to being simply Carla, a normal, ordinary girl, with her tastes, her dreams, and her stories. And, most importantly, she was no longer alone. 😊

A huge storm was brewing over Aprisco Farm. The weather service had warned of heavy rain and a risk of flash floods in the mountains. The caretakers worked quickly, securing shelters, reinforcing fences, and guiding the animals to safe areas.
The wind howled through the trees, shaking the branches with growing force. The first drops hit the ground like tiny, icy darts, turning the earth into a muddy mess in minutes.
Carola, like most of the adult goats at the sanctuary, had been born on the farm. Although she had seen other storms, none had ever felt as threatening as this one.

Two caretakers fought against the rain to close the pen where the goats were sheltering. Mud piled up at the base of the fence, making it hard for them to lock it completely. A gust of wind made them stumble, but they managed to secure the latch almost all the way and ran for cover just as a bolt of lightning lit up the sky.

The thunder rumbled like a roar in the mountains, shaking the entire farm. In the pen, the goats jumped, huddling together under the roof. The smallest ones hid between the legs of the older goats, who chewed their hay with a tense calmness.

Then, the flash of another lightning bolt tore across the sky. Almost at the same time, a deafening thunderclap exploded above them. In the chaos, three terrified little goat kids bolted and squeezed through the small gap left in the fence.
Without a second thought, Carola dashed after them. ✨

The mud came up to her knees. Every step was a battle against the slippery ground, but she couldn't stop. The kids were running wildly, driven by panic. The rain fell brutally, darkening the air and muffling all sounds.
Carola bleated with all her might. Her voice cut through the storm.
A faint bleat answered from far away, at the edge of the forest.
Following the sound, she found two of the kids huddled under a thorny bush. They were trembling, soaked, and scared. Carola sniffed them firmly, making sure they were okay, but one was still missing.
She called out again. Nothing.
The forest wasn't safe. The wind was tearing off branches, and the ground was giving way to small torrents of muddy water.
Then, she heard it.
It was a desperate bleat, farther away, higher up.

Carola lifted her head and saw her: the third goat kid was trapped on a rock, surrounded by a furious current of water. The creek had overflowed, and its channel was now a raging flood that grew with every minute.
The little one cried out, terrified.
Carola got as close as she could. The water lapped at her legs, but she stood firm and called to the kid insistently.
—Come on— she seemed to say. —Trust me.
The little kid hesitated. She clung to the rock with her fragile hooves.
The water was rising.
Carola tensed her muscles and leaned forward, calling with urgency.
With her heart pounding, the little one closed her eyes and leaped into the air.
Carola met her with a precise nudge, guiding her safely to solid ground. The kid shook, trembling, and ran to hide under her body.
The storm still roared. They couldn't return to the farm in these conditions.

Carola looked around and found a solid, sturdy stone wall. She led the three kids there, tucking them between the rock and her own body. The rain fell relentlessly, but she remained motionless, protecting them, keeping them warm, and gently nibbling their little heads whenever thunder rumbled in the sky.
After a while, the storm began to calm down.
The rain softened to a murmur, the wind died down, and the thunder moved farther away.
Carola was exhausted, soaked, and her body was numb from the effort. But the little kids were safe.
As she tried to figure out the way back, a familiar sound filled her with relief.
The dogs. 🐕

Back at the farm, the caretakers had noticed that some animals were missing from the pen and had released the mastiffs. Turco, the oldest and wisest, led the search. His nose was to the ground, though the rain made it hard to follow any scent. With his steady paws against the mud, he guided the others with deep barks.
Carola heard him and bleated loudly.
Turco lifted his head and headed straight for them, with the determination of someone who has found what they were looking for.
When he reached them, he sniffed the little kids and nudged Carola with his snout, with the gentle roughness of an old guardian.
—Let's go home— Turco seemed to say with his big, bright eyes.
Carola followed him, tired but proud.
When they arrived at the farm, the other animals greeted them with a chorus of sounds: bleats, neighs, squawks, and howls.
The caretakers also ran toward them, checking them over, drying them with blankets, and hugging them with relief.
But the biggest cheer came from the animals themselves.
That day, Carola became the hero of the farm. 🎉

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jack who lived with his mother in a small country cottage. They were very poor and only had a dairy cow, which they depended on for their livelihood. One day, the cow stopped giving milk, and Jack's mother, in despair, asked him to take her to the market and sell her to get some money. 🐄

On the way to the market, Jack met an old man who offered him a handful of magic beans in exchange for the cow. 🌱 The old man assured him that these beans were not ordinary and that, if he planted them, they would grow right up to the sky. Jack, intrigued by the promise, accepted the deal and returned home with the beans instead of money.

When his mother saw what he had done, she was so angry that she threw the beans out the window and sent Jack to bed without supper. 😠 During the night, the beans began to grow without stopping, forming an enormous beanstalk that reached up beyond the clouds. 🌿☁️

The next morning, Jack woke up and saw the gigantic plant climbing into the sky. Full of curiosity, he decided to climb it. He climbed and climbed until he reached a strange land, where a massive castle stood. 🏰 Jack approached cautiously, and when he knocked on the door, a gigantic woman greeted him.
"Go away before my husband finds you," the Giantess warned him. "He is an ogre who devours children." 😨

But Jack was hungry and begged her to give him something to eat. The Giantess, taking pity on him, offered him some bread and milk. Just at that moment, the ground began to shake, and a thunderous voice echoed through the castle.
"Fee, fi, fo, fum! I smell the blood of an Englishman! Alive or dead, I'll catch him and eat him!" 🦴

It was the Ogre, who had returned home. His wife quickly hid Jack in a corner and convinced her husband that he only smelled the leftovers of his meal. The Ogre sat at the table, devoured a great feast, and then pulled out a bag of gold coins. 💰 He counted them over and over until, finally, he fell asleep.

Jack, taking advantage of the opportunity, came out of his hiding place, took the bag of gold, and ran as fast as he could to the beanstalk. He climbed down carefully and, upon reaching home, showed the gold to his mother. Thanks to this, they were able to live well for a time. 💰✨

But fortune does not last forever, and soon they found themselves in poverty once again. Jack decided to climb the beanstalk one more time and return to the castle. This time, the Ogre's wife did not want to let him in, but Jack convinced her and hid again when the Ogre arrived.
"Fee, fi, fo, fum! I smell the blood of an Englishman!" 😡
After eating, the Ogre brought out a hen and ordered:
"Lay a golden egg!" 🥚✨
When the Ogre fell asleep, Jack took the hen and ran toward the beanstalk. His mother was amazed. With the magic hen, they never went hungry again. 🐔💛

But Jack was still curious about what else he might find in the Ogre's castle. For a third time, he climbed the beanstalk. That night, after his meal, the Ogre brought out a golden harp and ordered it:
The harp began to play an enchanting melody all on its own. But when Jack grabbed it, the harp cried out:
"Master, master, I am being stolen!" 🔊
The Ogre woke up immediately and saw Jack escaping with the harp. Furious, he got up and chased after him. Jack hurried down the beanstalk as fast as he could.
"Mother, bring me an axe!" 🪓
His mother brought him the axe, and Jack, with all his might, chopped the beanstalk. The plant creaked, shook, and finally collapsed, causing the Ogre to fall from high above and die. ☠️
From then on, Jack and his mother lived happily, without a care in the world, thanks to the hen that laid the golden eggs and the magic harp. 🎶✨

Mikey was a curious boy who loved to play, run super fast, and draw, but when something didn't go his way, he would erupt in a fit of anger and get so mad that he couldn't do anything for a long time.

One day at school, Miss Sarah asked them to draw a castle with many towers. Mikey tried, but the lines came out crooked. He tried again, and nothing! He felt himself getting angry, and without meaning to, he pressed harder and harder on the pencil, until snap! the tip broke and tore the paper a little.
He felt his chest tighten and his cheeks turn red. He slammed his hand on the table and threw the pencil.
—Stupid castle!—he shouted, crossing his arms.
At that moment, his friend Lily, who was sitting next to him, raised her hand and exclaimed:
—Teacher! Mikey looks like a volcano!
Miss Sarah smiled and walked to the center of the classroom.

—Good observation, Lily! In fact, we all have a volcano inside—she said—. And when we get frustrated, we feel it start to heat up and bubble. If we don't do anything, BOOM!, it explodes. Has anyone ever felt like that?
Several children nodded.
—And what can we do to keep our volcano from exploding?—the teacher asked.
She paused and then said:
—I'm going to teach you three tricks to cool down your volcano. We're all going to try them together.
—First, let's practice the volcano breath: imagine you have a candle in your hand. Now we're going to blow very slowly, without putting out the flame—explained the teacher.
Everyone took a breath and blew gently.
—Very good! When we breathe like this, we help our volcano release some of its lava, but without exploding.
Mikey felt his anger going down with each soft breath.
—Now, let's try to put the volcano to sleep: squeeze your hands tightly, as if you were full of lava… and now relax them little by little to let it out without exploding!
The children closed their fists tightly and then relaxed them.
—Do you notice how your body loosens up? This helps release the tension.
Mikey no longer felt so angry. With these tricks, he had managed to release some of that feeling and felt ready to listen to the last step that Miss Sarah proposed.
—When something doesn't work out for us, instead of giving up, we can think: “Can I try another way?” or “Can I ask for help?”
Mikey, who had been listening attentively, raised his hand.
—Teacher… I think I want to try again, but this time I'll just do one tower first.
The teacher smiled.
—That's a great idea, Mikey! You've found another way to do it.

Mikey got up from his desk, picked up the pencil (which he had to sharpen again), and began to draw a single tower. When he finished it, he made another, and then another. In the end, his castle had four straight towers and one a little crooked.
—I did it!—he exclaimed excitedly.
Lily looked at his drawing and smiled.
—And besides, that crooked tower makes your castle special.
Mikey also smiled.
From that day on, every time he felt his volcano wanted to explode, he remembered Miss Sarah's tricks:
🔥 Breathe as if blowing out a candle. 🔥 Squeeze and release your hands to release the lava. 🔥 Think of another way to do it.
Because all volcanoes can roar, but they can also learn to release their lava little by little. 🌋

114.t: The Star That Rocked on the Sea
p: High in the night sky, with the last rays of sunlight, a star ✨ awoke.

At first, its light was barely a soft glow, a faint shimmer that pulsed within, like the echo of a dream just left behind. It stretched slowly, feeling the light reborn once more in its chest, warm and vibrant, and spreading throughout its body. First, it reached its arms, then down its legs, until clarity filled it completely, swirling under its skin.
It was ready to shine.

From up there, the world slept under a dark blanket. The mountains rose majestically, covered by a thin mist that floated over the valleys like a river of clouds. Everything was calm. Only the wind whispered among the leaves of the trees, rocking the branches slowly, as if they too were about to fall asleep.
Stella saw her sisters awaken little by little, illuminating the firmament with their beauty.
