With the silent turn of the Earth, its light began to slide over the landscape. First, it caressed the top of the mountains, tingeing the rocks and the tallest trunks with silver reflections. Then, it descended gently to the valleys, where a river snaked between the fields.
Stella decided to follow the course of the water.

From up there, the river looked like a silver ribbon shining in the darkness. Its waters reflected the moon 🌕 with small sparkles that danced on the current. As she passed, Stella saw how the leaves of the nearest trees trembled with the night breeze, whispering invisible stories to anyone who knew how to listen.

The clouds passed from time to time around it. They were so light, so soft, that touching them tickled it. Stella laughed silently as they floated beside her, leaving behind a trail of fine, cold mist.

A little further on, Stella felt a soft warmth on her skin. She looked to the side and there was the moon, suspended in the sky, watching everything with its whitish light. Stella knew that this glow was a gift from the sun, which was still sleeping on the other side of the world.
The air became denser, more humid. It smelled of salt.
Then, Stella saw it:
Dark and deep, it stretched as far as the eye could see. Its surface moved slowly, in a constant sway, as if it too were breathing. Stella leaned in a little and saw her own reflection on the water.
The waves distorted it, lengthened it and shrunk it, as if its light also floated with the tide.
And there, looking at herself in the infinite ocean, she let herself rock.
The movement of the water enveloped her in a serene calm. She swayed gently, without haste, without worries. It was like being in a cradle made of light.
On the horizon, behind the mountains, an orange glow began to appear.
The sun was waking up. 🌞
Stella knew it was time to rest again.

She let her light slowly return to her interior, closing her eyes with the tranquility of someone who has finished a long journey. The waves continued to cradle her with their eternal song, enveloping her in the stillness of dawn.
And so, with the rocking of the sea, Stella fell sweetly asleep.

Lily was in the park, pushing her toy truck through the damp sand, when something tiny caught her eye among the fallen leaves. She bent down and saw some very small shoes, the size of her dolls' shoes. What was most striking, besides the fact that they were beautiful, was that they had all the details to look like real shoes. Whoever had made them had created incredible shoes. 👀

She looked around, hoping to find who they might belong to, but she didn't see anyone. Had they fallen off a child? Were they from a forgotten doll? She carefully picked them up and put them in her jacket pocket and continued playing until she was called home.

Back in her room, while arranging her dolls on their toy bed, she remembered the little shoes. "They'll be perfect for them," she thought. She picked up the doll with the yellow dress and put the tiny shoes on its stiff plastic feet.

—Ouch!—a stifled cry escaped when the doll suddenly changed color. Her whole body turned a deep purple. Lily dropped her in shock, and as soon as the shoes came off her feet, the doll returned to her original color.

Lily's heart was beating fast, but curiosity was stronger. She picked up the doll and put the shoes back on. Ploof! Purple again. She tried with another doll, this time the one with braids, and as soon as she adjusted the shoes, the doll began to move on her own, taking small, clumsy hops across the table as if trying to dance. 💃

Lily spent the whole afternoon experimenting with her dolls. Some changed color, others moved their arms or legs, and one even started floating around the room. That night she fell asleep thinking about the shoes and the wonders they caused.

The next day, at the park, she stared at the place where she had found them. Then she saw something that left her speechless: a little person as small as one of her dolls was walking among the leaves. She had tangled hair and bare feet, with very dirty socks. 🧚‍♀️
—Hello!—greeted the tiny figure—I'm looking for some little shoes. I left them here yesterday and they've disappeared. Haven't you seen them?

Lily felt a pang in her stomach. She knew they were her shoes, but the idea of giving them back was difficult. She had played with them so much... they were magical. If she returned them, would her dolls go back to being normal?
—No, I haven't seen them—she said softly.
The fairy sighed.

—The same thing always happens to me. I took them off so I wouldn't get them dirty when I went to help some ants trapped in a puddle, and when I came back, they were gone. I don't want to ask for new ones because I always get scolded for losing my things...—she looked at her dirty feet and wrinkled her nose—And my feet already hurt from walking without them.

Lily felt even worse. That afternoon she tried to play with the dolls, but she couldn't. Something inside her stirred every time she looked at the shoes. She thought about the fairy and her bare feet, how sad she looked.

The next day, she returned to the park intending to return them. She searched everywhere, but the fairy wasn't there. So she left a folded note on the leaf where she had found them: "I have your shoes. I live in the house with pink curtains above the flower shop on the corner."

That afternoon, Lily didn't even want to touch the dolls. She was lying on her bed when, suddenly, a knock on the window made her jump. She turned and saw the fairy floating outside, with her arms crossed and a frown on her face.
—It was you!—exclaimed the fairy—I've been walking barefoot all this time!—she raised a foot and showed her her torn socks.
Lily lowered her head.
—I'm sorry—she said, offering her the shoes—I liked them a lot... but they were yours.
The fairy stared at her, then sighed and took the shoes. She put them on and took a little spin in the air, smiling again. ✨
—Well, at least you returned them. And I know you liked them... so I'll play with you for a while. But this time, with my magic.

Lily opened her eyes with surprise and excitement when the dolls began to move again, but this time in even more incredible ways. Some floated, others did impossible pirouettes. The whole room filled with magic. ✨🧚‍♀️

The fairy laughed with joy as she snapped her fingers, making small flashes of light dance around Lily. Her dolls were no longer simple toys: they seemed to come to life completely, as if they were part of a great show. Lily spun around, trying to follow the whirlwind of lights and colors that unfolded around her. For a moment, she felt like she was inside a fairy tale.
When the magic began to fade little by little, the fairy landed gently on her pillow and looked at her with a mischievous smile.
—You don't need magic shoes to make things special—she said—Sometimes, the real magic is in sharing.

Lily nodded, understanding that the moment they had just experienced had been much more magical than any spell. From that day on, Lily and the fairy became friends and shared many afternoons of games. And Lily learned that, although it is sometimes difficult, doing the right thing always brings good things. 💖

Once upon a time, a beautiful young girl lived with her stepmother and two stepsisters. Her father had been widowed when she was very little, and since he had to travel often for work, he thought it would be best to marry a woman who seemed suitable, especially since she had two daughters around the same age as his own little girl.
Envious of her stepdaughter's beauty and kindness, the wicked woman always looked for ways to put her own daughters first and treat the sweet girl unfairly.

Together, the three of them forced her to do all the household chores—cooking, cleaning, and doing the laundry. Despite her difficult life, the young girl never lost her smile or her gentle heart. While her stepsisters dressed up in luxurious gowns, she dreamed of better days.

One evening, exhausted from all her hard work, the girl fell asleep near the fireplace. When she woke up with her face smudged with cinders and ash, her stepsisters laughed endlessly. From that day on, they mockingly called her Cinderella. Yet, even in her worn-out rags and with soot on her cheeks, she was still a hundred times prettier than they would ever be.

One day, grand news arrived: the king was hosting a magnificent royal ball at the palace to celebrate the prince's birthday, and every young maiden in the kingdom was invited! Cinderella was thrilled and daydreamed right alongside her stepsisters, helping them pick out their dresses and style their hair. But when the day of the grand party finally arrived, her stepmother sneered:
"Cinderella, you are not going. You will stay right here, scrub the floors, and have dinner ready for when we return."

The three women departed for the palace, laughing cruelly as they left. Cinderella ran out to the garden, sank onto a bench, and began to cry. She wished with all her heart that she could go to the ball. Suddenly, her Fairy Godmother appeared in a shimmer of light and asked gently:
"You would love to go to the ball, wouldn't you, my dear?"
"Oh, yes!" Cinderella sighed.
"Well then, dry your tears!" said her Fairy Godmother. "I will make sure you go. Run to the vegetable patch and bring me a pumpkin."
Cinderella immediately went to pick the finest pumpkin she could find and brought it to her Fairy Godmother, though she couldn't guess how a pumpkin would help her get to the royal ball.
Her Fairy Godmother tapped it with her magic wand, and POOF! Instantly, it transformed into a beautiful, gleaming golden carriage.

Next, she peeked inside the mousetrap and found six live mice. She told Cinderella to lift the trapdoor just a little bit, and as each mouse scampered out, she gave it a tap with her wand. Zap! Zap! Zap! They transformed into six spirited horses of a lovely dapple-gray color.

Then, the Fairy Godmother spotted a larger mouse with magnificent whiskers. With a quick tap of her wand, he became a handsome, sturdy coachman. Finally, she asked Cinderella to fetch six lizards from the garden. With a final flick of the wrist, they were turned into footmen in crisp green uniforms, who immediately hopped onto the back of the carriage as if they had been doing it their whole lives.
The Fairy Godmother smiled and asked:
"Well, here is your ride to the ball! Are you feeling happier now?"
"Yes, but... what about my clothes? I can't go looking like this."

The Fairy Godmother just smiled and tapped Cinderella with her wand. Instantly, her ragged clothes transformed into a magnificent gown woven from gold and silver threads, glittering with precious jewels. To top it all off, she gave her a pair of glass slippers—the most delicate and beautiful shoes in the entire world.
"Now you are ready for the ball," the Fairy Godmother warned gently. "But remember, you must return before the stroke of midnight. When the clock strikes twelve, the magic will fade."

Cinderella promised to watch the time and set off excitedly for the castle. Upon her arrival, her beauty and grace dazzled everyone in the ballroom. Her stepsisters didn't recognize her at all, and the Prince, the moment he saw her, couldn't take his eyes away. He asked her to dance, and they spent the entire evening waltzing together. Cinderella was having so much fun that she completely lost track of time.

Suddenly, the grand clock began to chime. BONG... BONG... It was almost midnight! Panicking, Cinderella dashed out of the palace without a word of explanation. In her frantic rush, one of her glass slippers slipped off on the grand staircase. Just as the twelfth chime echoed through the night air, her glamorous gown turned back into rags, and her golden carriage became a simple pumpkin once more.

When she arrived home, she realized that the Fairy Godmother had let her keep the other glass slipper as a memory of that magical night. As she gazed at it, her stepsisters burst through the door, bubbling with excitement. Clueless to her secret, they babbled on and on about the dazzling mystery princess who had stolen the Prince's heart.

The very next day, the Royal Emissary traveled throughout the kingdom, searching for the owner of the lost glass shoe. First, they tried it on all the noble ladies, but when it didn't fit anyone, they decided to have every young maiden in the land try it on. When they finally reached Cinderella's house, her stepmother tried to stop her from stepping forward, arguing she was just a lowly maid. But the Royal Emissary, seeing her standing there, insisted she be given a fair chance.

Cinderella slipped her foot into the delicate glass shoe, and it was a perfect fit! At that exact moment, the Fairy Godmother appeared once more. With a brilliant flash of light, she restored Cinderella's breathtaking ballgown.

The Royal Emissary escorted her straight back to the palace. The moment the Prince saw her, he knew she was the lovely girl he had danced with. A magnificent royal wedding was planned. True to her gentle heart, Cinderella forgave her stepsisters and wished them nothing but the best.

Cinderella lived happily ever after with the Prince, surrounded by people who truly loved her. Even though her life had changed forever, she never forgot who she was or the lessons she had learned. And every night, when she looked up at the starry sky, she fondly remembered her Fairy Godmother, who, with a little bit of magic and a whole lot of hope, had helped her find her true destiny.
Arthur was walking home from school with his mom when, as they turned their usual corner, he saw something new: an antique shop that had never been there before. His mom stopped, surprised.
—What a pretty window display! —she exclaimed—. Let's take a look.

As soon as they crossed the threshold, Arthur felt like they had entered another world. The shop was enormous, much bigger than it looked from the outside, with shelves overflowing with curious objects, like antique mirrors, figures and dolls of all kinds of materials and sizes, lamps of countless shapes and colors, and clocks from all eras ticking at different rhythms.

He wandered away from his mom without realizing it, fascinated by everything he saw. In one of the aisles, among all the objects, one in particular caught his eye: a pocket watch with a golden chain. It was placed on a red velvet cushion and seemed to change color slightly depending on the angle from which he looked at it.
When he picked it up in his hands, he felt a kind of electricity run through his skin.
—That is a very special clock —said a voice behind him.
Arthur turned around and saw a picturesque-looking man. He was wearing a blue velvet vest, round glasses, and an enigmatic smile.
—It's a wishing clock —he added.
Arthur's eyes widened.
—How does it work? —he asked, as all sorts of wishes crowded into his head. 🎩✨
—First of all, it's important to know the rules of any magical object —With an elegant movement, the man made a parchment appear in his hand and unrolled it, showing the contents to the little boy.
—Read carefully —he said, pointing with his finger to a list that appeared little by little.
Arthur read aloud:
—"The Altruistic Wishing Clock"
Arthur's eyes widened.
—That's incredible! How much does it cost?
The man smiled kindly and handed him the clock.
—I'll lend it to you. But remember: wishes are powerful. Use them well.

That night, Arthur stayed in his room looking at the clock. He wondered what wish he could make that wasn't selfish. He decided to try it out. He thought of his neighbor, Mr. Johnson, an old man who always sat on a park bench, but lately he seemed sad. Arthur remembered that his mom had said that his dog, Buster, had been lost a few days ago. 🕰️✨
With the clock in his hand, Arthur closed his eyes and said in a low voice:
—I wish Mr. Johnson would find his dog Buster.
The clock vibrated slightly, and for an instant, its hands spun on their own.
The next day, when Arthur passed through the park on his way to school, he saw Mr. Johnson with Buster in his arms, smiling.
Arthur felt a tingle of excitement. The clock worked! ✨
After a long day of school and extracurricular activities, Arthur still had homework to do. He looked at the notebooks with boredom and, with a sigh, took the clock in his hands, muttering:
—I wish there was no school tomorrow.

The clock vibrated and its hands spun. The next morning, the sky dawned dark and the wind roared against the windows. The rain fell non-stop and the streets were completely flooded. A tremendous storm had flooded the city and there was no school, but there was also no electricity or internet. Arthur spent the day bored, unable to play with his friends or leave the house.
—This can't be! —he lamented—. I wish I hadn't wished for that.
That same night, repentant, Arthur thought of someone who really needed help. He remembered his neighbor, Mrs. Davis, who had trouble carrying grocery bags up the stairs.
He took the clock and whispered:
—I wish Mrs. Davis would receive help with her bags when she needs it.
The next day, when Arthur went outside, he saw how his older brother, without being asked, helped Mrs. Davis carry the bags with a smile.

Arthur then understood that a wish was not just a magical whim, but an opportunity to make the world a little better. If he used the clock with intelligence and generosity, he could make a difference in the lives of those around him.

The days passed, and one afternoon, when Arthur was returning from school, he noticed something strange as he turned the usual corner: the antique shop had disappeared as if it had never existed. He reached into his pocket and realized that the clock was no longer there. Instead, he found a small velvet case. With his heart beating fast, he opened it.
Inside was a golden medal with the inscription: "You have used your time well". Next to it, a small folded piece of paper. He unfolded it carefully and read the words written in elegant calligraphy:
The time for wishes is over, but the power to do good remains in you. Continue helping others without the need for magic. Thank you for using the clock wisely.
Arthur smiled. He knew that the clock had disappeared, but its lesson would remain with him forever. ✨

In the heart of London, when the sun sets and the house lights flicker out, the stars keep watch over the dreams of children. In one such house lived Wendy, John, and Michael Darling, three siblings who absolutely adored bedtime stories. They were especially fascinated by tales of Peter Pan, the boy who refused to grow up and lived on a magical island called Neverland. 🌟
What the Darling siblings didn’t know was that Peter Pan wasn’t just a character in a book. He was real.

The first time Mrs. Darling learned of Peter was one night while tidying the nursery. As she leaned in to kiss her children goodnight, she noticed leaves scattered across the floor. "How strange," she thought, for those leaves didn’t belong to any tree in their neighborhood. Then, looking closer, she discovered something even more unsettling: she found a shadow, folded up as if someone had dropped it like a handkerchief.
Confused, she tucked it into a drawer, unaware that she had just locked away a piece of the dream world. ✨

That very night, Peter Pan returned for his shadow. He flew right through the open window, his hair messy and a mischievous grin on his face. Fluttering beside him was a tiny ball of golden light: Tinker Bell, his inseparable fairy friend, who left a trail of shimmering pixie dust wherever she went.

Peter rummaged through the drawers until he found what he was looking for. But when he tried to stick the shadow back on, he realized he didn’t know how. He pulled at it, stomped on it, and tried to hold it in place… but nothing worked. Frustrated, he flopped onto the floor and began to sob.
That was when Wendy woke up.
"Why are you crying?" she asked, surprised to see a strange boy in her room.
"Because my shadow won’t stick!" Peter exclaimed with frustration.
Wendy, kind and curious by nature, wasn’t scared. Instead, she grabbed a needle and thread and, with great patience, sewed the shadow back onto Peter’s shoes. When she finished, he jumped for joy.
"Look how perfectly it fits!" he said, strutting around the room.
Wendy giggled. There was something fascinating about this boy with the defiant smile and eyes full of adventure.
"Who are you?"
"I am Peter Pan."
"The one from the stories?"
"The stories they tell you, yes. I come every night to listen to them."
Wendy’s eyes went wide. Peter Pan was real!
"And where do you come from?"
"From Neverland, an island where children never grow up. I live there with the Lost Boys, mermaids, fairies, and pirates."
Wendy could hardly believe her ears. A place with no homework, no rules, and no one to tell you it’s bedtime...
Peter leaned in closer and whispered:
"You could come with me."
Wendy’s heart skipped a beat. Go to Neverland? It would be the greatest adventure of her life!
But before she could answer, Peter looked at John and Michael, who were now awake and watching curiously from their beds.
"They can come too," he added. "We need a mother to take care of us and tell us stories."
Wendy felt flattered. Mother. It sounded nice.
"But how will we get there?"
Peter laughed and pointed at Tinker Bell.
"With pixie dust, of course."

Tinker Bell, who had been hovering on the sidelines, looked at Wendy with annoyance. She didn't like Peter paying so much attention to this girl. But Peter was the boss, so, somewhat grudgingly, she shook her tiny wings and sprinkled a fine golden dust over them. ✨
"Now, think happy thoughts," Peter instructed.

Wendy, John, and Michael squeezed their eyes shut. Wendy imagined the starry sky, her mother’s stories, and the thrill of adventure. John thought of pirates and battles. Michael thought of the candy he got after dinner. 🍬
And then, the impossible happened.
Their bodies became as light as feathers, and suddenly... they were floating! 🕊️
John did a somersault in the air. Michael squealed with delight. Wendy felt the breeze ruffle her hair as she drifted around the nursery.
"Are you ready?" asked Peter, hovering by the window.
"Yes!" they all shouted.
And so, with pixie dust shimmering around them and their hearts pounding with excitement, Wendy, John, and Michael flew out of their bedroom and into the night, bound for Neverland. 🌌✨

Wendy, John, and Michael soared over London, feeling the crisp night air on their faces. The city lights stretched out like a sea of fireflies beneath their feet, and every time Peter turned to check on them, his mischievous laughter filled the sky.
"Faster!" he shouted, spinning in the air as if flying were just a game.
The children struggled to keep up, learning to bank and turn with every gust of wind. Michael, the youngest, was laughing so hard he almost forgot he was actually flying.
"Is it much farther?" asked John, trying to keep his balance with his nightcap still on his head.
"Just follow the second star to the right and fly straight on 'til morning," Peter replied confidently.

But what they didn’t know was that someone else was watching their arrival. From the deck of a pirate ship, a man with a stern face and a hook instead of a hand glared at the sky with a furrowed brow.
"It’s him!" growled Captain Hook, gritting his teeth.
Beside him, the clumsy but loyal Mr. Smee nodded worriedly.
"Yes, Captain… Peter Pan has returned."
Hook narrowed his eyes. His hatred for Peter was as deep as the ocean.
The captain clenched his fist. This time, he would catch Peter Pan and have his revenge once and for all. 🏴‍☠️
When the children crossed the final cloud, they finally saw it: Neverland. 🏝️

It was an island covered in lush green forests, with tall mountains and waterfalls that sparkled under the moonlight. There were lagoons where mermaids swam, mysterious caves, and a great rock in the sea where a pirate ship lay anchored. ⛰️🌊
"Welcome to Neverland!" Peter exclaimed, diving down.
Wendy, John, and Michael descended after him, amazed by the beauty of the place. But their awe didn’t last long.
"Peter, look out!" screamed Wendy.
From the pirate ship, Hook had ordered the cannons to fire. A massive cannonball whizzed past the children and exploded in the air with a deafening BOOM. 💥
"Pirates!" shouted Peter, dodging another shot with ease. "Come on, move!"
The children dove at full speed while cannon fire echoed through the sky. Tinker Bell flew faster than anyone, leaving a golden trail behind her. ✨
When they finally landed in the forest, Wendy looked around, trying to catch her breath.
"Do they always welcome you like this?" she asked, her heart still racing.
"More or less," Peter replied with a carefree grin. "But don't worry, here you are free to do whatever you want."
John and Michael exchanged a look. They had never been to a place with no rules, no school, and no orders from grown-ups. The adventure was just beginning. 🚀
But deep in the forest, someone else was watching them in silence. The Lost Boys. 👀

Peter led Wendy and her brothers to a cave hidden among the tree roots. There, a group of children waited with curiosity. These were the Lost Boys—children who, according to Peter, had fallen out of their strollers when they were babies and were never claimed by their parents.
"Guys, this is Wendy, John, and Michael!" Peter announced proudly. "Wendy is going to tell us stories and be our mother."
The Lost Boys clapped excitedly. 👏
But among them, a small, glowing figure floated with a frown. Tinker Bell was furious. 😠
From the moment Wendy appeared, Peter hadn't paid any attention to the fairy. And now... he wanted her to stay forever?
The little fairy clenched her teeth. She wouldn't allow it.
So, in a fit of jealousy, she flew over to the Lost Boys and whispered with a malicious voice:
"Peter wants you to get rid of that girl. He says she's a wicked bird."
The Lost Boys, who always obeyed Peter without question, grabbed their bows and arrows and prepared to attack. 🏹
"Here she comes!" shouted one of them as he saw Wendy approaching.
And without thinking twice... they fired.
An arrow flew through the air, and Wendy barely had time to scream before feeling an impact on her chest. 💔
The Lost Boys ran to see their "catch," but as soon as they saw her on the ground, pale and still, they realized what they had done.
"What happened?" asked Peter, arriving on the scene.
The boys, trembling, pointed at Tinker Bell.
"She told us to do it..."
Peter turned his head slowly. He had never been so angry. 😡
Tinker Bell, realizing her mistake, shrugged and tried to smile.
"I... I just wanted to protect you..."
But Peter didn't want to hear it.
"Tinker Bell, I banish you forever."
The fairy turned pale. It couldn't be.
For the first time in her life, she felt the crushing weight of loneliness.
With a heavy heart, she turned around and disappeared into the thick of the forest. 🌿
Meanwhile, Wendy slowly opened her eyes. The arrow had only grazed her. She was alive. 😲
"I think I need to rest..." she whispered, still dazed.
Peter sighed with relief.
"Don't worry. Here in Neverland, nothing bad will happen to you."
But Wendy wasn't so sure about that.
And she didn't know that far away, hiding in the darkness, Hook's pirates were already planning their next attack. ☠️

After the incident with the arrow, Wendy stayed in the Lost Boys' hideout, a great underground cave beneath the roots of a massive tree. 🌳 There, she recovered quickly and began to learn more about life in Neverland.

There were no rules or homework, just games, adventures, and constant challenges. Every day could be a battle against pirates, a meeting with mermaids in the lagoon, or an expedition through the jungle in search of magical creatures. 🏹🦑🌿
But there was something else. Wendy noticed that Peter avoided talking about growing up or anything that seemed too "adult."
"Do you never think about the future?" she asked him one night.
Peter shrugged.
"The future is boring. I prefer adventures."
Wendy said nothing, but in her heart, she began to wonder if, perhaps, one day she would want to go back home. 🏠✨

One day, while exploring the island, the children heard a distant cry. They approached cautiously and found Tiger Lily, the brave princess of the island's native tribe, tied to a rock at the water's edge.
Peter frowned.
"This is the pirates' doing," he said angrily. "I bet they left her there to drown when the tide comes in."
Without hesitating, he dove into the water and cut the ropes with his dagger.
Just at that moment, Hook and his men appeared from the trees.
"Attack, lads!" roared the captain, pointing his sword at Peter. ⚔️
The Lost Boys ran to hide, but Peter didn't back down. With a defiant smile, he raised his dagger and prepared to fight.

The duel was fierce. Peter was as fast as the wind, dodging Hook's attacks with ease. But the captain was experienced, and every time Peter tried to strike, Hook countered with his sharp steel hook. 🏴‍☠️
For a moment, Peter was about to fall, but then Tiger Lily, now free, leaped onto one of the pirates and snatched his sword.
"We fight together!" she exclaimed, ready for battle.

With the help of the Lost Boys and Tiger Lily, the pirates were defeated and forced to flee. Hook, furious, jumped into the sea to escape... just as the crocodile appeared, mouth wide open and eyes gleaming with hunger. 🐊
The captain swam desperately as the tick-tock of the clock inside the crocodile's belly echoed in the air. He barely managed to get away.
Peter, laughing, spun in the air victoriously.
"That'll teach them not to mess with us!"
Tiger Lily, grateful, took them to her tribe's camp, where they threw a feast in honor of Peter Pan. 🎉🔥
But while everyone celebrated, Wendy couldn't stop thinking about something...
What if she, John, and Michael were stuck in Neverland forever? 🤔
Captain Hook was furious. Peter Pan had humiliated him again.
He wouldn't rest until he caught him.
While plotting his revenge, he saw something glowing in the darkness. It was Tinker Bell. ✨
The little fairy, still bitter about her banishment, was flying alone through the forest.
Hook smiled cunningly.
"Poor fairy..." he said with a sugary voice. "Peter Pan has treated you very badly, hasn't he?"
Tinker Bell crossed her arms and didn't reply.
"I bet he doesn't even miss you... But tell me, my dear, do you know where his hideout is?"
Tinker Bell hesitated.
"What if you tell me?" whispered Hook. "We could get rid of Wendy, and then Peter would pay attention to you again."
Tinker Bell blinked. Was it possible?
After a long silence... she nodded.
Hook smiled maliciously.
That very night, the Captain and his pirates set out. 🏴‍☠️
While the pirates prepared to attack, Wendy was trying to convince her brothers that they needed to go home.
"This is fun, but Mom and Dad must be worried," she said, looking at John and Michael.
John hesitated. He didn't want to admit it, but he missed his bed and his life in London too.
Peter, on the other hand, crossed his arms.
"Go back if you want. I'm staying."
Wendy was hurt by his indifference.
"Then... I suppose this is goodbye," she said, feeling a lump in her throat.
Peter didn't answer.
That night, before sleeping, Wendy left a small cup of medicine next to Peter's bed.
"Just in case you get a headache," she said softly.
Peter nodded without looking at her.
When Wendy was finally asleep, Hook's silhouette appeared at the cave entrance.
He approached silently and poured a few drops of poison into Peter's medicine.
Then, he disappeared into the darkness with an evil smile. 😈
The next morning, when Peter woke up, he saw the medicine cup and picked it up.
"I don't know why Wendy left me this," he mumbled.
Just as he was about to drink it, a golden light flew in his direction.
It was Tinker Bell.
"Don't drink it!" she screamed, desperate.
Peter stopped, surprised.
"It's poisoned!"
And before he could react, Tinker Bell darted toward the cup and drank all the poison herself.
Peter stared at her in horror.
"What have you done?"
Tinker Bell smiled weakly. Her light began to flicker.
"I couldn't let anything happen to you..."
Peter felt his heart shrink.
"You can't die, Tinker Bell!"
But the fairy's glow was fading more and more.
Then, Peter remembered something.
"Tinker Bell, fairies can live if someone believes in them, right?"
She nodded faintly.
Peter stood up and shouted into the air:
"If you believe in fairies, clap your hands!"
A strange wind swept through Neverland.
And then, Peter heard a sound.
Then another. And another.
The sound grew, filling the island with its echo. 👏
And just when all seemed lost, Tinker Bell's light shone brightly once again.
"You're back!" Peter exclaimed, relieved.
Tinker Bell fluttered in the air, smiling with her radiant glow.
But before they could celebrate, a scream pierced the air.
The pirates had attacked the cave.
Wendy, John, Michael, and the Lost Boys had been captured.
Peter clenched his fists.
"I'm going to rescue them."
And with a determined look, he flew toward the battle. 🏴‍☠️✨
The moon shone over the sea as Wendy, John, Michael, and the Lost Boys were dragged onto the Jolly Roger, Captain Hook's ship. 🌊🏴‍☠️
The sails flapped in the wind, and the sound of waves hitting the wooden hull beat a spooky rhythm.
"Welcome aboard!" announced Hook with a cruel smile. "Today you will have the honor of becoming pirates... or walking the plank."
The Lost Boys looked at each other in fear.
"We will never be pirates!" shouted John, trying to sound brave.
Hook shrugged.
"Then let the ceremony begin."
The pirates prepared the plank for the children to jump into the sea. Wendy, keeping calm, tried to buy time.
"At least allow me to sing one last lullaby to my brothers."
The pirates laughed, but Hook raised a hand.
"Very well, my dear. Sing."
Wendy cleared her throat and began to hum a soft melody. 🎶
Meanwhile, up in the sky, Peter Pan was already on his way. ✨
Peter Pan descended silently onto the ship, moving through the shadows.
Tinker Bell, fully recovered, flew by his side.
"There are too many pirates," she whispered. "What's the plan?"
Peter smiled with his signature twinkle in his eyes.
"Do what I do best: have fun."
Without making a sound, he began to untie the ropes holding the ship's sails. Then, he whistled, mimicking the sound of the crocodile. 🐊
The pirates turned pale.
"Did you hear that?" whispered Smee. "It's the crocodile!"
"Silence, you idiots!" growled Hook, though his own hand trembled on the hilt of his sword.
At that instant, Peter appeared atop the mast.
"Hello, Hook!" he shouted with mocking joy. "Did you miss me?"
The pirates shouted in surprise. Peter jumped and landed on the deck with a perfect somersault.
"Get him!" ordered Hook.
But Peter was too fast. He moved like a lightning bolt, dodging swords, leaping over barrels, and disarming pirates with ease. ⚔️
The Lost Boys, seeing their chance, used the chaos to free themselves and grab weapons from the fallen pirates.
The battle had begun. 🏴‍☠️🔥
Hook, furious, advanced with his sword drawn.
"You won't escape this time, Peter Pan."
Peter laughed.
"You always say that, don't you?"
They crossed swords. The sound of steel rang through the air.
Peter moved lightly, laughing and teasing with every strike. Hook, on the other hand, attacked with rage, trying to catch him with his sharp hook.
But Peter wasn't easy to catch.
"You know what, Hook?" he said, dodging another blow. "You'll never learn that children like me always win."
Hook roared and lunged, but Peter spun in the air, disarming him with an agile strike.
Hook's sword clattered to the floor.
At that moment, a terrible sound was heard: tick-tock, tick-tock. ⏳🐊
The crocodile was near.
Peter smiled.
"Looks like someone is coming to see you, Captain."
Hook backed away slowly. The crocodile emerged from the water with its mouth wide open.
"No! Back, you beast!" screamed Hook, losing his balance.
The pirates, seeing their leader in danger, panicked and jumped into the water to flee.
Peter took a step forward.
"Goodbye, Captain Hook."
And with a light push... Hook fell into the sea.
The crocodile snapped its jaws shut. 🐊
The surviving pirates fled, rowing away in boats, leaving the ship behind.
Peter and the Lost Boys celebrated with shouts of joy.
"The ship is ours!" exclaimed John, raising a sword.
But Wendy just looked at the sea in silence.
It was time to go home. 🏠✨
With Peter in command, the Lost Boys hoisted the sails of the Jolly Roger and flew the ship back to London. 🏴‍☠️✨
When they landed in the Darling nursery, everything was just as they had left it. The beds were made. The window was open.
Wendy felt a lump in her throat.
"Do you think Mom and Dad will be waiting for us?" asked John.
"I'm sure they are," whispered Wendy.
The children entered the room cautiously.
And there, in the armchair, asleep with a handkerchief in her hands, was Mrs. Darling.
Wendy ran to her.
Mrs. Darling opened her eyes with tears of happiness and hugged her children tightly. 🤍
The Lost Boys watched the scene with sadness.
"We wish we had a mother too…" one of them whispered.
Mrs. Darling looked at them tenderly.
"You can stay with us, if you like."
The Lost Boys exchanged looks and nodded excitedly.
All except one.
Peter stayed by the window, watching the scene without moving.
Wendy turned to him.
"Peter… aren't you staying?"
He shook his head.
"I never grow up."
Wendy felt a pinch in her heart.
"But... you could try."
Peter looked down.
"I don't want to grow up."
Wendy walked over and took his hand.
"Promise me you'll never forget us."
Peter smiled, but didn't answer.
"Goodbye, Wendy."
And with one last spin in the air, he disappeared into the night. 🌙✨
Years later...
Wendy grew up.
One night, many years later, while she was telling stories to her own daughter, Jane, the window flew open.
Wendy looked in amazement.
Peter Pan was there, looking exactly the same.
"Wendy, I've come to take you flying with me."
But Wendy shook her head.
"I can't, Peter. I'm all grown up now."
Peter looked at her with disbelief.
"But… you said you wouldn't forget me."
Wendy smiled sadly.
"I never forgot you."
Peter hung his head.
"Then... you can't come?"
Before Wendy could answer, her daughter Jane got out of bed.
"Mom, who is he?"
Peter looked up. Jane had the same sparkling eyes Wendy had as a child.
"Do you believe in Neverland?" Peter asked her.
Jane nodded enthusiastically.
Peter held out his hand.
"Do you want to come with me?"
Jane looked at her mother.
Wendy stroked her hair.
"Go on, sweetie."
And so, with an excited smile, Jane flew out the window with Peter Pan. ✨
Neverland always found the children who still wanted to dream.

119.t: Far Horizons 8: Shadows on the Moon
p: The base hallway reflected the dim artificial light as Aura walked forward with a frown, her arms crossed over her chest, her mind in turmoil. She’d had another argument with Isaac. Not an open fight, but an exchange of subtle phrases, small stabs wrapped in affection. What started as a conversation about the new shift distribution at the base ended in a series of insinuations from him about Zoe. About how she also needed support, about how Aura was too busy with other things to notice.

She clenched her teeth. It wasn’t the first time Isaac had slipped in comments that made her doubt her own perception. Sometimes she felt trapped in a labyrinth where reality was distorted, where he was the only constant. And that suffocated her.
It was then that she received the message from her mother.

Mara had requested her presence in the meeting room. When Aura arrived, her mother was standing next to a holographic screen where a three-dimensional image of a gray, crater-marked moon floated. Her expression was serene, but her mind worked with surgical precision. Mara had been observing. Her daughter was fading. The brilliance of her character was blurring day by day, absorbing Isaac’s shadow.
She knew she couldn’t force her to see what was happening, but she could give her a truce. An opportunity to get away and breathe fresh air. Even if it was under a different sky.
—I’m going to recommend you for an expedition to the moon mine, 😊 —she said bluntly.
Aura blinked. —Me? What for?
—So you can learn more about Tantalum mining and the telecommunications being established there, —Mara explained, in a neutral tone. Too neutral.
Aura narrowed her eyes. —But there are specialized adults for that. It doesn’t make sense for someone young and inexperienced to go.
—We consider it a learning opportunity. A youth group with potential in various areas has been selected. Liam will also be on the expedition.
Aura felt a small pang in her chest. Liam. It had been months since they had barely spoken. Her world had become so reduced to Isaac that she had lost connection with her old friend.
—Are Zoe and Isaac coming? —she asked, with a voice more insecure than she intended.
—No, —Mara replied. —Isaac has assigned tasks at the base, and Zoe is busy with her work in biological research.

Aura frowned, feeling that something didn’t quite add up. She didn’t understand why her mother insisted on sending her, but the idea intrigued her. Suddenly, an unexpected sensation ran through her. The excitement of doing something new, of getting out of the routine. Maybe even escaping a little. 🚀

On the day of embarkation, the ship was ready on the launch pad. Isaac had been extremely angry with Aura’s departure, so as a sign of protest, he didn’t want to go to say goodbye. Aura climbed the ramp along with the other selected young people. When she was about to enter through the hatch, she felt a hand on her shoulder.
She turned and saw her mother with a small translucent container in her hands. Inside, Nim slept curled up, his feline-lizard body rising and falling with a calm breath.
—Take him with you, —Mara said softly. —He’ll keep you company.
Aura took the container carefully. Something in her chest loosened. She looked at her mother, who held her gaze firmly, and without more words, they said goodbye with a brief but warm hug.

The transport ship was small compared to the enormous shuttle that had brought them to Veridia-7. As they settled into the seats, Liam, with whom she had barely exchanged words, sat near her, but not next to her. Aura felt the distance between them, a gap that she hadn’t noticed how much it affected her until now.

The takeoff was smooth, and they quickly reached the outer area of the atmosphere. The jolts of the ship gave way to the silence of space, dark and enveloping. As the moon grew in the ship’s visor, Aura felt something strange: the lightness in her chest was increasing. As if, with every kilometer away from the base, something heavy was left behind.
—Prepare for partial weightlessness, —the pilot announced.

When they landed, the young people were equipped with spacesuits. Their movements were clumsy, and each step made them jump much further than they had imagined. Soon the games and laughter began among them, bouncing as if they were on trampolines.

In this way, between friendly pushes, they went outside. The mining base was a robust structure, of a metallic white that reflected the light of the system. The corridors were narrower than those of Veridia-7, and each surface seemed designed with extreme functionality. Aura couldn’t help but feel a growing excitement as they explored.

That night, a small welcome party was held in the common area, taking advantage of the newly arrived supplies. It was there that Aura truly reconnected with Liam. While they served themselves rehydrated food and listened to the miners’ stories, he gave her a smile that seemed familiar.
—You’re still a disaster with space food, —Liam joked when Aura spilled part of the food from the tray and tried to intercept it in a clumsy movement.
She smiled, and for a moment, it was as if nothing had changed between them.
They sat on some benches that were partially occupied by station technicians, who introduced themselves with friendly smiles.

—I’m Soren, —said a young technician, with dark hair and a calculating gaze that observed Aura with intensity before introducing himself. There was something about him that seemed familiar, but she couldn’t pinpoint what. Their conversation was fluid, interesting. And for the first time in a long time, she felt that she was able to dialogue with someone in a different way, without Isaac’s shadow projecting over her.

The following days were full of exploration. First, they visited the mine, where they were shown the Tantalum extraction processes, the tools used, and the strict safety protocols. Soren, with his calm but efficient attitude, guided them through the tunnels illuminated with blue lights, explaining every detail with a level of knowledge and affection for his work that began to capture Aura’s attention.

Another day, they went to the telecommunications base, where Aura saw Zoe’s parents working. In addition to improving communications with Earth, they tracked a whole part of space that was still unknown to them.

On another day, they toured the moon in solar ATVs, enjoying the low gravity and exploring the arid and rocky landscape. The experience was fascinating, and Soren proved once again to be an excellent and attentive guide.

Finally, they visited the laboratory where scientists were investigating new applications of Tantalum. Thanks to its particularities, they were studying its possible use in building materials resistant to corrosive sandstorms on Veridia-7.

As the days passed, Aura was feeling more like herself, enjoying the company of Liam, Nim, and her new friends at the lunar base. Little by little, her participation in the conversations was gaining the prominence that she used to have in the past, making, without seeking it, that the others listened to her fascinated, her jokes were the most laughed at and that the affection towards her and the cohesion of the group grew. Aura was shining again with her own light. ✨

Thus, the weeks of exploration passed, until one day the base suffered an unexpected anomaly. Upon returning that afternoon, they found the facilities with the emergency lights activated. Nim ran into Aura’s arms, behaving strangely, restless and emitting high-pitched sounds. Soon after, the life support system suffered a thunderous explosion, causing everyone to detach several centimeters from the ground and hit their heads on the structure.

The backup systems were automatically activated, and the areas affected by the explosion began to be sealed, but in one of the areas the gap was too large. The temperature dropped, and the pressure began to fall. The alarms were deafening, and panic seized the group, but Soren directed them to the pressurization room to put on their spacesuits. There they met other technicians who helped the most inexperienced.
The mechanics came to repair the gap with a sealing expansive foam, but it took a lot of effort and time during which the oxygen reserves were running out.
Finally, they managed to stop the imminent emergency alarms, but the light signals did not turn off, something was still going wrong.

Nim, as Aura took him out of his container, went squealing through a ventilation area, alerting everyone to another possible leak. Following him, they found another tiny gap. The small hybrid had found the problem: for some reason the shield had failed and a rain of micrometeorites had impacted against the base, affecting not only the life support systems, but also the secondary ones. The damaged machinery began to function erratically, causing overloads and, finally, explosions in different parts of the station.

Soren shouted to Aura to run; a second explosion was imminent. She moved with clumsy movements, trying to hold her pet while heading to the door, fighting against the low gravity. Soren pulled her to cover her with his body just as the burst occurred, scattering particles in all directions. The shock wave pushed them into the hallway, where Liam held them so they wouldn’t hit themselves and the door closed protecting them from the vacuum. Soren had received impacts, but had been able to protect Aura and Nim.

Although they had managed to contain the leak temporarily, the damage was serious, and the base could no longer support all the miners. Some could endure in the telecommunications station, but there was not enough space. The team had to return to Veridia-7 to bring reinforcements and supplies.

Back on the planet, when the ship landed, Aura descended from the platform feeling that something in her had changed. Despite the recent events, for weeks, she had been free. She had reconnected with Liam, had met Soren, and had felt like herself again.

But then she saw him. There, among the rest of the colonists relieved and happy to receive their family and friends, was Isaac, who was waiting for her at the end of the walkway with concern drawn on his face, opening his arms to receive her. Beside him, Zoe looked at her with a forced smile.
And in that instant, the weight returned to her chest.

That summer, Simon was sent to stay with his grandparents at their house in the country. It was a small town of low houses with orange-tiled roofs, tucked between the mountains like a well-kept secret. You could count all the neighbors on your fingers, and almost all of them were old. They walked slowly, their skin golden from the sun and their hands weathered by work, always holding something: a branch, a basket, a handful of seeds. 😊

His grandparents were always busy, taking care of the house and the animals. Simon sometimes helped, carrying buckets of water for the chickens or scattering feed, feeling the rough, warm texture of the seeds slipping through his fingers. Other times, they let him wander through the town. And then he would get lost in the sound of his own footsteps on the packed-earth paths, in the smell of baking bread wafting from a window, in the whisper of the trees swaying in the breeze. 🌳

He liked to hide in the hayloft. The air there was warm and smelled of sunshine trapped in the hay fibers. When he lay down among the bales, the rustle of the straw wrapped around his ears like a whisper, and he could feel the prickly bits of hay poking his arms. The air was filled with a sweet, dry scent, a mix of golden hay and trapped sunlight that filled his lungs with the smell of summer. He would close his eyes and feel the golden dust floating in the air, his own breath slowing to match the quiet of the barn. 🌞

Other times, he would go look at Mr. Henderson's tractor. It was huge, with wheels almost as tall as he was. He would climb up the back and slide into the cab. It smelled of hot rubber and gasoline, and metallic grease. He would run his hand over the rough, dusty seat, touch the levers, and imagine he was the one driving that noisy monster across the vast, dry fields. 🚜

That day, however, he decided to explore a little farther. He walked down a little street that was barely more than a dusty path, taking shelter in the cool shade of some mulberry trees, feeling the gnarled roots that broke through the earth under his feet. The song of the cicadas surrounded him, a steady, vibrating melody. He walked without any rush, until he found himself in front of a half-open wooden door. Inside, the dim light seemed thicker than in other houses. 🌬️

He went in. The air was cool, with a faint scent of damp earth and ash. The shelves were filled with pottery pieces of all shapes and sizes. Large urns as big as barrels, narrow-necked jugs, plates with soft and delicate patterns. He ran his fingertips over the smooth, cool surface of an urn, feeling a pleasant tingle at its perfection. 🏺
“Hello!” —a voice said from behind him.
Simon jumped.
“You’re Grandma Rose’s grandson, aren’t you?”
He turned and saw a woman with white hair pulled back in a loose bun. Her hands were stained with clay, and her dark eyes sparkled with curiosity.
“Yes,” —he answered, a little embarrassed.
“I’m Eleanor. Do you like pottery?”
Simon shrugged.
“Have you ever tried it? Come.”
She led him to a large wooden table. On it were lumps of clay, tools, and small bowls of water.

“First, get your hands wet. Like this.” Eleanor dipped hers into the clear water, and Simon copied her. The water was cold, slippery. He felt a shiver run up his skin, as if the coolness woke something up inside him. ❄️
Eleanor handed him a piece of clay. It was soft and cool, and when he squeezed it with his fingers, it gave way with a silky smoothness.
“Make a little figure. How about a rabbit?”

Simon got to work. He pressed his fingers into the clay, turned it, squeezed it, and molded it. When it got a little dry, he would dip his fingers in the water and start again. The feeling was intoxicating: the coolness, the slippery texture, the faint, wet sound as he smoothed the surface. First, a big ball for the body. Then a smaller one for the head. He joined them gently, smoothing the seam with his wet fingers until it disappeared. He was completely absorbed, lost in the game between his hands and the clay. 🎨
“Come here, kiddo.” Eleanor motioned for him to come over.
He walked over and saw a strange, round, wooden table with a stand and a pedal at the base.
“Sit right here, in front of me.”
When he did, Eleanor began to press the pedal. The table started to spin with a soft whirring sound. In the center, the lump of clay began to move.
“Get your hands nice and wet,” she said, guiding him.

Simon obeyed. Then, Eleanor wrapped her hands around his and, with a slow movement, brought them to the spinning clay. At first, the feeling was strange: the clay vibrated with the motion, pushing against his fingers with an unexpected force. But Eleanor guided him gently, patiently. Her large, firm hands held his and taught him how to press, to lift, to open up the clay.

To the rhythm of the pedal's gentle creak, the clay stretched, shrank, and took shape with an amazing gentleness. Simon felt its softness gliding between his fingers, as if the clay were responding to his thoughts. His hands slipped and sank, feeling the spin, the sway of the shape emerging, growing, transforming, like a dancer on a stage. It was hypnotic, as if he and the clay understood each other without words. 🌀
Eleanor stopped pressing the pedal, and the wheel slowed to a stop. With a piece of wire, she cut the base of the vase they had formed together.
“Now I have to fire it in the kiln,” Eleanor explained. “When it’s ready, I’ll call you so you can come and paint it.”
Eleanor dipped Simon’s hands into a large basin of cool water and gently washed away all the clay, leaving his skin softer than ever before. “But that,” she said, “is for another day.” 😌

🔹 Warning for Parents and Caregivers 🔹 This story deals with the farewell of a beloved pet and is intended to help children process grief. We recommend respecting the suggested age (+8 years) and, in the case of especially sensitive children, reading it with an adult who can accompany them and answer their questions.
One night Whiskers came to visit me.
It couldn't be real, but there she was, really, in my dreams.
Her gray and dull fur from the last time I saw her was now the bright, intensely colored fur of her youth. Her body was once again compact, flexible, and graceful.

Whiskers came in through the bedroom door as if all those weeks hadn't passed and jumped onto the bed, next to me, purring, looking at me with her blue eyes as if to say, “Here I am, dear owner, one more night with you.”
I loved her so much that I couldn't feel fear or perplexity at seeing her, touching her, smelling her, listening to her.

I hugged her, kissed her, caressed her, pressed her against my body to feel once again that soft and close touch that filled me with peace. That warmth that emanated from her, as if she were a container so full of love that it overflowed.

I began to slide my hand under the blanket. She loved that game. “Hunting” that bulge that I moved in a tempting way, moving it slowly, approaching little by little. Then faster. Suddenly, she, with a quick movement of her little claws, tried to catch it. But I quickly took the bulge to another side and she jumped.

Sometimes I let her catch me, and then she grabbed on like a mini wild beast, biting and attacking with her hind paws. She knew she wasn't hurting me; the blanket protected me. As soon as I took my hand out, everything went back to being soft and cuddly.

Then she asked me, as she had done so many nights, to get into bed with me. She would put herself where the pillow was and try to pull the blanket back with her little paw, while looking at me as if to say, “It's bedtime.”
I let her slide under the blanket and snuggle against my belly, in the hollow left by my body on its side, with my legs bent.

There the little engine started again. Her purring gladdened my ears while I gently caressed her in all the areas that I knew she loved, which she indicated to me with her movements, stretching her little neck, raising her little paws, exposing her soft belly.
The best feeling in the world.
We spent the whole night together. I didn't waste a minute taking care of sleeping. I dedicated myself to her completely, without tiredness, full of happiness and gratitude.
When dawn broke, she got up, brushing against me for the last time. —“Goodbye, my dear owner. I love you.”
—Thank you, Whiskers, for coming to say goodbye. I love you. I will always love you—.
And she left, with her silent steps and her tail held high with happiness, towards the clarity of the hallway ✨.
They can't fool me. I see it clearly. My math teacher is turning into a witch 🧙‍♀️. And it's not just my imagination; I have proof.
To start, there's her hair. It used to be blonde, but little by little, it changed. First, it was light brown, then darker... And now it's as black as coal. Classic.
Her eyes too. I'm absolutely sure they used to be brown, but now they're green. And not just any green, no. A mysterious green, like the bubbling potions in fairy tales 🔮.
But the worst thing is the wart. An unmistakable sign. There, on her nose, tiny, but it grows a little more each day. I wouldn't be surprised if it started sprouting hairs any minute now.
Then there's her laugh. When someone gets a problem wrong, she lets out a sharp cackle. "HA-HA-HA" 😂. Like a bat screeching. It gives me goosebumps.
And let's not forget the shoes. She went from wearing normal sneakers to ones with pointy toes, like the witches in storybooks. No one seems to care, but I'm paying attention.
However, what really convinced me was the chocolate. One day, Miss. Laura showed up with a giant bag and gave pieces to everyone. "To sweeten your day," she said with a mysterious smile 😏.
Of course! Witches fatten up their victims before eating them. My classmates don't suspect anything; they're delighted with her. "Miss. Laura is so nice!" they repeat. But I have no doubt.
I'm in danger 😨.
Today, as I was leaving class, she looked at me with a sweet smile and ruffled my hair with her hand. "You're something else, always so observant" 😊.
There you have it! She's already getting fond of me so I'll taste better.
I'm warning you now: if I disappear one day, investigate Miss. Laura. Someday, you'll all see! 🔍

Tommy 🐰 was a little bunny with long ears and a fluffy tail who lived in a forest full of leafy trees. He was always in a good mood, hopping from one place to another and laughing with his friends. But there was something about him that sometimes caused problems: he said things without thinking.
If his friend Benny 🦡, the badger, tripped over a root, Tommy 🐰 would laugh: — "You're clumsier than a snail!"
If Emily 🐦, the woodpecker, tried to tell a joke and stumbled, Tommy 🐰 would joke: — "Your humor is worse than a log!"
For him, they were just words, but he didn't stop to see how others felt.
One afternoon, his grandma 🐇 called him to her burrow. She was a wise bunny, with gray fur and a look that always made him think.
— "Tommy 🐰, my little one, do you know what empathy is?"
— "Empa… what?"
Grandma 🐇 smiled: — "It's putting yourself in someone else's shoes. Feeling what they feel."
— "I just say what I see. It's not my fault that Benny 🦡 is clumsy or that Emily 🐦 makes mistakes."
Grandma 🐇 opened an old trunk and took out some small brown shoes with golden laces.
— "These are magic shoes. When you wear them, you'll feel what others feel when you talk to them."
Tommy looked at them curiously. He had never had shoes before. He put them on and went out to play without thinking too much about it.
Soon after, he found Benny 🦡, who was trying to dig up some roots to eat. He failed several times, until Tommy 🐰 burst out laughing: — "Benny 🦡, you look like a blind mole looking for food!"

In that instant, the shoes worked their magic. A knot tightened in his stomach, as if the whole forest was watching him and waiting for him to fail. He felt Benny's 🦡 frustration, his desire to do well, and his sadness at being ridiculed.
The badger lowered his gaze. — "I just… was trying to get better."
— "Sorry, Benny 🦡. If you want, I'll help you dig."
Later, Tommy 🐰 saw Emily 🐦 telling a joke to a group of friends. She stumbled on a word, and he couldn't help but let out a mocking laugh: — "Emily 🐦, you talk worse than a sleeping parrot!"

But as soon as he finished the sentence, the shoes activated again. His heart started beating fast, and an uncomfortable heat rose to his cheeks. He felt clumsy, observed, and afraid of making another mistake.
Emily 🐦 lowered her head. — "Sometimes I get nervous…"
Tommy 🐰 took a deep breath. It was the same feeling he had just experienced.
— "Your story is funny, Emily 🐦. How does it go on?"
The bird looked at him with surprise and, encouraged, finished her story with a smile.

Throughout the day, the shoes continued to teach him. When Sophia 🐿️, the squirrel, lost her favorite nut and he laughed, he felt her anguish as if it were his own. When he ignored Nick 🦔 the hedgehog when he showed him a drawing, he felt his disappointment.
Every little mockery or indifference became a weight on his chest.
That night, Tommy 🐰 sat in his burrow and looked at the shoes. Now he understood their purpose. The next day, he decided to do something different.
When he saw Benny 🦡 trying to dig up a worm, instead of making fun of him, he encouraged him: — "I'm sure you'll get it this time!"
Benny 🦡 smiled and, in the end, caught one.
When Emily 🐦 told a joke, Tommy 🐰 waited until the end and laughed with her, instead of laughing at her.
When Sophia 🐿️ lost another nut, Tommy 🐰 helped her look for it.
Little by little, his words stopped hurting and started making others feel good.
That afternoon, he returned to his grandma's 🐇 burrow.
— "Grandma 🐇, I don't need the shoes anymore. Now I know what empathy is."
The bunny smiled and put the shoes back in her trunk. Then she hugged her grandson tenderly.
— "I'm proud of you, Tommy. Words have power, and you have learned to use them well."

From then on, Tommy 🐰 remained the same playful bunny as always, but now his jokes were kind, his words helped, and his heart understood others. And so, the forest became a warmer and happier place for everyone. 🌳🌞

The air had that cold, clean scent of early February, when winter still clings to the earth, but the sun peeks shyly through the clouds. The damp dirt path wound between the pine trees, tall and solemn, their needles swaying gently in the breeze. Lily walked slowly, feeling the icy air fill her lungs and clear her mind. ❄️

Each step echoed on the ground softened by the damp fallen leaves. Her boots crunched with a faint sound, and with each deep breath, she perceived the scent of resin, of wet wood, of earth sleeping under the winter. Silence enveloped everything. A serene, vibrant silence, the silence of the mountain waiting for the snow. 🍂

She looked up. The clouds had closed in a pearly gray blanket, dense and soft, stretching like an infinite ceiling. Then, it happened. First, a slight white sparkle danced in the air and landed on her rosy cheek, like a cool little kiss. Then, another fell. And another. Lily stretched out her hand, catching one with the tip of her fingers. Just an instant, and the flake turned into a cold drop on the wool. She took off her gloves and extended her hands to the sky, watching the tiny snow crystals accumulate on her palm before slowly melting. 😊
—It's snowing… Lily whispered, as if afraid to break the spell of that moment. ❄️

The flakes began to multiply, twirling in the air, floating with an ethereal lightness. The snow covered the path, the tops of the pine trees, the roofs of the little wooden houses scattered across the mountain. The world acquired an even deeper calm, as if everything were snuggling under a white veil. ❄️
—Come inside! Mom called from the house. 🏠

She wiped her hands on her pants and walked to the door. As she peered inside the house, the contrast was immediate. As she took off her boots in the entrance, the warmth of the home enveloped her like a fluffy blanket. An unmistakable aroma floated in the air: that of wood burning in the fireplace, with earthy and resinous notes. She closed her eyes for an instant, feeling that scent fill her chest and remind her of other winters past. 🔥

She went to the window. The snow fell in a slow dance, floating with a serene harmony. As she pressed her face against the icy glass, her breath formed a mist that dissipated slowly. She exhaled softly again, this time seeking to create a circle of fog. With a finger, she drew a spiral and watched it disappear from the outside in, while the whiteness of the outside covered everything. The flakes accumulated on the branches of the pine trees, on the window sills, in the curves of the roof. 🪟

The fire crackled in the fireplace, the sound was a warm murmur, almost a whisper. She dropped onto the sofa, sinking her fingers into the thick blanket that rested on the back. She closed her eyes for an instant and listened. The wind outside was barely a distant murmur, like a sleeping echo. Inside, only the crackling of the wood consuming little by little. 🔥

She snuggled further into the softness of the blanket and let her eyes follow the incessant dance of the snow behind the window. Everything was white, soft, serene. Time didn't matter. Only that instant, that stillness, the sensation of being in a world on pause, covered in cotton. 💤
Mom appeared with a steaming mug and offered it to her. ☕
—Hot chocolate, she said with a smile. 😊

Lily held it in her hands, feeling the heat pass through the ceramic and reach her skin. She brought her lips to the mug, the first sip was thick and comforting, a liquid hug that went down her throat leaving a trail of warmth. ☕
Outside, the snow continued to fall. Silent. Incessant. Like a winter spell that wrapped the world in a peaceful dream. ❄️

The milkmaid walked with a light step along the path, carefully balancing a pail of milk on her head. She had filled it early that morning and was now going to the market, where she would sell it for a good price. 😊

As she walked, the sun shone over the golden fields, and a gentle breeze ruffled her bangs just a bit. But she paid no attention to any of that, because her mind was already far away, dreaming of everything she would do with the money she would earn.

"With what they pay me for this milk," she thought, "I will buy a dozen eggs. When the eggs hatch, little chicks will be born. I will raise them carefully, and when they are grown, I will sell them to buy a piglet."
She smiled to herself, imagining the little pig trotting around the yard.

"I will feed him well until he grows plump and strong. Then, I will sell him, and with that money, I will buy a calf. I will care for her until she becomes a dairy cow, and then I will have my very own milk to sell every day."
The milkmaid was so excited about her plans that she couldn't help but give a little jump for joy.
"And when I have my cow and sell her milk, I will be so prosperous that I can buy anything I want!"

But right at that moment… smash! As she jumped, the pail slipped from her head, fell to the ground, and broke into a thousand pieces. The milk spilled all over the path, forming a white puddle that slowly seeped into the dirt.
The milkmaid stood perfectly still, looking at the disaster. Her chicks, her piglet, her calf, her cow… everything had vanished in an instant.
She sighed and shook her head. She had learned an important lesson: dreams are beautiful, but before thinking about what is to come, you must take care of what you have right now.

But the story doesn't end here. The very next day, the milkmaid did not give up. She woke up early again, carefully milked the cow, and made sure to walk with a steady, sure step. She didn't let the disappointment of the day before stop her. This time, she made it to the market and sold her milk, earning the first coins to start her plan. 🐄

Over time, with hard work and determination, the milkmaid managed to buy her eggs, raise her chicks, sell them for a piglet, and finally, get her very own dairy cow. It didn't happen overnight, but she learned that dreams come true with hard work and patience, not just with imagination. 💪
The call came early, just as the sun 🌄 began to peek over the mountains. A shepherd had found a vulture on the ground, unable to fly. A few yards away, a power line tower stood tall against the sky.
—"It looks like it was electrocuted by the power lines. It's still moving, but it's hurt," —the man said over the phone.

The wildlife officers received the alert and, after coordinating with the team from the El Aprisco Sanctuary, they set off. A couple of officers went to pick up two of the sanctuary's caretakers, one of whom was a veterinarian. They all climbed into the SUV, bringing thick gloves, blankets, a special crate, and a first-aid kit.

When they arrived at the meadow, they saw the vulture a few yards from the path. One of its wings was slightly extended, and its gaze was fierce, ready to defend itself. Noticing the humans, it hissed and snapped its beak loudly.
—"A scared vulture is dangerous. Its beak is very strong—if it tries to defend itself, it could really hurt someone," —warned Marta.
Bruno, one of the wildlife officers, smiled with a wink.
—"Don't worry, we'll be gentle... although with those snaps he's giving us, we already have a name for him. We'll call him 'Rayo' ⚡️, for the lightning and for how fast he strikes," —said Bruno.
Everyone laughed, easing the tension of the moment. But they knew the rescue would be tricky.
—"He's not going to make this easy for us," —muttered Marta, getting the blanket ready.
—"And he shouldn't. He's scared. His fear is normal. We're the strangers here," —replied Bruno.
One of the caretakers positioned himself to one side, while another approached calmly. The vulture took clumsy hops, trying to get away, but its injured wing made it wobble.
—"Careful, don't let it get near the tower again," —warned Miguel, the other caretaker, as he circled around the bird to block its path.
The vulture let out another warning snap and began to flap its wings, straining its injured one, but Bruno, with firm and careful movements, managed to throw the blanket over its head.
—"Easy there, buddy, we've got you," —said Bruno.

The team acted quickly. They held the vulture firmly but gently, making sure it wouldn't injure itself further, and placed it in the padded crate. The bird, though still restless, calmed down slightly without the direct light in its eyes.
—"We're taking you somewhere safe, Rayo," —Marta whispered softly.
On the way to the El Aprisco Sanctuary, Bruno explained to the others why vultures were so important.

—"A lot of people think vultures are ugly or dangerous, but they're essential. They eat the remains of dead animals and prevent diseases from spreading. Without them, the countryside would be full of decaying carcasses," —explained Bruno.
—"They're like the cleanup crew of the forest," —commented Miguel, nodding.

—"Exactly. But poorly designed power lines are causing a lot of accidents for them. They could be prevented with simple measures, like insulators on the wires, but you know things aren't always done the way they should be..." —said Bruno.

When they arrived at the sanctuary, they took Rayo to the small wildlife hospital. Marta quickly prepared a mild sedative to calm him and keep him from getting hurt more during the examination. Very carefully, they gave him the dose and waited for him to relax before starting the check-up. Once he was sedated, Marta examined him carefully: he had minor burns on his wing and an injured talon, but there were no signs of any serious fractures she could see. However, before making any decisions about his recovery, they would need to take X-rays to make sure there was no internal damage or broken bones in his wing.
—"For now, we can't know if he'll be able to fly again. We'll have to wait for the results and see how he recovers," —said Marta as she covered him with a soft blanket.
Bruno, who was watching from the doorway, nodded seriously.
—"Either way, he's in good hands," —said Bruno.

The wind 🌬️ rustled the branches outside the clinic, and inside, Rayo breathed slowly, still under the effects of the sedative. His wings, which once soared through the skies, now lay still, and his future depended on what the X-rays would reveal.
Miguel turned off the light, leaving only the soft glow of a lamp in the corner. Marta stayed by the crate a moment longer, watching Rayo's silhouette.
—"We'll know more tomorrow," —Marta whispered, as if the bird could hear her.
No one said it out loud, but they all shared the same thought: Would Rayo ever feel the wind beneath his wings again? Or, like so many others, would he have to learn to live on the ground?
In the darkness of the clinic, Rayo's fate remained a mystery.

Once upon a time, there was a miller who, upon his death, left his mill, his donkey, and his cat as an inheritance to his three sons. The division was simple: the eldest inherited the mill, the second the donkey, and the youngest received the cat. The youngest brother lamented his luck, for while his brothers could earn a living working with what they had received, he only had a simple cat.

But the cat was no ordinary animal. One day, he spoke to his master and said: “Do not worry, my lord. If you provide me with a pair of boots, a sack, and a wide-brimmed hat, I will show you that your inheritance is not as poor as you think.”

The young man, though surprised by the words of Puss in Boots, decided to humor him and got him what he asked for. With his new attire, Puss in Boots began his plan. He gathered some grain and headed to a forest clearing, where he scattered the seeds near a snare trap. Patiently, he waited for the hares to come and eat, and at the precise moment, he pulled the snare, trapping them. Next, he ventured into a field where he knew partridges gathered and used his agility to catch them with great skill. Once he had enough prey, he put them in his sack and headed toward the royal palace.

Puss in Boots, with his elegant hat and shiny boots, looked so extravagant and curious that the guards, surprised by his unusual bearing, could not help but let him pass to present himself before the King.
“Your Majesty, I am Puss in Boots, loyal servant to the Marquis of Carabas,” he said politely. “My master wishes to offer you these gifts.”

The hares and, above all, the partridges pleased the King greatly, as they were his favorite dish. Intrigued by the generosity of the Marquis of Carabas, the monarch accepted the gifts with a smile and ordered them to be served at his table. Puss in Boots continued to appear at the palace for several weeks, delivering increasingly choice prey. The King's curiosity grew to the point of asking his advisors exactly who this generous nobleman was and why he had never met him in person, though none had ever heard of him.

One day, Puss in Boots learned that the King was going to visit the river in the company of his daughter, the princess, and said to his master: “Do as I ask, my lord: go to the river and bathe in the place I shall show you. I will take care of the rest.”

The young man obeyed, and while he bathed, Puss in Boots hid his clothes in some bushes. Just as the King's carriage passed by, Puss in Boots began to shout: “Help! The Marquis of Carabas is drowning!”

The King, remembering the generous gifts he had received, ordered his guards to rescue the young man. Puss in Boots hurried to inform the King: “My lord has been the victim of bandits! While he was bathing, they stole his splendid clothes and left him in this pitiful state.”

The King, impressed and eager to help such a generous Marquis of Carabas, ordered his servants to give him one of his own suits. Dressed in rich fabrics and adornments worthy of a nobleman, the young man was invited to step into the royal carriage. Inside was the princess, who, upon seeing the handsome Marquis of Carabas, felt immediately attracted to him.

Puss in Boots, delighted to see that his plan was beginning to work, ran ahead of the carriage. Finding some peasants harvesting a field, he told them: “If the King asks you whose lands these are, answer that they belong to the Marquis of Carabas. If you do, you will receive a great reward.”
When the King asked, the peasants answered in unison: “Your Majesty, these lands belong to the Marquis of Carabas.”

Puss in Boots repeated the same warning to all the peasants he met along the way, and each time the King was more impressed by the supposed wealth of the Marquis. Marveling at the abundance of his domains, the monarch wished to see the residence of such a noble knight.

Finally, the cunning Puss in Boots arrived at an imposing castle, home to a fearsome ogre who was actually the owner of all those lands. Knowing his reputation, Puss in Boots requested an audience with him and, so as not to be turned away, praised his prodigious powers.
“They say you can transform yourself into any animal,” said Puss in Boots. “Is that true?”
“Of course I can. Do you doubt it?” replied the ogre.
“Oh, not at all,” replied Puss in Boots. “I just find it hard to imagine something so impressive. Could you turn yourself into, say, a lion?”

The ogre did not hesitate and, in an instant, his body lengthened and widened until he became a fearsome lion. He roared with such force that Puss in Boots pretended to shrink in fear and beg for mercy. Satisfied with the feline's reaction, the ogre returned to his original form with a smug smile.

“Extraordinary!” exclaimed Puss in Boots. “But I wonder if you could do something even more amazing. Transforming into such a large creature is impressive, but what about the opposite? Would you be able to turn into something as small as a mouse?”

The ogre, eager to prove his power once again, quickly shrank down until he became a tiny mouse. It was his last mistake, for the cunning Puss in Boots, with an agile leap, pounced on him and swallowed him in one bite.
Shortly after, the King's carriage arrived at the castle. Puss in Boots ran to receive them and announced with great enthusiasm: “Welcome, Your Majesty, to the castle of the Marquis of Carabas!”

The King, dazzled by the magnitude of the castle and the riches of its supposed owner, did not hesitate to offer the princess's hand in marriage. The young man, who had once been poor, became a prince thanks to the cunning of his faithful companion.
