The Marquis of Carabas never forgot the favors of his faithful companion and rewarded him with a new cape, hat, and boots. From then on, Puss in Boots lived surrounded by luxury and never had to hunt mice again, unless he did it just for fun.

128.t: A New Visitor in the Garden
p: In the enchanted garden, where fruits and vegetables lived in harmony, life went on amidst laughter and chats under the sun. But the peace of the garden was about to be shaken by the arrival of an unexpected visitor. 😊

One morning, with the sun gilding the leaves, a mysterious character crossed the boundaries of the garden. He was tall, with skin of a vibrant green that turned reddish in parts of his body, and a sweet, exotic fragrance. He walked with a distinguished bearing and observed everything with an expression of curiosity, though there was also an air of distrust in his eyes.
Carlota, the carrot, was the first to approach with her usual enthusiasm. "Hello! I haven't seen you here before. My name is Carlota, what's yours?" 😊

The character, who was not used to such direct questions, opened his eyes in surprise and hesitated for a moment, looking her up and down, before replying "My name is Mangé, and I'm a mango from a garden far from this one." 🍃
Carlota reached out to give him a warm squeeze on the arm and said, "Welcome to the garden!" with a smile. 😊

Mangé felt uncomfortable, so he separated a little with a somewhat haughty gesture. "Thank you, but I doubt this place can compare to my old home. There, everything was more elegant, and the fruits were venerated for their sweetness and sophistication."
Melvin, the melon, who had been listening, frowned and commented, "Well, here we all respect each other equally. We don't need to be venerated to live happily."

Manuela, the apple, who never missed an opportunity to stir up discord, crossed her arms and said, "What Melvin means is that perhaps this isn't the right place for someone so... sophisticated!" Mangé pursed his lips and lowered his gaze slightly, feeling a pang of discomfort. He wasn't used to being questioned in that way, and although he didn't want to show it, insecurity began to take root inside him. 😕
Carlota gave Melvin and Manuela a disapproving look and accompanied Mangé to settle in, telling him all the nice things the garden had to offer. 🌺

As the days passed, Manuela and Melvin continued with their cold attitude, making fun of Mangé whenever they could, making him feel rejected. Thus, Mangé, instead of trying to adapt, began to highlight his customs with more arrogance. "In my orchard, the fruits have their own space and don't mix with the vegetables. And we also have our own rules of coexistence, much more refined than what I see here."

The tension grew in the garden. While Carlota tried to get everyone to give Mangé a chance, Melvin became increasingly annoyed with his attitude. "If you like your old orchard so much, I don't know why you came here," he snapped one day. 😠

Mangé felt a sting inside. He didn't want to admit it, but he had left his orchard because he didn't feel accepted there. He had been different from the other mangoes, more curious and less interested in following the strict rules of his home. But instead of telling the truth, he simply walked away without answering. 😞

It was Carlota who, as always, had the patience to understand what was happening. One afternoon, she found him sitting under a large sunflower, with a lost look and slumped shoulders. Mangé was distractedly drawing lines in the dirt with a dry leaf, as if trying to find answers on the ground. 🌻

Carlota sat down next to him, silently at first, giving him space to talk. Finally, in a faint voice, Mangé murmured: "Sometimes I wonder if I really fit in anywhere. I try to show that I'm worthwhile, but it seems that the more I try, the more rejection I provoke..."

Carlota gave him a sympathetic look and said: "Mangé, I know it's difficult to adapt to a new place, but you don't have to prove anything. Just be yourself. You're not alone, let us really get to know you." 😊

Mangé sighed and commented: "It's just that I don't feel welcome. And when I'm rejected, the only thing that comes out of me is to show that my customs are better... although deep down I don't know if I really believe it." 😔
Carlota smiled and added: "Look, every place has its good things. Why don't you teach us some of your customs, and we'll teach you ours?" 😄

Mangé accepted. The next day, he organized a great tasting with the flavors of his orchard: exotic combinations that resulted in sweets that surprised everyone. In return, the inhabitants of the garden taught him their traditions: the games, the songs, and the cooperation that made the garden such a special place. 🍍🍓

Little by little, Mangé began to feel part of the community. And Melvin, seeing that he had been acting just like those who had once rejected him and Carlota, reflected and was the first to apologize. "I guess I had a hard time accepting someone new... But you have great things to contribute." 🙂
Manuela, although with some reluctance, ended up accepting Mangé too, although not without uttering her classic: "Well, I guess a little exoticism wouldn't hurt the garden..."
From then on, the enchanted garden was not only a place of peace and friendship, but also of diversity. And so, with fruits and vegetables learning from each other, everyone grew a little more. 🌈

On the stage, the light is soft, welcoming, as if the air were illuminated by tiny invisible candles ✨. Two figures slowly appear in the center, a pair of dancers. The initial silence seems to breathe with them, until a soft sound, almost whispered, begins to fill the room.

It’s a cello, deep and warm, born like a shy murmur, resonating in their bodies. Sarah closes her eyes, and David tilts his head slightly, letting himself be guided by the musical caress. Their hands slowly reach for each other, and as soon as they touch, the music seems to vibrate in their skin, guiding their first soft, fluid, almost floating movements 🎻.

The melody slowly grows, expanding like a delicate wave, and now a piano joins in, clear and crystalline, tracing tiny sonic stars on the deep cloak of the cello. Their bodies respond instantly, flexible, playing with gravity, intertwining gently like branches moved by a nocturnal breeze 🌌.

A violin, sweet and nostalgic, joins the dance. Emotions begin to fill them completely. Each note vibrates in their muscles, in their bones, in their synchronized breaths. They rise together, Sarah supported by David, light as a feather, descending in a spiral as the music caresses every corner of the room 🎶.

The intensity keeps rising; a soft and constant percussion appears, marking the rhythm of their accelerated hearts. The dancers are in a trance, feeling every beat, every joint breath. Their movements become more powerful, passionate, but always in harmony, always united by invisible threads woven by the music 💓.
The music reaches its climax. Instruments and bodies seem to merge in an eternal instant of strength and emotion. Sarah twirls, David holds her firm, safe, with absolute confidence.
Then, slowly, like a tide receding, the music begins to lose intensity 🎼.

The instruments say goodbye gently, one by one. First the percussion, leaving a subtle echo in the air. Then the violin, slowly retreating, saying goodbye with tenderness. The piano whispers its last notes, leaving only the cello again, which returns to its initial sweetness. The dancers' bodies now flow more slowly, as if floating in warm water, relaxing with each note that disappears into the room 🌙.

Finally, Sarah reclines on the stage, and David follows, wrapping her in his arms in a soft and warm embrace. Their synchronized breaths reveal the sweet tiredness that invades their bodies. Sarah slowly moves her arms, as if she wanted to reach the music that still floats around them 🤗.

The cello sighs its last note, delicately fading until it merges with the absolute silence. The dancers remain lying down, together, motionless, surrendered to the deep rest that follows the lived intensity. The curtain slowly falls, enveloping them in the most absolute stillness 🎭.

Aura was in the main room of the official facilities. The space had a clean and serene atmosphere, with walls and furniture made of a white polymer with a ceramic finish, smooth to the touch and with rounded shapes, without visible joints. The soft light that entered through the large windows glided over the pearly surfaces, highlighting their subtly nacreous finish. Everything seemed designed to be functional, but at the same time welcoming, with an unexpected warmth in a technological environment. In front of her, Mara activated a holographic screen that projected three-dimensional images of gleaming structures.

—We have made tremendous progress, Aura —began Mara with a proud smile—. During your stay on the moon, our team here was analyzing in depth the exact chemical composition of the corrosive sand. We discovered that it is mainly formed by particles containing high concentrations of alkaline sulfates and highly reactive metallic fluorides. When they come into contact with the synthetic and metallic materials that we brought from Earth, these compounds cause a rapid chemical reaction, generating acids that corrode and deteriorate our structures almost immediately.
Aura frowned slightly, trying to grasp all the technical information. Mara caught her expression and decided to simplify the explanation.

—To put it more simply: imagine that the sand contains very aggressive substances that react with everything we brought from Earth, rapidly decomposing it. Thanks to the research carried out on the moon on the properties of Tantalum, we have been able to create a very special new alloy, combining that metal with the Veridite we found here. This new formula is resistant to corrosion, because Veridite neutralizes the destructive chemical reactions, something similar to what occurs naturally in local organisms.
Aura nodded with genuine admiration. She was fascinated by how her mother and the scientific team managed to transform each challenge into an opportunity for learning and improvement.

At that moment, one of the room's gates slid open with a soft buzz, giving way to a tall and robust man, with a graying beard and an affable expression. Aura recognized him instantly, although she had barely interacted with him. She remembered that, during the journey in the ship, he had given them a lecture on the construction of structures respectful of the environment. He had always transmitted a sense of calm and confidence to her, but there was something more in him. The age marked on his face and the golden flecks that shone in his dark eyes gave him an air of serene wisdom, as if he saw beyond the obvious.

—Aura, you already know Dorian. He is leading the planning of a new base site, ensuring that the area is sustainable and better adapted to the conditions of the planet —explained Mara, approaching him with a smile that reflected years of collaboration and professional respect—. With the new materials, we will build more resistant structures in harmony with the environment. I want you to accompany him in the supervision of the new module area and learn everything you can from him.
—I will —replied Aura, feeling a spark of enthusiasm for having real responsibilities.

That same afternoon, Aura shared the news about the new constructions with Isaac. He listened to her without paying too much attention, until suddenly an idea crossed his mind. He looked at Aura with enthusiasm and commented spontaneously:
—What if we take advantage and move in together when the constructions are finished?
Aura felt a shiver of emotion. She smiled widely and nodded without hesitation.
—I'll tell my mother as soon as I see her.

However, that night Mara returned late to the compartment. By then, Aura was already sound asleep. They didn't coincide the following morning either. When Aura woke up, her mother had already left, starting her activities early as usual, before most of the colonists began their shifts.

With a sense of urgency in her chest, she dressed quickly and headed to the community dining room, but barely tasted a bite. Her stomach was too shrunken by anxiety. Although the idea of moving in with Isaac filled her with emotion, she knew that her mother would not approve of it easily. She saw it coming. She could imagine the conversation, Mara's arguments, the worried tone she would adopt.

She nibbled her toast listlessly, drumming her fingers on the table impatiently. She glanced sideways every time someone entered the dining room, hoping to see her appear, but the constant flow of hurried colonists only increased her frustration. When she finished her infusion, she decided that she couldn't wait any longer. She left the tray in the cleaning area and headed directly to her new assignment. Arriving at the work area, she found Dorian leaning over a control table, reviewing a holographic map of the terrain. The bluish glow of the projection illuminated his concentrated face as he slid his fingers across the floating images, organizing the plans for the day.

—Aura! Good morning. Come, come closer. Look at the formations of the terrain; it is essential to take them into account. Remember that we don't just build. We observe, we listen, we respect. We are integrating ourselves into the planet, not the other way around —he said in a serene voice as he unfolded the interactive map of the new site.

Just at that moment, Mara entered the room and stopped for a moment when she saw Aura next to Dorian, watching with a silent smile how they interacted. Aura, noticing her presence, felt a lurch in her chest. Without hesitation, she approached her and, with her heart racing, seized the opportunity to tell her about her plans with Isaac.
—Move in with Isaac? —Mara paled for an instant, but her expression quickly hardened—. I don't think it's a good idea.
Aura clenched her fists, feeling the frustration building inside her.
—Mom, I need to live my life. On this damn planet it seems that I always have to be under your shadow.
—It's not my shadow that worries you, but that I don't let you do whatever you want —replied Mara seriously—. And, in this case, I have reasons to worry.
Aura snorted, crossing her arms.
—You always find a reason to be against Isaac.
—Because I don't like how your relationship affects you —replied Mara bluntly—. And you know it.
—You don't know anything, Mom —blurted Aura furiously, her voice trembling—. You can't decide for me.
Mara held her gaze, firm but less sharp.
—No, but I'm not going to pretend it's the best idea in the world either.
The silence that settled between them was thick. Finally, Mara sighed and shook her head.

—Do what you think is right. I just hope that, if things go wrong, you don't turn away from those of us who really care about you. If you want to live with Isaac, we'll prepare one of the living quarters for you.
Without adding more, she turned to leave the room. Before leaving, she exchanged a worried look with Dorian, who was observing discreetly from a distance.

Hours later, when she completed her workday, Aura ran to inform Isaac that, finally, Mara had accepted. She barely finished the sentence, Isaac hugged her enthusiastically, lifting her off the ground with ease. Aura felt the firmness of his arms around her, the security that his contact always transmitted to her. When he put her back on the ground, he gave her a radiant smile, the one that made her stomach flip.
—I knew you would get it —he murmured, with that tone of absolute certainty that made everything seem easier.
Aura felt a wave of emotion run through her, but before she could respond, Liam appeared, smiling as always.
—Hi, Aura! Hey, are you coming later? Some friends and I are going to play in the simulator with a new forest adventure update.
Aura, instinctively, looked at Isaac before answering. This gesture did not go unnoticed by Liam.
—Aura doesn't need to ask your permission, right? —said Liam with a relaxed but firm smile.
—It's not that —Aura hastened to say, feeling the heat rise to her cheeks—. I just... wanted to see if we already had other plans.
Liam raised an eyebrow.
—Count me in —added Aura quickly.
Liam nodded pleased and walked away calmly. When they were alone, Isaac exploded with an unexpected rage.
—Do you always have to make me look bad in front of your friends? —he said raising his voice, with a dark glint in his eyes.
—I'm not making you look bad. I simply don't need permission to do something, right? —replied Aura trying to stay calm.
—You haven't taken me into account for your plans! I wanted us to celebrate the good news. You haven't even told your friend, it seems like you don't care about anything related to me!
Isaac hit the nearest wall hard, causing Aura to step back instinctively. Without saying another word, Isaac stormed off down the hall, leaving Aura frozen.
Isaac, striding, took refuge in his quarters. He closed the door with a brusque movement and, without stopping to think, activated a video communication with Zoe.
She responded almost immediately, with a soft smile, but her eyebrows rose slightly, reflecting her surprise at the call.
—Isaac? What a surprise! —Zoe looked up from her terminal and smiled as she carefully picked up the creature that was resting curled up next to her—. I was reviewing the behavior of the Quivelis.

She held in her arms a small specimen, similar in size to a fox, with a silky coat that ranged between turquoise and bluish tones, speckled in soft silver. Feeling that it was being lifted, the animal stretched its legs instinctively, unfolding the translucent membranes that allowed it to glide. Zoe smiled and brought it closer to her face with an almost automatic gesture, brushing her nose against the animal's in a brief but affectionate caress.
—I introduce you to Lúnir —she said in a low voice—. He is especially sensitive today.
The Quivelis let out a soft gurgle, squinting its large dark eyes with golden pupils, while showing its gleaming teeth in an affectionate grimace.
Isaac sighed heavily, running a hand through his hair, his brow furrowed in a way that seemed almost theatrical.
—Are you okay? —asked Zoe, tilting her head with a hint of caution in her voice—. You seem… upset.
Isaac clicked his tongue with frustration and rested his elbows on the table, burying his face in his hands before looking at her again.
—I argued with Aura. She doesn't understand me, Zoe. No matter how much I do for her, she always finds a way to push me aside.
Zoe swallowed. She felt a pang of guilt intertwined with something harder to admit. Her chest tightened.
—Aura can be very stubborn, but she just needs time. Be patient with her —she said in a low voice, striving to sound neutral.
Isaac let out a short, bitter laugh.
—It's always the same. "Be patient, Isaac," "Understand her, Isaac." And who is patient with me? Who understands me?
Zoe felt the air get heavier. She lowered her gaze for an instant and distractedly stroked the soft fur of Lúnir, who seemed to capture her agitation.
—Isaac… —she began, but he interrupted her.

—You're the only person who really listens to me, Zoe —he said in a lower, more intimate tone. His expression softened slightly, and his gaze locked on hers—. With you I don't have to explain myself, I don't have to fight to be understood. I just… exist.
Zoe felt her heart accelerate, a mixture of euphoria and danger throbbing in her chest.
—That's not true —she murmured, trying to smile, although her voice sounded insecure—. Aura loves you.
Isaac shook his head slowly.
—I wish Aura valued me as you do.
The silence that remained between them lengthened, thick. Zoe felt the warmth of Lúnir against her body, as if the little Quivelis perceived the tension and tried to soothe her.
—Thank you, Zoe. Really —continued Isaac, with a warm, almost sweet tone—. I don't know what I would do without you.
Before she could respond, the connection was cut off.

Zoe blinked, as if she had just come out of a trance. She remained motionless, her gaze fixed on the empty space where, seconds before, Isaac's image had been. Her breathing was slow, contained, as if she feared that moving too much would make her face what she had just felt.
Lúnir watched her from her lap, with its ears slightly tilted back. The little Quivelis fluttered its membranous wings with an almost imperceptible beat, reflecting its owner's unease.
Zoe slid her fingers through its fur without thinking.

—What am I going to do, Lúnir? —she whispered, feeling how the weight in her chest did not disappear completely, but at least became bearable—. I like Isaac so much, but... I can't do this to Aura, she's my friend.
Lúnir emitted a soft gurgle, tilting its head with curiosity before unfolding its wings slowly, wrapping her in an instinctive gesture of comfort.

Zoe closed her eyes and rested her forehead on the warm body of the Quivelis. The paused breathing of the little being appeased her for a moment, as if the simple contact could alleviate the tangle of emotions that gripped her.
—Thank you, my friend —she whispered, feeling how the weight in her chest did not disappear completely, but at least became bearable—. Maybe someday I'll tell her everything.
The animal rubbed gently against her skin.
—But now, I just… can't.

Later, although she didn't feel completely cheerful, Aura decided to accompany Liam to the virtual simulator. She wasn't sure if it was what she needed, but she didn't want to be alone with her thoughts either.

Arriving, she was pleasantly surprised to see that Alexia and Derek were also there, with whom she had not shared any activity for some time. The simulator room projected a wooded environment, with trees with twisted trunks that swayed with an almost real virtual breeze. The interface responded precisely to each of their movements, enveloping them in an immersive experience where the fog floated among the roots and the air smelled of damp earth.

During the first few minutes, Aura remained silent and distant, simply following the others through the simulated thickness. However, little by little, the dynamics of the game and the complicity of the group managed to dissipate part of the tension that oppressed her. Alexia joked about the hidden traps on the path, Derek impulsively threw himself against the challenges without thinking twice, and Liam, with his carefree attitude, encouraged her to move forward.
By the time the game ended, Aura no longer felt so trapped in her own head.
Back to the residential area, Liam walked beside her, with his hands in his pockets.
—Are you okay? —he asked, giving her a friendly nudge with his elbow.
Aura sighed deeply before answering.
—I argued with Isaac —she admitted—. I think my mother might be right about some things...
Liam looked at her seriously, but without losing his understanding tone.

—Aura, in case you haven't realized what I think about Isaac yet, I think he's not good for you —he said frankly—, but it's you who has to realize it. I just want you to know that, when that happens, I'll be here to support you.
Aura held his gaze for an instant before smiling with gratitude.
Arriving in front of her quarters, she saw Isaac waiting for her at the door. Liam said goodbye to her with a warm hug that Isaac observed with evident displeasure, although he tried to hide it.
Isaac waited for Liam to leave before approaching.

—Aura, sorry about before —he began, softening his voice—. I shouldn't have reacted like that, but sometimes I don't know how to control myself when I see that you don't take me into account. You know how much it affects me that you don't value my feelings.
Aura remained silent, feeling how guilt was slowly settling in her chest.
—I'm sorry, Aura —continued Isaac, with a soft but firm tone—. I wish you understood how much you hurt me when you do things like that.

Aura lowered her gaze, confused and unable to respond. Something inside her warned her that what Isaac was saying was not entirely correct, but she could not find what it was. The sensation was uncomfortable, as if she was trying to hold sand between her fingers. In the end, she surrendered to his yearning gaze.
—Forgive me, Isaac, I didn't want you to feel that way.
He drew her towards him, wrapping her with his body, making her lose herself in the sensation of warmth and protection that always disarmed her, suffocating any doubt that had tried to arise.
—It's okay —whispered Isaac in her ear, his voice sliding like an electric touch on her skin—. When we live together everything will be easier.

Aura barely had time to process his words before he kissed her. She rose on tiptoe without thinking, letting herself be carried away by the intensity of the moment. Isaac held her firmly, his hands holding her face with the precision of someone who knows exactly what he is doing.
When they separated, his eyes shone with that intoxicating intensity that only he possessed.
—Good night, my love —he murmured, waiting for her to close the gate.

Aura was left with that mixture of feelings once again. With the warmth of the kiss still latent on her lips, she felt how much she loved Isaac, but she was also filled with that persistent pang, that silenced certainty that something was not as it should be.

Lily spent hours with her colored pencils, filling page after page with all sorts of drawings, like animals, landscapes, and fantastical creatures. She had a boundless imagination and loved bringing it to life on paper.

One rainy afternoon, her dad came home from work with a box of pencils in metallic shades. While he made her an after-school snack, Lily couldn't resist trying them out and immediately thought of the best thing she could draw with them: dragons.

Excited, she took a blank sheet of paper and ran her fingers over the texture of the new pencils. She imagined the vibrant colors gliding across the page and, without hesitating, began to create. First, she drew a small green dragon that she imagined would change color with its mood if it were real. Then, a long, bubblegum-pink one that would fly so fast you could barely see it in the sky. After that, an orange one with big wings that would shoot out golden sparks when it roared. The more she imagined them, the more real they seemed.

When she finished her third dragon, she put down her pencil and sighed with satisfaction. But then, something incredible happened. The drawings began to tremble gently on the paper, as if an invisible gust of wind were rustling them. Lily watched with wide eyes as the figures lifted off the page in a dance of light and movement. The dragons now fluttered around her, light as air, but as real as if they had always existed.

Fascinated, she spent the afternoon creating new dragons: black and yellow ones, some with rounded scales, others with enormous eyes or long horns. Each one lifted off her drawings and, with great excitement, played with each other or perched on her hands and shoulders. But then, a new idea crossed her mind. She decided to create a different kind of dragon, a mysterious and strong one with an imposing presence. She imagined it to be independent, able to take care of itself, and needing no one. She picked up the red pencil and drew a slender body with pointy, gold-tipped scales, wide wings, and intense eyes.

When she finished, she waited excitedly for the dragon to awaken. This dragon, however, was different. It didn't flutter about curiously or come close to her like the others. Instead, it remained still for a few seconds, watching her with a mistrustful gaze. Then, without warning, the dragon powerfully flapped its wings, pulled away, and before Lily could react, it shot out the open window, escaping into the darkness outside.

Lily ran after it, but the dragon had already disappeared into the overcast sky. She spent the whole night worrying. What if it rains harder and the dragon's paper gets ruined? What if it never comes back? A tightness of sadness squeezed her chest.

The next day, she decided to do something about it. She sat under her favorite tree in the park and began to draw. This time, she imagined a large, kind dragon of a deep blue, with eyes full of intelligence and understanding. As she created it, she whispered to the drawing:
—I need your help.
The blue dragon came to life and rose gracefully into the air. Lily watched in amazement as it elegantly beat its wings and flew off in search of the runaway dragon.

She didn't have to wait long. From the branches of a nearby tree, the red dragon suddenly appeared, with the same mistrustful look as before. But when the blue dragon landed beside it, something changed. For the first time, the lonely dragon didn't flee. It watched Lily in silence, as if it were waiting for something.

Lily understood what had happened. She had created a dragon without giving it a purpose, without a connection to her or anyone else. She took out her sketchbook and carefully drew a detail on its chest: a golden heart, shining like the sun.

The red dragon blinked, confused, and then something inside it seemed to calm down. Its wings stopped moving nervously, and its eyes no longer seemed so distant. It slowly approached Lily and, with a faint crinkle of paper, curled up on her arm.
—Now you can love, too —Lily whispered with a smile.

The dragon, while still independent and a bit of a loner, had understood that strength didn't have to mean being without affection. Now it knew it could fly free while still enjoying the company of those who cared for it from time to time. From then on, the paper dragons continued to soar through the sky, each with its own story, but all connected by the heart of little Lily.

132.t: Emma and the Mystery of the Talking Mirrors
p: In the Kingdom of Luminaris, a most unusual problem broke out: shiny, chatty, and completely unexpected.

It all began one morning when Princess Emma woke with a start. An endless murmur filled her room. Pipo, her inseparable friend and tiny rabbit, peeked his head out of her special pocket, also bewildered. Emma rubbed her eyes and looked around. No one was there… except for her mirror.
—Good morning, Your Highness!— the mirror exclaimed enthusiastically.
Emma jumped up in bed, her eyes wide. From her special pocket, Pipo’s ears popped up, and he blinked in amazement at what they had just heard.

—Oh! I'm sorry if I woke you, but I couldn't help myself. You're shining with your own special light today, Princess!— the mirror continued, its reflection wobbling instead of staying still like always.
Emma blinked. It wasn't every day that a mirror gave you a compliment when you woke up.

But the surprise didn't end there. When Emma left her room, she discovered that all the mirrors in the castle were talking nonstop. Some were laughing, others were arguing about who had the best reflection, and others simply wouldn't stop giving advice on fashion and hairstyles. The mirrors had come to life, and the castle was in chaos. The servants couldn't do their jobs, the guards couldn't concentrate, and even the cook had received complaints about her reflection.
Queen Margarita held her head, exhausted.

—Emma, something magical has happened. The mirrors have come to life, and the castle is in chaos. Even the mirror in the great hall has refused to reflect people because it says it doesn't like the furniture and won't work like this!— the queen sighed.

Emma knew she had to step in. She took a deep breath, feeling the responsibility to restore calm to the castle. She adjusted her purple cape with determination and looked at Pipo, who nodded enthusiastically, ready for an adventure.
—We have to solve this!— she said with determination.

With her bubblegum sword in hand, the princess began her investigation. She went around asking the mirrors what had happened, but each one had a different version of the story. It was clear that none of them really knew, but they didn't want to leave the princess without an answer.
The Hallway Mirror claimed it all started when a mysterious reflection appeared in it and whispered a spell.
The dining room mirror insisted that someone had spoken in an unknown language in front of it the night before.
And the mirror in the great hall only said:
—I will not speak with a princess who doesn't wear her crown properly. Fashion is important!
Emma sighed. If she wanted answers, she had to find another way to get them.
She decided to go to the Enchanted Library, where the old librarian, Alarico, usually helped with the most ancient knowledge.

—A spell on the mirrors?— Alarico muttered, flipping through a dusty book. —Ah, here it is! It's the 'Spell of the Restless Reflections.' It's activated when someone says a series of magic words in front of a mirror. The reflection's energy comes to life and begins to speak and act on its own. To deactivate it, the same person must say the same series of words again.
—But who activated it?— Emma asked.
—Perhaps the first mirror that spoke has the answer,— the librarian suggested, as he copied the magic words to deactivate the enchantment onto a piece of paper:
Living light, echo straying, reflection free, now start saying.
Emma put the paper in her special pocket, in Pipo's care, ran back to her room, and stared at her mirror.
—Try to concentrate, my dear old mirror. Who caused this?
The mirror hesitated and then confessed:
—It was… it was Prince Lior. He appeared in our kingdom last night, somehow filling all of us mirrors with energy. I think he's looking for a way back to his world.
—Prince Lior?— Emma repeated, raising an eyebrow.
—He's a young prince from the Crystal Kingdom,— the mirror whispered. —He seems quite sad, but he must not know how to get back.

Emma understood there was only one way to fix everything: she had to help Prince Lior return to his kingdom and face his destiny. She placed her hand on the surface of her mirror, which rippled like the water of a lake, and with one last breath, she jumped inside.

The other side was astonishing: a brilliant world where everything was a reflection of the real world, but slightly twisted. The streets seemed to be made of liquid glass and floated in the air, reflecting skies of changing colors. Emma began to walk cautiously, feeling how the ground beneath her feet seemed to vibrate with every step.

Suddenly, a group of silvery shadows emerged from the reflections of the buildings. They were silhouettes that mimicked her movements, but with a slight delay, as if they were imperfect copies. One of them, larger than the rest, stepped forward and spoke with an echoing voice.
—You are not from here,— the shadow said. —Only those who have lost their reflection are trapped in this world.
Emma stood firm, with Pipo clinging to her pocket.
—I'm looking for Prince Lior. I know he's here, and I need to find him,— she said.

The shadows looked at each other and then pointed to a crystal tower in the distance. —If you seek answers, the Tower of Lost Reflections is the only way. But be careful. Some who enter… don't always manage to get out.

Emma felt a knot in her stomach and clenched her fists. Her heart was pounding, but a spark of excitement shone in her eyes. "If this is the way, then let's go," she whispered, starting to walk with Pipo holding on tight in her pocket.

As she climbed the crystal stairs, her reflection on the walls moved independently, sometimes imitating her gestures and other times acting as if it had a will of its own, making her feel unsure of her steps and lose her balance many times. Finally, at the top, she found Prince Lior, sitting on a gleaming platform, frustrated and thoughtful. Noticing her presence, the young man looked up, his eyes reflecting surprise.
—Who are you?— he asked cautiously.
—I am Emma, princess of Luminaris,— she replied confidently. —I've come to find you because the entire kingdom is in an uproar over your reflection, and I think you need help.

—Emma!— he exclaimed. —I didn't mean to cause trouble. I just wanted a simpler life… but now I'm trapped. I thought if I crossed into the Reflected World, I could live without worries and let someone else take my place. But being here all alone, I realized it wasn't a good idea. Besides, I forgot the words to return.

Emma took out the paper with the magic words and held it out to him solemnly. Lior took it with trembling hands, feeling the weight of his decision. He looked at Emma with gratitude and a spark of determination in his eyes, aware that this was the moment to face what he had left behind.
—Running away from responsibilities is never the solution,— she said with a smile. —But we all need help sometimes. Come on, let's go back together.
Lior took the paper, whispered the words, and in a flash of light, they both reappeared in their rooms, in their respective kingdoms.

The castle mirrors stopped talking, and everything went back to normal. The servants and inhabitants of the castle, who had spent hours on end with incessant advice about their hairstyles and manners, sighed with relief. Queen Margarita smiled as she saw calm return, while the guards looked at their reflections in silence, enjoying the sudden peace.
Weeks later, Emma received a beautifully wrapped package. Inside were some magical sparkling gummies and a letter from Prince Lior.

“Thank you for your help, Emma. You've taught me that facing problems is better than running from them. As a token of my gratitude, here is a little spell. If you ever miss a good conversation, say ‘Gleaming reflection, voice so bright’ while holding this letter in your hand, and your mirror will talk to you again.”
Emma smiled and carefully put the letter away. She knew this wouldn't be her last adventure.
And with a rhyme and a cheer, this enchanted story ends right here. ✨

In Silence Valley, a magical calm always reigned. There, the flowers grew in unique colors, the trees whispered ancient secrets, and the inhabitants of Whisperville lived in complete harmony. Whisperville was known for being a silent town, because, according to legends, any loud noise could awaken the dreaded dragon Dorvax, who slept deeply under Cloudy Mountain.

Everyone in Whisperville was happy living gently and respectfully, except for a young boy named Brian, known in the village for his peculiar ability to create musical instruments from anything he found. Brian dreamed of playing his creations and filling the valley with the music he felt inside, but he was always forbidden for fear of the dragon.

One morning, Brian was walking near the Twinklewood Forest looking for new materials when he stumbled upon a small creature he had never seen before. It looked like a fox, but it was bright blue and had large silver eyes. Surprised, Brian asked:
—Who are you, little creature?
—I am Azure, the last of the Melodians. I have traveled far and wide looking for someone capable of returning music to the valley—replied the creature with a soft, musical voice.

Brian was thrilled to hear this. He had heard old stories about the Melodians, beings who could sing melodies capable of healing wounds and awakening joy in any heart. But he also knew that the dragon Dorvax would not tolerate any sound.
—I would love to help you, Azure, but it is forbidden to make music here. Dorvax could wake up and destroy Whisperville—said Brian sadly.
—What if Dorvax is not what he seems? Perhaps the music is not the problem, but the type of sounds that are made—suggested Azure mysteriously.

Intrigued and full of doubts, Brian decided to trust his new friend. Together they entered the Twinklewood Forest, searching for the ancient Temple of Harmony, where they could find answers about Dorvax.
Upon arriving at the temple, covered by vines and forgotten by time, Azure guided Brian to an ancient inscription:
"Music that is born from the heart will never awaken anger, but kindness."
Brian then understood that perhaps the legend was wrong. Music was not dangerous if it came from noble and pure feelings.

For days, Brian and Azure carefully prepared a special instrument: a flute made with wood from the Serene Tree, decorated with luminous petals from the Aurora Lily. Finally, when it was ready, Brian stood in the middle of the valley and, breathing deeply, began to play.

The melody was soft, tender, and full of love. Little by little, the inhabitants of Whisperville came out of their houses, fearful at first, but soon fascinated by the wonderful music they were hearing for the first time.

However, a deep roar arose from the bowels of Cloudy Mountain. Dorvax had awakened. The Whispervillians began to hide, terrified, but Brian continued playing, trusting in the inscription of the temple.

Dorvax appeared before everyone, huge and majestic, with scales that reflected the colors of the dawn. But, to everyone's surprise, the dragon did not attack. On the contrary, he began to move slowly to the rhythm of the flute, until silver tears rolled down his face.
—For centuries—said Dorvax in a deep but sweet voice—, I have slept restlessly, tormented by the absence of pure melodies. I could only be awakened by sincere music full of kindness.
The inhabitants then understood that they had been wrong to believe that all sound was dangerous. Music was not an enemy, but should always be born from the heart.

From that day on, Silence Valley changed its name to Harmony Valley. Music returned to fill every corner of Whisperville, and Brian became the most beloved musician in the village, always accompanied by Azure, the last Melodian.
And so, they discovered together that when we act from kindness and with sincerity, no fear can overshadow our dreams.
Moral: Sincerity and kindness have the power to transform fear into joy and harmony. 💖

Many, many years ago, in a medieval village called Sillyville, lived a boy named Danny Calamity. He was called that because not a day went by without him causing some kind of commotion. If the grown-ups said not to touch something, Danny touched it; if they told him not to go somewhere, he snuck in anyway. He thought adults were boring and exaggerated everything, and that he always knew better.

One day, a wise old man named Mr. Theodore arrived in town. He had a long, white beard, a cherry-colored robe, and walked slowly, leaning on a crooked cane. Mr. Theodore carried with him a mysterious book that he consulted constantly and claimed to know the solution to any problem.

Everyone in Sillyville listened attentively to Mr. Theodore's advice—everyone except Danny, who insisted it was all nonsense. One sunny afternoon, Danny overheard the old man warning about the old abandoned well on the outskirts of town, known as the Wise Well.
—That well has been dry for years, and no one should approach it—said the wise man—, for although it seems harmless, it hides a danger that only the elders know.
—Bah!—Danny laughed—. Another boring invention to keep us from having fun.

Driven by curiosity and his desire to prove he was right, Danny headed determinedly toward the well. When he arrived, he saw that it was a pretty normal well, covered in moss and loose stones. It didn't seem dangerous.
—I knew it, another exaggeration—he scoffed.
However, as he peered inside, he heard a small voice from the bottom:
—Psst! Hey, Danny! Down here!

Surprised, he leaned in a little more. Suddenly, he lost his balance, and whoosh! he fell into the well. But instead of hitting the ground, he landed softly in a magical room filled with mirrors that shone with a thousand colors.
In the center was a little elf with pointy ears and a mischievous smile, named Sparky.
—Welcome, Danny! I've been waiting centuries for someone as clever as you—said Sparky with a mocking giggle.
—Where am I? I want to get out!—Danny protested, scared.
—Relax, you just have to solve three riddles—replied Sparky—. Didn't you always say adults exaggerated? Well, prove to me that you know more than them.
Danny accepted, confident in himself. But each riddle proved more difficult than the last. The more he tried to solve them alone, the more confused and frustrated he became.
Finally, defeated and desperate, Danny remembered Mr. Theodore's words and realized that maybe the grown-ups were right after all. So, humbly, he asked Sparky:
—Can I ask for help?
Sparky nodded, satisfied. As soon as Danny acknowledged that he needed advice, the old man Mr. Theodore magically appeared in the room.
—We all make mistakes, Danny—Theodore said to him affectionately—. It's not about knowing more, but about listening carefully and learning from those who have experience.
Following the wise man's advice, Danny finally solved the riddles, and the room filled with light. Sparky clapped cheerfully:
—You've understood, Danny! Always remember this day.

Danny returned to the village a more sensible boy, but just as cheerful. From then on, he listened carefully to the warnings of his elders, not out of fear, but because he understood that their experience was a valuable treasure.
And Sillyville became a peaceful place again, though it never stopped being fun, especially thanks to Danny Calamity, who now shared his adventures with prudence and respect. 😊

135.t: The Mystery of the Dancing Bubbles
p: In the floating kingdom of Pompalia, a secret place hidden among the clouds, lived friendly little beings called Bubblies. They were small, fluffy, and changed color depending on their mood. Everyone lived happily, feeding on laughter and dancing on soft, bouncy clouds. But there was one problem: whenever a Bubblie got angry, it would turn gray and heavy, and stop floating.

One day, Pip, a mischievous, bright orange Bubblie, argued with his best friend, Lily, because he didn't want to share his favorite cloud. His anger was so big that Pip turned gray and heavy, falling down to the lower layers of the kingdom. He tried to float with all his might, but he couldn't. Finally, he landed on a strange, dark cloud with no music.
There he met Grumbles, an old Bubblie who had been trapped for years, always angry and grumbling nonstop.
Pip, scared at first, decided to ask him what had happened.
—A long time ago, I got mad at my friends over silly things and didn't know how to say sorry,— Grumbles confessed sadly. —I've been here ever since, all alone and heavy.
Pip realized he had made the same mistake with Lily. Determined not to end up like Grumbles, he suggested a plan for them to return home together.
—Dancing!— exclaimed Pip. —Music and dancing always make us happy and light. Let's try it!

At first, Grumbles grumbled, but seeing the little Bubblie's hopeful face, he decided to give it a try. They began to move slowly to the rhythm of the distant laughter from Pompalia. Little by little, they both got their color back, becoming lighter and lighter. Suddenly, hundreds of colorful bubbles surrounded them, floating and dancing along with them, guiding them back to the heart of the kingdom.

When they arrived, Pip ran to hug Lily, apologizing for being selfish. She apologized too for arguing. Grumbles, upon seeing his old friends again, understood that it was never too late to make things right. From that day on, everyone in Pompalia remembered that a good dance and a sincere apology can bring the color back to any gray Bubblie.

136.t: The Awakening of Bella the Butterfly
p: Snug and warm, in a hidden nook among the leaves of the forest's lushest tree, she sleeps. It's a light, warm, and comfortable sleep, where nothing can disturb her tranquility. She's protected by soft walls, delicately woven, that embrace her with sweetness.

She breathes slowly, feeling the gentle movement of her small body, which, little by little, is transforming. Each day she wakes up a little different, perceiving subtle tickles running through her tiny body, as if a thousand tiny paintbrushes were caressing her slowly.

Time passes slowly, very slowly, but she enjoys it in that cozy twilight that lulls her. One day, she opens her small eyes. She doesn't see clearly, but she knows that something wonderful awaits her outside. She perceives the light, diffused, delicate, filtering through her silk walls. She feels how the warmth of the sun begins to gently knock on her door.

As the days pass, the need to move grows inside her. She stretches timidly, stretching her body slowly, enjoying each new muscle that she now feels awake and alive. She notices beautiful changes in herself, although she doesn't yet know what they are.

Finally, a different morning arrives. Her refuge, which was so warm and protective, now seems too narrow. With delicacy, she pushes and opens a small opening. A fresh and fragrant breeze caresses her face for the first time, filling her with immense joy.

She propels herself gently outward, instinctively extending her body, now light and full of grace. She feels that something new and beautiful extends on both sides of her. The sunlight envelops her, warm and bright, as she discovers the world for the first time.

Without the walls that held her, she can stretch her whole body, starting with her back, which she moves in all the directions she can, feeling its flexibility, how her body lengthens. Then her legs, one by one, noticing that energy passes through them all as she stretches them. She touches her face softly, recognizing the delicate and light texture of her antennae, and finally, she decides to take care of the great novelty she has on her back.

She begins to unfold, little by little, some enormous and velvety wings. She doesn't yet know how to use them and they are weak, so she makes small movements to prepare them, up and down, making sure that the sun bathes them completely with its warmth.

Finally, she is ready. She begins to flap her wings gently and lightly and jumps off the branch she was on. She feels how she can play in the air, how she no longer depends only on her little legs to move.

And then, she approaches the crystal-clear water that flows calmly next to the tree. As she peers timidly, she sees a wonderful figure reflected, full of color and beauty. She stops to observe, marveling at what she sees, and realizes that, at last, she has become a butterfly. This is Bella, the butterfly.

In a quiet, ordinary forest lived Lily, a very observant and calm squirrel. All the animals enjoyed this place full of peace and harmony, although there was someone no one wanted to cross paths with: Susan, an owl who always seemed angry. She grumbled about everything, scolded for no apparent reason, and often argued with anyone who passed near her tree.
Lily, however, was very curious about Susan. She watched from afar how the owl, always alone or arguing, seemed to carry a great burden.
One day, walking distractedly near Susan's big tree, Lily heard a loud screech:
—Hey! You're stepping on my clovers!—shouted the owl angrily.
—I'm so sorry, Susan! I didn't realize it—replied Lily politely.
The next day, Lily wanted to apologize and left a small nutshell as a pot in front of Susan's door, with a beautiful clover planted inside that she had found in the meadow.
Little by little, Lily was thoughtful with Susan. Every time the owl seemed to get angry, Lily, calmly and sincerely, agreed with her and apologized, without seeking conflict.
One day, playing happily with her friends, the acorn they were using as a ball flew directly towards Susan's tree. Everyone froze.
—Forget about that acorn. It's not worth arguing with Susan—said the other squirrels.
But Lily decided to try. Determined, she approached and gently knocked on the door. Susan came out angry, but upon recognizing Lily her face softened a little.
—I'm so sorry, Susan. I came to pick up our acorn and I offer to repair any mess I may have caused—said Lily sweetly.
Just then, a tired and old voice was heard from inside:
—Who is it, dear?
—It's Lily, Mom, the little squirrel who left us that beautiful clover the other day—replied Susan in an unexpectedly soft voice.
Lily understood instantly: Susan wasn't angry with everyone for no reason; she was simply exhausted and overwhelmed by taking care of her elderly mother alone.
—Can I come by tomorrow to keep your mom company for a while, Susan?—offered Lily kindly.
Surprised, Susan accepted the proposal and returned the acorn with a shy smile.

The next day, Lily showed up with a beautiful bouquet of chamomile flowers. She spent a pleasant time chatting with Susan's mom, while the owl took the opportunity to rest and tidy up the nest quietly.

Thanks to Lily's empathy and patience, Susan began to feel calmer and more understood. Soon after, the owl decided to hire a little bird to help her with errands and cheer up her mother with her singing. Since then, a friendlier and happier atmosphere was breathed in the forest. 🌿💖
And sometimes, behind someone's anger, there is only hidden tiredness or worry. With a little patience and empathy, like Lily did, we can improve the lives of others and also our own.

In a rickety little house at the edge of a dark swamp lived Wendy, a very naughty witch, so wobbly-eyed that she couldn't tell her black cat from the magic cauldron. One afternoon, Wendy decided to go out for a drink at "The Sleepy Dragon Cafe," where they served the best nettle tea in town.

While sipping her tea, she absentmindedly left her thick glasses on the table. As she left, Wendy unknowingly picked up someone else's glasses, someone who was drinking a petal infusion right next to her.

Back home, Wendy put on the glasses and began to prepare the terrible "saponifying potion" that would turn all the children at school into toads. But with those strange glasses, the magic book looked different: everything was colorful, bright, and too pretty. "I must go to the optician tomorrow for new glasses," she grumbled, "but first I'll do my prank at school—it will be hilarious!"

She threw ingredients into the cauldron, but something wasn't right. Instead of the usual greenish color, the potion turned a bright blue and gave off a delicious aroma of summer at the beach and radiant rainbows. "How strange," she muttered suspiciously.

The next morning, Wendy poured the potion into a flask, not noticing that it was dripping merrily, leaving a trail of tiny flowers that sprouted with each step. She put it in her black bag full of wickedness and flew to school on her broom.

She landed in the backyard of the school and waited for the cook to go into the storeroom to sneak into the kitchen, opened her bag, and, to her surprise, a flock of multicolored hummingbirds flew out. Somewhat stunned, she quickly poured the contents into the pot that was on the stove and ran to hide behind a nearby bush.

The recess bell rang, and Wendy waited, eager to see the children turned into toads. But what she saw were rays of glitter, happy laughter, and cheerful songs coming out of the windows. Confused, she approached and poked her pointy nose through the glass—the dining room looked like a big party full of laughter and colors!
Suddenly, she felt someone touch her shoulder gently. She turned around startled, and there was the Fairy Godmother, smiling sweetly and offering her her real glasses.
—I think we got mixed up yesterday, dear Wendy,—said the fairy in a kind voice.
With a grunt, Wendy reluctantly exchanged the glasses and flew away on her broom with an evil laugh, eager to repeat her potion again.

The Fairy Godmother smiled as she watched her go, because what Wendy didn't know was that the fairy, very clever, had enchanted her real glasses. Now, no matter how hard she tried, Wendy could only create good magic.

So, from then on, without quite knowing how, Wendy ended up filling the whole town with flowers and smiles every time she tried to do her pranks. And although she pretended to be angry, deep down she was starting to like this new, cheerful, and bright magic. ✨

Benny was a restless, happy, and very fuzzy bee who, from a young age, had rhythm in his wings and legs. Everything he touched became an improvised drum set: cans, stones, leaves… anything was good for creating music.
His parents, seeing this early passion, decided to sign him up for classes with a respected centipede professor. But they always made it clear:
—Benny, music is great as a hobby, but remember that our real job is to pollinate flowers. It is essential for everything to work in nature.
Benny nodded, although secretly he dreamed of dedicating himself to music professionally. However, his parents' advice always weighed more, and he never dared to take the definitive leap.

One particularly boring day of flitting between flowers, Benny decided to escape for a while to a meadow full of bluebells. There, he set up an improvised percussion set with twigs and stones and began to play happily, forgetting everything.
Suddenly, he heard a soft and melodious voice:
—You've got a good beat, kid. Do you do this professionally?
It was a dragonfly with dark glasses and a bohemian air holding a shiny trumpet. Benny blushed.
—I wish, but… you know, pollination is important, and this is just a hobby.
Tony smiled sympathetically:

—Pollination is vital, of course. But music also makes the world more beautiful. By the way, my name is Tony, I play in a band, and we urgently need a drummer. Would you like to try out tonight at the Weeping Willow by the pond?

Benny felt a shiver of excitement. That evening, he went to the willow and found "Bugs in Tune," an incredible band formed by Tony on the trumpet, Gary, a grasshopper on the double bass, Rosie, a ladybug on the piano, and Lacy, a moth on the microphone. The chemistry was instant. Benny, with his drumsticks, gave his best, and the band made all the insects who came attracted by the music vibrate.
At the end, Tony and the rest of the band excitedly proposed:
—Benny, we need a full-time drummer. Do you want to stay with us?
Benny, feeling that he could finally fulfill his dream, happily accepted. Although he was afraid of disappointing his parents, he decided to bet on his happiness.

He spent his afternoons playing with "Bugs in Tune," making the other insects in the garden dance as they came to enjoy a well-deserved rest and disconnect a little from daily tasks. Some time later, his parents came to the Weeping Willow to hear Benny play. Seeing him so happy, they understood that passion is also an essential way to fill the world with beauty.
—We are proud of you, son —they told him, smiling—. Now we know that everyone can make the world bloom in their own way.
And so, Benny, the buzzing bee drummer, continued to bring joy, rhythm, and happiness to every corner of the valley.

Maya was a smart and curious girl, but there was one thing that worried her more than anything: making mistakes in front of others. The thought of failing or not knowing something made her feel so embarrassed that she did her best to go unnoticed. She always tried to sit in the back rows, looked down whenever someone asked a question, and avoided participating in class.

What Maya didn't know was that every time she tried to make herself invisible, she was slowly fading away, accidentally opening a portal to a strange world inhabited by a magical creature that fed on that very same embarrassment.
One day in class, the teacher asked a question:
—Does anyone know what animal can sleep all winter long?

Maya knew the answer, but doubt took hold of her, and she tried to shrink even smaller in her chair. Suddenly, she felt a jolt, and when she opened her eyes, she wasn't in her classroom anymore. She had fallen into the world of embarrassment.

She found herself in the middle of a huge, gray maze that was cold and terrifying. She tried to get out, running down different paths, but she always ended up back where she started. Suddenly, the sound of enormous footsteps echoed behind her, getting closer and closer. Thump… thump… thump… Frightened, Maya started running with no direction, until she heard a whispering voice:
—Over here! Run!
Without a second thought, Maya followed the voice and hid in a small crack in the wall. There, she found a girl named Lily, who explained:
—We’re trapped here because we let our shyness make us invisible. The magical creature is strong because it feeds on our fears.

Lily led Maya through narrow tunnels to a secret place where several other kids lived together. When they arrived, everyone looked down, embarrassed to see someone new. Far away, the creature let out a dark, booming laugh, fueled by their collective shyness.
Lily introduced her friends one by one:
—This is Leo; he built the huts where we sleep. That’s Chloe; she’s the best fisher. And Anna learned how to make fire.
Surprised, Maya exclaimed:
—But you’re all incredible! Don’t you see that?
Though they were shy, they all smiled with pride. As they did, distant screams were heard: the magical creature was losing its power.
—That’s it! —Maya said excitedly—. We each have to say what we’re good at and share it with everyone else.
One by one, they began to name their skills. Little by little, the maze became more and more transparent, until it disappeared completely.
Just before they left, Lily looked at Maya and said:
—You’re good at solving problems, Maya. You’re our hero!
A dizzying feeling returned Maya to her classroom, sitting at her desk. She took a deep breath, raised her hand, and answered the question:
—The bear, because it hibernates.
—Very good, Maya —said the teacher, and calmly continued with the lesson.
Maya understood then that even if she had been wrong, it wouldn’t have been a big deal. Classrooms are for learning, and making mistakes is as natural as breathing.

141.t: Pedaling Through Time: Towards the Caravels
p: Summer returned with its promise of sun, freedom, and secrets to discover. Like every year, the four cousins returned to their grandfather's house, a place where time seemed to stand still among the rows of the orchard and the distant song of crickets as evening fell.

Silvia, the eldest, had changed since last summer. Now she was fourteen, and knowing she was older than the rest, she had developed a strong sense of responsibility for her cousins. After what they experienced in Egypt, she promised herself that they wouldn't get into trouble again. So, she established a firm rule: forbidden to return to the shed.
—Not a bicycle, not a trip to the past, not another scare —she repeated, like a mantra, watching her cousins as if she were their captain.

But Carlos and Luis were still eager for adventures. Every afternoon, when their grandfather took his siesta, the two sneaked into the shed to examine the treasures hidden there. On one occasion, they found the box of past memories that their grandfather hid in a corner: coins from other eras, strange objects, beetles, and other amulets. But what fascinated Carlos the most was a fragment of a map, drawn with faded ink on parchment, showing the skeleton of a wooden ship. It had no title or signature, only perfect strokes and lines with annotations in old Castilian.

—This looks like the plan of a ship —he said to Luis, showing him the drawing—. What kind of vessel would they build, and where would they go? We have to find out! —he added, his eyes shining with excitement.
But Luis didn't dare disobey his cousin and risk a new adventure.

The days passed between swims in the lake, work in the orchard, and walks in the mountains. One night, their grandfather announced that he had to go to town early the next day and would spend the night away. He had important matters to resolve, so he would leave them enough food and the keys to the house. Silvia nodded seriously. Carlos did too, although the plan was already forming in his mind.
The next morning, when Luis woke up, Carlos's bed was empty. Only the piece of the map, carefully folded, was on the pillow.
—He's gone! —Luis shouted as he entered the kitchen—. Carlos has taken a bike!
Silvia paled. Carolina, still in her pajamas, rubbed her eyes.
—Is he in the forest?
—No. He's gone back in time —said Luis, showing the parchment.

Silvia hesitated. Her instinct screamed at her to stay. What if they didn't appear at the same time as him? Or even if they found him, would they be able to return? But the fear that Carlos was trapped in some dangerous past pushed her to act.
—We're going to look for him. Now!

They ran to the shed. Sure enough, one bicycle was missing. Without wasting any more time, the three mounted theirs, descended the slope of the forest, and, once again, the whirlwind of leaves, wind, and light enveloped them.

They appeared among cobbled alleys, with houses with white facades and wrought-iron balconies. The air smelled of salt, fish, manure, and damp wood. In the background, they heard hammering, energetic voices, and the rhythmic tapping of tools against wood.
—Where are we? —asked Carolina, still dizzy from the journey.
Luis shrugged.
—We're in some coastal town —he whispered—. But clearly not from our time...
Next to them was an alley full of junk, and they checked, relieved, that Carlos's bicycle was under a large tarp. They hid the others and prepared to look for him. But where to start?
Then they saw a boy of their age coming up the street quite quickly, with patched pants, a loose shirt, and his hair ruffled by the wind. He looked them up and down and approached.
—Are you looking for something? —he asked without hostility.
—We're looking for our cousin. His name is Carlos, and he's not from around here —explained Silvia.
The boy nodded.

—I was with him. He was arrested by the port soldiers. They said he was spying in the shipyards, because of the look of his clothes. The town is very stirred up lately. There are spies, rumors, tensions with the nobles, and any stranger raises suspicions. With all the money being invested in this voyage, suspicion is the order of the day. I was going to get help.
—A voyage? Who are you? —asked Carolina.
—Alonso. My father works building ships for the House of Trade. I sometimes carry tools or run errands. Come with me!
They ran after him through narrow streets until they reached the shipyards, where a huge caravel under construction rose above the waters. The cousins stopped, speechless.
—That's like Columbus's ship! —whispered Luis.

—It's not like Columbus's ship —corrected Alonso proudly—. It is Columbus's ship. The Santa María. Although it was actually called La Gallega before, and it was a merchant ship ceded by Don Juan de la Cosa.
—Who? —asked Carolina.
—The cartographer of the voyage. They say he's the one who drew the maps that will take them to the Indies. He's a friend of Admiral Columbus.
Silvia's eyes widened.
—What year is it?
—Don't you know? It's 1492 —said Alonso—. They'll soon be setting sail for the Indies! They're looking for a new route!
—And where are we?
—In Palos de la Frontera, kid! Have you bumped your head or something?
Luis swallowed, he knew that they would never reach the Indies by that route, but they would make a much more important discovery. However, he understood that he couldn't say anything.
Alonso led them through a passageway that bordered the shipyards, to a small stone office guarded by a soldier.
—Carlos is in there. I heard that they want to take him before some high official. Luckily, Don Juan de la Cosa hasn't arrived yet.
—We need to get him out before someone important arrives —said Silvia with determination.
They hid until the guard was distracted by a group of sailors arguing about the cargo. Alonso pointed to an open window.
—Go in through there. I'll distract the soldier.
Silvia and Luis climbed up and helped Carolina through. Inside, Carlos was sitting on a bench, tied with a rope.
—I knew you'd come! —he exclaimed, smiling despite the situation.
—You're reckless —Silvia blurted out, while untying him.
—But you came! —he joked.
The back door opened suddenly, it was Alonso signaling them to hurry. But they weren't counting on a second guard, who discovered them.
—Stop right there!
They ran through the alleys until they got lost in a group of children playing with wooden tops.

Alonso led them to his house, a modest workshop full of rolled-up fabrics, long needles, and large baskets with hemp. His mother, a kind-eyed woman, hid them in the basement. After a while, when the danger had passed, she invited them out.
—It's not the first time my son has gotten into trouble for helping strangers —she said, winking at Silvia.
—Do you work here? —asked Carolina.
—Yes, dear. I sew the sails for the caravels. Every stitch has to be well made, or the wind won't forgive.

At dusk, Alonso's father arrived, his hands stained with tar and his face tired from work. When he saw the children, he frowned, but then let out a sigh, washed his hands in a trough full of water, and sat down next to them to eat dinner.

—Don't you really know what's happening? —he asked in a grave voice while chewing a piece of bread—. The Catholic Monarchs have financed a voyage that could change the world. Columbus has been negotiating his project for years, and many don't believe in him. Some say he's crazy, others that he's a genius. But he has convinced Queen Isabella, and that has changed everything. The riches of Asia, the spices, the gold... all that could arrive by a new route. If he succeeds, it will change history. But if he fails...
He was silent for a moment, looking through the window.
—Here we all work with hope, but also with fear. Not everyone agrees. Some fear that it's money thrown into the sea.
That night, Alonso showed them navigation charts, naval carpentry tools, and pieces of wood used in the caravels.
—Oak from the north, Galician pine, tar to seal the joints. Everything that floats and withstands storms —he explained enthusiastically.
In a toolbox, Carlos saw something that made him hold his breath: a piece almost identical to the map he had found in his grandfather's shed.
—This... this completes the fragment that my grandfather had —he whispered.
Alonso shrugged.
—I found it in the port months ago. If it's useful to you, it's yours.
Carlos accepted it solemnly. It was more than a piece of paper; it was a link between times, a testimony of the voyage.

At dawn, as they prepared to return, from the window of the workshop they saw a man arrive with a round face, a haughty bearing, and a marked accent from another place, with a group of officers escorting him. Alonso pointed them out in a low voice.
—That's Admiral Columbus.
The cousins watched him in silence, feeling history pass before their eyes.
However, there was no time to lose, they had to return to their time before their grandfather returned home and missed them. They said goodbye to Alonso with sincere hugs.
—Will we see each other again? —he asked.
—Who knows... —said Silvia, with an enigmatic smile.
They looked for a cobbled slope and mounted their bicycles. The wind turned again, the houses blurred, and, in a sigh, they were back in the forest.
They entered the house just as their grandfather returned. Nothing seemed to have changed, but their hearts beat with the strength of what they had experienced.
That night their grandfather went to the shed. He rummaged among the objects and found the new map, complete for the first time. A smile appeared on his weathered face.
He sighed, closed the box, and hung the key in its place.
And although he didn't say a word, his eyes shone with the certainty that the adventure had only just begun. 🌍🚲✨

Mara held the tablet steady, reviewing the detailed medical report she had just received. Her eyes quickly scanned the lines of text, carefully absorbing the latest data on the adaptations observed in the colonists.

The scientific meeting room, circular with high ceilings, was decorated with translucent fabrics woven with Veridian fibers that softened the light, creating a relaxed atmosphere. In the background, the tuning music for the festival began to play softly, anticipating the start of the event they had been preparing for weeks. Several researchers exchanged excited glances; they knew that the work of an entire cycle was about to be shared with the rest of the colony.

"It has been exactly one full orbit around the sun of Veridia-7, which is equivalent to a year and a half on Earth," Mara began, looking up to address the other scientists gathered in the room. "The physiological improvements of the colonists are evident. The golden iris is no longer an exception; changes in coloration can be seen in all individuals and is the norm in all babies born here. This accompanies notable visual and neurological changes. The yellowish eyes have significantly increased our visual perception, especially in low light conditions, allowing us to capture nuances that were previously invisible, and considerably increasing our ability to react quickly to visual stimuli from the environment."
"Dorian," she added, turning to him, "would you like to comment on what you observed in the nursery area?"
The chief scientist, with his robust and serene presence, leaned forward slightly. His eyes, speckled with gold, seemed to reflect the planet's glow.

"Yes, of course. In the most recent births, we have begun to register reflex responses to natural light stimuli from the environment. That is, the babies seem capable of reacting almost instinctively to certain lights from the bioluminescent creatures of the forest or to movements of the foliage, as if their senses have already developed a primitive form of dialogue with Veridia."
A murmur of astonishment went through the room.
He paused briefly, observing the attentive reactions of his colleagues, before continuing seriously.

"The skin of the colonists presents a slight glow under certain light conditions, indicating deep and stable cellular changes. Those individuals who experienced wounds from direct exposure to Veridite have developed intricate and organic patterns in the affected areas. These gray tattoos seem to respond emotionally to the environment and are more pronounced in subjects like Aura and Isaac, who were the first to have direct contact."
Dorian nodded.

"The touch sensors we installed to measure bioelectric conductivity have detected variations associated with the individual's emotional state and the presence of nearby living beings. The skin literally 'feels' Veridia. Some colonists have begun to use it intuitively to avoid risk areas or detect mood changes in nearby creatures."
Mara paused to catch her breath and continue with her presentation.

"On a physical level, our bodies have adapted remarkably to the planet's lower gravity. Our muscles have become more streamlined and toned considerably; our bones, although they have reduced their density to compensate for the reduced gravity, have undergone alterations that make them more resistant to fractures or injuries. In addition, we have grown significantly; between the low gravity and the adaptation of the veridite, adults have reached about 6 centimeters more in this period, with this difference being significantly greater in children and adolescents still in the growth period when we arrived, reaching in some cases a growth of up to 16 centimeters more than an earthling individual."

A series of murmurs ran through the team. All these changes were so gradual that they went unnoticed in the day-to-day life of the colony. They already found it difficult to remember the people they were when they left Earth.

"On the other hand," Mara continued, "our cardiovascular resistance has increased dramatically, improving the oxygenation of the body in this particular atmosphere. Our movements have become more graceful and fluid, adapting perfectly to the specific conditions of Veridia-7."

"And breathing has also changed," Dorian interrupted softly. "It has become more paused, less urgent. We have measured a decrease in the basal heart rate, but an increase in variability. That could be linked not only to physiological adaptation, but to emotional adaptation. We live with more synchronicity, not only with the environment, but among ourselves."
Mara looked at him with gratitude and continued:

"But perhaps the most fascinating and still difficult to quantify is the emotional and sensory connection we have developed with the planet. As we have already mentioned, numerous individuals report being able to perceive shared sensations with other local species, reacting emotionally to situations of stress or danger that affect the ecosystem. This deep sensory integration could be the key to our long-term survival, even if it irremediably differentiates us from our original species."
"Perhaps we are becoming something new," Dorian added in a low voice. "Something that does not yet have a name, but that is, without a doubt, a form of humanity deeply rooted."

Mara closed the report with a smooth movement of her hand. She felt the excitement of her colleagues. Although their evolution as a species was important, that day they were preparing the Communion Festival. A day that they had organized to commemorate their return to the Sun of Veridia, where competitions, contests, games, as well as a great dinner and a final dance would take place. It would serve to present all their advances, to the children born in Veridia-7 and to celebrate their connection with the planet that housed them.
"Go with your families," Mara added with a smile. "Today we not only celebrate what we are. We also celebrate what we could become."

In their new house, built with a shiny alloy of tantalum and veridite, Aura was finishing a dessert in the company of Isaac. The walls, a resplendent white, softly reflected the natural light of the sunset.
"Do you think they'll like it?" Aura asked, delicately scattering emerald berries over the dessert.
Isaac, who had finished preparing a tray of aromatic vegetables, approached affectionately from behind, observing her work.
"I'm sure they'll love it," he murmured, wrapping his arms around her and giving her a soft kiss on the neck.
Aura smiled, aware of the pleasant warmth she felt in her chest. Since they had moved in together, they seemed to have found some stability and calm, enjoying these everyday moments together.

"The colony is beautiful, don't you think?" In reality, the colony had been impressive. Derek, along with other colonists, had supervised every detail of the decoration, integrating local luminescent plants that emitted a soft light, creating a cozy and magical atmosphere. Liam's parents had deployed systems that emitted enveloping music, perfectly adapted to the planet's acoustics.

They had been doing various activities and games all day. In the Galebre races, Alexia stood out as an amazon, beating all her companions, and Zoe presented the Drumek, the new domesticated creature, large and muscular with six legs, similar to a terrestrial rhinoceros but more slender and adapted to transport heavy loads.

"The one who is beautiful is you," Isaac replied, giving her a kiss on the tip of her nose. Aura wore a deep blue dress, carefully woven with soft and slightly silky fibers extracted from local plants. The fabric adapted gracefully to her movements, discreetly reflecting the ambient light, generating small almost hypnotic flashes. To the touch, the fabric was fresh and flexible, light as a second skin. The skirt flowed delicately, although it could be easily removed to reveal comfortable shorts that allowed her to move with absolute freedom and security, ready for any eventuality that the planet had in store for her. "Hurry up or we'll be late for the rest of the games and celebrations," he added, giving her a pat on the butt, which unleashed a playful giggle in Aura.
